# anfra interaction patterns

> 54 analytical interaction patterns for anfra Data Apps: filters, selections, dates and time, drilling, tables and calculations, scenarios and saved state. Each pattern has a Markdown page with its AQL, its @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0 wiring, a complete working example and what a good result looks like, all on the `ecommerce` sample Dataset.

Read [AGENTS.md](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/AGENTS.md) first: how to use these patterns in a Data App, and the rules that keep the SDK wiring working.

When told to follow an example by name, fetch its page: "date filter" is [date-filter.md](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/date-filter.md), "date drill" is [date-drill.md](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/date-drill.md), "cross-filtering" is [single-select.md](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/single-select.md), "underlying data" is [underlying-records.md](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/underlying-records.md), "drill down" is [hierarchy-drill.md](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/hierarchy-drill.md), "what-if parameter" is [what-if.md](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/what-if.md).

## Dates & time

Choose the period, its detail, and what to compare it with.

- [Date filter](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/date-filter.md): Pick exact dates, a range like "last 3 months", or a phrase like "last quarter".
- [Date drill](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/date-drill.md): Switch the time detail between day, week, month and quarter, or click a period to see it in more detail.
- [Fiscal calendar](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/fiscal-calendar.md): Report by a fiscal year that starts in July instead of January.
- [As-of anchor](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/as-of-anchor.md): Count "last 30 days" back from the newest data instead of from today.
- [Incomplete periods](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/partial-period.md): Mark a month that isn't over yet, so its short bar doesn't look like a drop.
- [Period comparison](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/period-compare.md): Show each month next to the month before and the same month last year.
- [Custom period comparison](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/custom-compare.md): Compare any two date ranges side by side, like H1 2026 and H2 2025.
- [Period to date & trailing period](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/to-date.md): Show a year-to-date total and a rolling 3-month total for each month.

## Selections

Click or drag on a chart to filter the others.

- [Cross-filtering](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/single-select.md): Click one or more bars, a country on the map or heatmap cells, and other charts show only those.
- [Range brushing](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/range-brush.md): Drag across months on a chart, and other charts show only that period.
- [Histogram brushing](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/numeric-brush.md): Drag across a range of order sizes, like $1,000 to $2,000.
- [Cross-highlighting](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/cross-highlight.md): Hover a country, and other charts keep their totals but highlight its share.
- [Multiple cross-filters](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/two-selections.md): Keep a selection in two charts at once, like Germany in one and Software in the other.
- [Selection cohort](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/selection-cohort.md): Select some customers and compare what they buy with everyone else.

## Filters

Decide which rows count.

- [Field filter](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/field-filter.md): Pick values from a list, like Vietnam and Singapore, and every chart shows only those.
- [Widget filter](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/scope-vs-filter.md): A rule built into one chart, like "completed orders only", that viewers can't remove.
- [Filter group](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/compound-filter.md): Combine conditions with AND and OR, like (Vietnam and Software) or cancelled.
- [Metric filter](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/aggregate-filter.md): Filter on a total, like customers who spent more than $12k.
- [Range filter](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/range-filter.md): Drag a slider to keep orders between two values, or above or below one.
- [Text filter](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/text-search.md): Type part of a name to find matching rows, ignoring upper and lower case.

## Tables & calculations

Choose what a chart shows and how its numbers are calculated.

- [Dynamic metric](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/metric-switch.md): Switch the chart between revenue, orders and units with one click.
- [Dynamic dimension](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/dimension-switch.md): Switch how the chart groups data: by country, category or status.
- [Sort](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/sort.md): Click a column header to sort the table by that column.
- [Top N & Others](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/top-n.md): Show the top 3 countries and group the rest into "Others".
- [Pivot table](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/pivot.md): Countries down the side, categories across the top, and each cell's share of its row.
- [Subtotals & grand totals](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/totals.md): Add a total for each category and one for everything.
- [Percent of total](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/percent-of-total.md): Show each country's share of all revenue, like Australia at 24%.
- [Running total & moving calculation](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/cumulative-moving.md): Add a running total and a 3-month average to a monthly chart.
- [Indexed view](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/index-100.md): Start every line at 100, so growth compares fairly between big and small series.
- [Rank](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/ranking.md): Number each customer by revenue, overall and within their country.

## Drilling

Go from a number to the detail behind it.

- [Drill down](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/hierarchy-drill.md): Click a region to see its countries, then customers, then their orders, and climb back with breadcrumbs.
- [Drill path](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/drill-path.md): Keep a trail of every step down and up, and click any step to go back to it.
- [Break down](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/adhoc-breakdown.md): Right-click a bar to split it by another field, like order status.
- [View underlying data](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/underlying-records.md): Click a column on a chart to see the individual orders behind it.
- [Drill-through](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/drillthrough.md): Click a country to open another app already filtered to that country. (proposed)
- [Row actions](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/row-actions.md): Put links on each table row: open the customer in your CRM, email them, or see their orders.

## Scenarios & analyses

Try assumptions and run ready-made analyses.

- [Binning](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/bins.md): Group orders into size bands, like under $100 or over $1,000.
- [Reference line](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/targets.md): Draw a target line and show how far each month is above or below it.
- [Trend line](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/trend-line.md): Draw the line of best fit through a chart, to show which way it is heading.
- [What-if parameter](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/what-if.md): Try a price change, like +10% on Software, and watch revenue change.
- [Rule-based cohort](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/cohort-from-rank.md): Define a group by a rule, like the top 10% of customers by revenue.

## Controls

Decide what each control and click changes, and when.

- [Filter mapping](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/one-control-many.md): Choose which charts a filter changes, so a benchmark chart can stay unfiltered.
- [Parent-child filter](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/cascading-options.md): Picking a category limits the product list to products in that category.
- [Apply button](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/apply-button.md): Change several filters, then press Apply to update every chart at once.
- [Cross filter](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/selection-to-filter.md): Turn a clicked selection into a filter chip, so your next click narrows further.
- [Zoom / pan](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/zoom-pan.md): Scrolling zooms the picture, and double-clicking reloads that month week by week.
- [Legend visibility](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/legend-toggle.md): Click a legend item to hide its line, or Alt-click to show only that line.
- [Custom right-click menu](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/custom-menu.md): Right-click a data point to open a menu of actions, and choose which actions it offers.

## Save & share

Keep, share, undo and export what you're looking at.

- [Bookmarks](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/bookmarks.md): Save the current view and come back to it with one click.
- [Filter state URL](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/url-state.md): Copy a link that opens the app with the same filters. (proposed)
- [Reset filters](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/reset.md): Clear one filter, or all of them, back to the defaults.
- [Undo / redo](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/undo-redo.md): Step back and forward through your filter and drill changes.
- [Saved views](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/saved-views.md): Keep named views that are still there next week, on any device. (proposed)
- [Refresh & cache](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/references/refresh.md): Rerun the queries and see how fresh the data is.

## Optional

- [All patterns in one file](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/llms-full.txt): every pattern page, concatenated.
- [The gallery](https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html): the human page, with trailers and live demos. It is one large HTML file; agents should read the Markdown instead.

# Field filter

> Pick values from a list, like Vietnam and Singapore, and every chart shows only those.

- Pattern id: `field-filter`
- Category: Filters (also Controls)
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#field-filter
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader picks **Vietnam** and **Singapore**, then **Completed**. The monthly revenue trend redraws, and the bars slide down from $1.28M to $281k.

Why: Most dashboards need a filter first. Here the filter field is checked when the app starts, and its options come from the data.

## What to build

Picking values in a filter narrows every chart it feeds to the matching rows, with the full total faint behind.

Layout: Monthly revenue columns under a row of filter chips; the unfiltered total stays as a grey ghost so the drop is visible.

Instruction: Add pickers above the main chart whose options come from the data, so readers can narrow the page to the values they pick.

Done when: Each pick redraws the chart to match, the full total stays visible behind it, and clearing the picks restores it.

On the ecommerce sample: Pick Vietnam and Singapore, then Completed: the monthly bars drop from $1.28M to $281k, with all orders still grey behind them.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count }
  sorts { period asc }
}
```

Reader input the SDK sent:

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "field": "customers.country",
      "operator": "is",
      "values": [
        "Vietnam",
        "Singapore"
      ]
    },
    {
      "field": "orders.status",
      "operator": "is",
      "values": [
        "completed"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Saved result:

| period | total_revenue | num_orders |
|---|---|---|
| 2025-06-01 | 10740.24 | 19 |
| 2025-07-01 | 13348.31 | 16 |
| 2025-08-01 | 13828.80 | 14 |
| 2025-09-01 | 16837.78 | 22 |
| 2025-10-01 | 16101.22 | 25 |
| 2025-11-01 | 11726.84 | 13 |
| 2025-12-01 | 9598.43 | 13 |
| 2026-01-01 | 21756.92 | 29 |
| 2026-02-01 | 26735.00 | 18 |
| 2026-03-01 | 6056.81 | 16 |
| 2026-04-01 | 16120.41 | 19 |
| 2026-05-01 | 29807.51 | 28 |

(4 more rows)

## SDK wiring

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const trend = app.createQuery('trend', {
  dataset: 'ecommerce',
  aql: TREND_AQL,
});

const country = app.createFilter('country', {
  dataset: 'ecommerce',
  field: 'customers.country',
});
const status = app.createFilter('status', {
  dataset: 'ecommerce',
  field: 'orders.status',
});
// options come from the data
await country.loadOptions();

app.mapControl(country, trend, { field: 'customers.country' });
app.mapControl(status, trend, { field: 'orders.status' });

country.setCondition({
  operator: 'is',
  values: ['Vietnam', 'Singapore'],
});
// re-runs only what changed
await app.execute();
```

State it touches: Analytical: two filter conditions. Renderer: the grey ghost bars.

## Notes

- One filter and one mapping per query. The SDK sends `filters[]`, and the AQL text never changes
- A typo in `field` fails at once, with a "did you mean" suggestion
- `loadOptions()` fetches values that this reader is allowed to see

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Country</span><span class="chips" id="countries"></span></div>
		<div class="row"><label class="lbl" for="status">Status</label><select id="status"><option value="">Any status</option></select><span class="hint">Both filters reach the KPI and the trend</span></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Monthly revenue: <span id="kpi">–</span></b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="trend"></div>
		<div class="legend"><span><i style="background:var(--violet)"></i>Filtered</span><span><i style="background:rgb(24 20 31 / 0.07)"></i>All orders</span></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Field filter', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const AQL = 'explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { period asc } }';
const trend = app.createQuery('trend', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: AQL });
const all = app.createQuery('allOrders', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: AQL });
const country = app.createFilter('country', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.country', label: 'Country' });
const status = app.createFilter('status', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'orders.status', label: 'Status' });
app.mapControl(country, trend, { field: 'customers.country' });
app.mapControl(status, trend, { field: 'orders.status' });
const picked = new Set();
const chips = K.$('#countries'), sel = K.$('#status');
const apply = () => { if (picked.size) country.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [...picked] }); else country.reset(); if (sel.value) status.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [sel.value] }); else status.reset(); app.execute(); };
country.loadOptions().then((vals) => vals.forEach((v) => { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = v; b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', 'false'); b.onclick = () => { picked.has(v) ? picked.delete(v) : picked.add(v); b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(picked.has(v))); apply(); }; chips.appendChild(b); }));
status.loadOptions().then((vals) => vals.forEach((v) => sel.add(new Option(v[0].toUpperCase() + v.slice(1), v))));
sel.onchange = apply;
const mon = (v) => new Date(v).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', year: '2-digit', timeZone: 'UTC' });
app.subscribe(() => {
K.status(trend, K.$('#s1'));
if (!trend.result) return;
const ghost = new Map((all.result?.rows || []).map((r) => [r.period, r.total_revenue]));
K.$('#kpi').textContent = K.compact.format(trend.result.rows.reduce((t, r) => t + Number(r.total_revenue), 0));
const rows = all.result ? all.result.rows.map((r) => trend.result.rows.find((x) => x.period === r.period) || { period: r.period, total_revenue: 0 }) : trend.result.rows;
K.columns(K.$('#trend'), rows, { label: (r) => mon(r.period), value: (r) => r.total_revenue, ghost: (r) => ghost.get(r.period) });
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [trend]);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read the KPI: **Monthly revenue** starts at $1.28M for all orders
2. Click **Vietnam** and **Singapore** in the **Country** row
3. Pick **Completed** in the **Status** list
4. Read the trend: the violet bars drop to $281k, with all orders in grey behind them

## Other Filters patterns

- [Widget filter](scope-vs-filter.md): A rule built into one chart, like "completed orders only", that viewers can't remove.
- [Filter group](compound-filter.md): Combine conditions with AND and OR, like (Vietnam and Software) or cancelled.
- [Metric filter](aggregate-filter.md): Filter on a total, like customers who spent more than $12k.
- [Range filter](range-filter.md): Drag a slider to keep orders between two values, or above or below one.
- [Text filter](text-search.md): Type part of a name to find matching rows, ignoring upper and lower case.

---

# Widget filter

> A rule built into one chart, like "completed orders only", that viewers can't remove.

- Pattern id: `scope-vs-filter`
- Category: Filters
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#scope-vs-filter
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

A "Completed orders only" badge is part of the query and can't be removed. The reader still picks **Germany**, and the chart shows Germany's completed revenue.

Why: Readers need to know which rules are fixed, such as "we never count cancelled orders", and which ones they control.

## What to build

A fixed rule is built into the chart's query and shown as a locked badge; the reader's filters apply on top.

Layout: A locked scope badge next to normal filter chips, above a monthly trend.

Instruction: Keep a fixed rule on a chart, shown as a locked badge, separate from the reader's filters so Reset never removes it.

Done when: The locked badge has no control, filters narrow the chart within its rule, and Reset clears the filters but keeps the badge.

On the ecommerce sample: Pick Germany: the chart reads Completed revenue · Germany at $127k. Reset filters clears Germany, and the Completed orders only lock stays.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue }
  filters { orders.status == 'completed' }
  sorts { period asc }
}
```

Reader input the SDK sent:

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "field": "customers.country",
      "operator": "is",
      "values": [
        "Germany"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Saved result:

| period | total_revenue |
|---|---|
| 2025-06-01 | 9940.44 |
| 2025-07-01 | 8072.26 |
| 2025-08-01 | 3829.95 |
| 2025-09-01 | 13544.18 |
| 2025-10-01 | 8709.35 |
| 2025-11-01 | 5313.83 |
| 2025-12-01 | 9769.84 |
| 2026-01-01 | 9811.05 |
| 2026-02-01 | 8871.96 |
| 2026-03-01 | 11064.88 |
| 2026-04-01 | 8042.44 |
| 2026-05-01 | 3452.73 |

(4 more rows)

Trailer frames 1 and 3 approximate the completed-only total at 70% of all revenue. Frame 2 is the real run result.

## SDK wiring

```js
// scope: in the AQL, so no reader can remove it
const trend = app.createQuery('trend', {
  dataset: 'ecommerce',
  aql: `
    explore {
      … filters { orders.status == 'completed' }
    }
  `,
});

// reader filter: a control on top of the scope
app.mapControl(country, trend, { field: 'customers.country' });
resetBtn.onclick = () => {
  country.reset();
  app.execute();
};
```

State it touches: Analytical: the fixed scope lives in the declaration, and the reader filter is a control condition.

## Notes

- The fixed scope sits in `filters { }` and the reader filter goes through `mapControl`. `executedAql` shows both
- `reset()` can never remove the scope

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><span class="lock" title="Part of the query: no reader control can remove it">🔒 Completed orders only</span><label class="lbl" for="country">Country</label><select id="country"><option value="">All countries</option></select><button type="button" id="reset">Reset filters</button></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Completed revenue<span id="for"></span>: <span id="kpi">–</span></b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="trend"></div>
		<div class="hint">Reset clears the country. The lock is in the AQL filters block, so it stays</div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
		<style>.lock { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; height: 28px; padding: 0 10px; border-radius: 999px; font-size: 12px; background: var(--sunken); border: 1px dashed var(--rule-strong); color: var(--weak); cursor: not-allowed; }</style>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Widget filter', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const trend = app.createQuery('trend', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() } measures { total_revenue: revenue } filters { orders.status == \'completed\' } sorts { period asc } }' });
const country = app.createFilter('country', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.country', label: 'Country' });
app.mapControl(country, trend, { field: 'customers.country' });
const sel = K.$('#country');
country.loadOptions().then((vals) => vals.forEach((v) => sel.add(new Option(v, v))));
sel.onchange = () => { if (sel.value) country.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [sel.value] }); else country.reset(); app.execute(); };
K.$('#reset').onclick = () => { country.reset(); sel.value = ''; app.execute(); };
const mon = (v) => new Date(v).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', year: '2-digit', timeZone: 'UTC' });
app.subscribe(() => {
K.status(trend, K.$('#s1'));
const c = country.appliedCondition;
K.$('#for').textContent = c && c.values && c.values.length ? ' · ' + c.values.join(', ') : ' · all countries';
if (trend.result) {
	K.$('#kpi').textContent = K.compact.format(trend.result.rows.reduce((t, r) => t + Number(r.total_revenue), 0));
	K.columns(K.$('#trend'), trend.result.rows, { label: (r) => mon(r.period), value: (r) => r.total_revenue });
}
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [trend], () => ['scope (in the AQL, not reader input) → orders.status == \'completed\'']);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read the badge: **🔒 Completed orders only** is part of the query and has no control
2. Pick **Germany** in the **Country** list
3. Read the chart: **Completed revenue · Germany** shows $127k
4. Click **Reset filters**: Germany clears, and the lock stays

## Other Filters patterns

- [Field filter](field-filter.md): Pick values from a list, like Vietnam and Singapore, and every chart shows only those.
- [Filter group](compound-filter.md): Combine conditions with AND and OR, like (Vietnam and Software) or cancelled.
- [Metric filter](aggregate-filter.md): Filter on a total, like customers who spent more than $12k.
- [Range filter](range-filter.md): Drag a slider to keep orders between two values, or above or below one.
- [Text filter](text-search.md): Type part of a name to find matching rows, ignoring upper and lower case.

# Filter group

> Combine conditions with AND and OR, like (Vietnam and Software) or cancelled.

- Pattern id: `compound-filter`
- Category: Filters
- Status: Works with app code: anfra supplies the queries, the app adds some logic
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#compound-filter
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader builds two groups: **Vietnam and Software**, or **Status is cancelled**. The table keeps only the rows that match either group.

Why: Readers ask "this, or that" questions all the time. Plain filter bars can only combine conditions with AND.

## What to build

Readers fill groups of conditions; all conditions in a group must hold, any one group can match, and the query rebuilds.

Layout: A small condition builder (two groups joined by OR) above a breakdown table.

Instruction: Let readers combine groups of conditions with AND and OR, and show the combined condition in plain words.

Done when: The condition reads back in plain words, the table keeps only rows that match some group, and emptying a group drops it.

On the ecommerce sample: With Vietnam and Software in Group 1 and Cancelled in Group 2, the title reads (Country is Vietnam and Category is Software) or Status is cancelled.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { country: customers.country, category: products.category, status: orders.status }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue }
  filters { (customers.country == 'Vietnam' and products.category == 'Software') or orders.status == 'cancelled' }
  sorts { total_revenue desc }
}
```

Saved result:

| country | category | status | total_revenue |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vietnam | Software | completed | 37777.00 |
| Australia | Services | cancelled | 31000.00 |
| Singapore | Software | cancelled | 28524.00 |
| Australia | Software | cancelled | 23594.00 |
| Germany | Services | cancelled | 21500.00 |
| Vietnam | Services | cancelled | 18000.00 |
| Singapore | Services | cancelled | 18000.00 |
| United States | Services | cancelled | 17500.00 |
| Vietnam | Software | cancelled | 17321.00 |
| United States | Software | cancelled | 15243.00 |
| Vietnam | Software | shipped | 13136.00 |
| Germany | Software | cancelled | 8953.00 |

(14 more rows)

The query runs as written. A reader-built group, though, can't be sent as SDK input: controls are ANDed, and only selections become OR expressions.

## SDK wiring

```js
// Today: each new set of groups is a new query (AQL is fixed once
// declared)
let n = 0;
// where: built ONLY from picked option values
function applyGroups(where) {
  current?.abort();
  current = app.createQuery('grp' + ++n, {
    dataset: 'ecommerce',
    aql: buildAql(where),
  });
  app.execute();
}
// Proposed: app.createConditionGroup('g', { any: [[countryIs,
// categoryIs], [statusIs]] })
```

## Notes

- The AQL `filters { }` block accepts `and` / `or` and brackets
- `executedAql` shows the exact condition that ran
- Limits: Works with app code: build and validate the expression from picked values only, and declare a new query for each change. A condition-group control is proposed.

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<div class="grp" id="g1"><span class="lbl gl">Group 1</span></div>
		<div class="row"><span class="or">OR</span><span class="hint">A row is kept when it matches every pick in either group</span></div>
		<div class="grp" id="g2"><span class="lbl gl">Group 2</span></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b id="words">–</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="table"></div></div>
		<div class="hint">App code: each change declares a new query, its filters built from picked values only</div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
		<style>.grp { display: flex; gap: 6px; align-items: center; } .grp select { width: 128px; } .gl { width: 48px; } .tw { max-height: 160px; } .or { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--violet-ink); background: var(--violet-soft); border-radius: 999px; padding: 2px 10px; }</style>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Filter group', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const FIELDS = [{ key: 'country', field: 'customers.country', label: 'Country', any: 'Any country' }, { key: 'category', field: 'products.category', label: 'Category', any: 'Any category' }, { key: 'status', field: 'orders.status', label: 'Status', any: 'Any status' }];
const OPTS = {};
const groups = [{ country: 'Vietnam', category: 'Software', status: '' }, { country: '', category: '', status: '' }];
const BASE = ['explore { dimensions { country_name: customers.country, category_name: products.category, status_name: orders.status } measures { total_revenue: revenue }', ' sorts { total_revenue desc } }'];
const cache = new Map();
let n = 0, cur = null, where = '';
const ok = (k, v) => v && OPTS[k] && OPTS[k].includes(v) && !/['\\]/.test(v);
function build () {
	const parts = groups.map((g) => FIELDS.filter((f) => ok(f.key, g[f.key])).map((f) => f.field + " == '" + g[f.key] + "'")).filter((p) => p.length);
	where = parts.map((p) => parts.length > 1 && p.length > 1 ? '(' + p.join(' and ') + ')' : p.join(' and ')).join(' or ');
	const words = groups.map((g) => FIELDS.filter((f) => ok(f.key, g[f.key])).map((f) => f.label + ' is ' + g[f.key])).filter((p) => p.length).map((p) => p.length > 1 ? '(' + p.join(' and ') + ')' : p[0]);
	K.$('#words').textContent = words.length ? words.join(' or ') : 'All rows: pick values to build a condition';
	const aql = BASE[0] + (where ? ' filters { ' + where + ' }' : '') + BASE[1];
	if (!cache.has(aql)) cache.set(aql, app.createQuery('grp' + (++n), { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql }));
	cur = cache.get(aql);
	app.execute();
}
const probes = FIELDS.map((f) => app.createFilter('opt_' + f.key, { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: f.field, label: f.label }));
Promise.all(probes.map((p) => p.loadOptions())).then((lists) => {
	FIELDS.forEach((f, i) => { OPTS[f.key] = lists[i].map(String); });
	groups.forEach((g, gi) => {
		const box = K.$('#g' + (gi + 1));
		FIELDS.forEach((f, fi) => {
			if (fi) { const a = document.createElement('span'); a.className = 'lbl'; a.textContent = 'and'; box.appendChild(a); }
			const s = document.createElement('select'); s.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Group ' + (gi + 1) + ' ' + f.label);
			s.add(new Option(f.any, ''));
			OPTS[f.key].forEach((v) => s.add(new Option(f.key === 'status' ? v[0].toUpperCase() + v.slice(1) : v, v)));
			s.value = g[f.key];
			s.onchange = () => { g[f.key] = s.value; build(); };
			box.appendChild(s);
		});
	});
	build();
});
const cap = (v) => v ? v[0].toUpperCase() + v.slice(1) : v;
app.subscribe(() => {
if (!cur) return;
K.status(cur, K.$('#s1'));
if (cur.result) K.table(K.$('#table'), [{ key: 'country_name', label: 'Country' }, { key: 'category_name', label: 'Category' }, { key: 'status_name', label: 'Status', fmt: cap }, { key: 'total_revenue', label: 'Revenue', num: true, fmt: (v) => K.money.format(Number(v)) }], cur.result.rows);
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [cur], () => ['condition (in the AQL, rebuilt by app code) → ' + (where || 'none')]);
});
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read **Group 1**: it already holds **Vietnam** and **Software**
2. Pick **Cancelled** in the **Any status** list of **Group 2**
3. Read the title: (Country is Vietnam and Category is Software) or Status is cancelled
4. Read the table: it keeps only the rows that match either group

## Other Filters patterns

- [Field filter](field-filter.md): Pick values from a list, like Vietnam and Singapore, and every chart shows only those.
- [Widget filter](scope-vs-filter.md): A rule built into one chart, like "completed orders only", that viewers can't remove.
- [Metric filter](aggregate-filter.md): Filter on a total, like customers who spent more than $12k.
- [Range filter](range-filter.md): Drag a slider to keep orders between two values, or above or below one.
- [Text filter](text-search.md): Type part of a name to find matching rows, ignoring upper and lower case.

---

# Metric filter

> Filter on a total, like customers who spent more than $12k.

- Pattern id: `aggregate-filter`
- Category: Filters (also Scenarios & analyses)
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#aggregate-filter
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

Drag the slider to **$12k**. The customer list shrinks from 200 rows to the 16 who spent more than that.

Why: A condition on a total is a different kind of filter from a condition on a row. The reader shouldn't have to know that.

## What to build

Moving the slider sets a minimum total; the list keeps only items whose summed value clears it, and counts them.

Layout: Customer leaderboard with a threshold slider; rows below the line fade out.

Instruction: Add a slider that filters on a total, like revenue per customer, rather than on single rows, and show how many remain.

Done when: Raising the slider shortens the list, every item left is above the threshold, and the count shown matches the rows left.

On the ecommerce sample: The list starts at 200 of 200 customers; dragging Revenue over to $12k shrinks it to 16 of 200, each of whom spent more.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { customer: customers.name, country: customers.country }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count }
  sorts { total_revenue desc }
}
```

Reader input the SDK sent:

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "field": "revenue",
      "operator": "greater_than",
      "values": [
        "12000"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Saved result:

| customer | country | total_revenue | num_orders |
|---|---|---|---|
| Customer 184 | Australia | 23750.30 | 13 |
| Customer 25 | Singapore | 20785.85 | 18 |
| Customer 140 | United States | 16482.34 | 9 |
| Customer 27 | Vietnam | 13553.76 | 9 |
| Customer 14 | Australia | 13460.39 | 12 |
| Customer 55 | Australia | 13447.66 | 11 |
| Customer 92 | Germany | 13118.24 | 14 |
| Customer 66 | Vietnam | 12779.49 | 12 |
| Customer 85 | United States | 12760.59 | 9 |
| Customer 43 | Singapore | 12551.70 | 13 |
| Customer 127 | Australia | 12543.48 | 16 |
| Customer 114 | Vietnam | 12464.46 | 9 |

(4 more rows)

Mapping a control onto the dataset metric `revenue` becomes a `having` condition. A **query-local** metric was rejected ("unknown field: expected a dataset field as model.field or a dataset metric"), so `aov` is now a Dataset metric: run 44 filters customers to AOV over $1,300 the same way.

## SDK wiring

```js
const minRevenue = app.createFilter('minRevenue', {
  type: 'number',
  label: 'Revenue over',
});
// dataset metric → having
app.mapControl(minRevenue, customers, { field: 'revenue' });

// or on any field, with an aggregation
app.mapControl(minUnits, customers, {
  field: 'order_items.quantity',
  aggregation: 'sum',
});

slider.oninput = () => {
  minRevenue.setCondition({
    operator: 'greater_than',
    values: [String(slider.value)],
  });
  app.execute();
};
```

State it touches: Analytical: one number condition, applied after aggregation.

## Notes

- The same `mapControl` call works. Point it at a metric, and anfra puts the condition in `having`
- Number values are strings, so no digits are lost

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><label class="lbl" for="min">Revenue over</label><input type="range" id="min" min="0" max="24000" step="1000" value="0" style="width: 220px"><b id="val">no minimum</b></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Customers by revenue: <span id="kpi">–</span></b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="table"></div>
		<div class="hint" style="margin-top: 6px">The condition is on the revenue total, so anfra puts it in having, after aggregation</div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Metric filter', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const customers = app.createQuery('customers', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { customer_name: customers.name, country_name: customers.country } measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const minRevenue = app.createFilter('minRevenue', { type: 'number', label: 'Revenue over' });
app.mapControl(minRevenue, customers, { field: 'revenue' });
const slider = K.$('#min');
let all = null, t = 0;
const label = () => { const v = Number(slider.value); K.$('#val').textContent = v ? K.compact.format(v) : 'no minimum'; };
slider.oninput = () => {
	label();
	clearTimeout(t);
	t = setTimeout(() => { const v = Number(slider.value); if (v) minRevenue.setCondition({ operator: 'greater_than', values: [String(v)] }); else minRevenue.reset(); app.execute(); }, 250);
};
app.subscribe(() => {
K.status(customers, K.$('#s1'));
if (customers.result) {
	const rows = customers.result.rows;
	const c = minRevenue.appliedCondition;
	if (!(c && c.values && c.values.length)) all = rows.length;
	K.$('#kpi').textContent = K.int.format(rows.length) + (all != null ? ' of ' + K.int.format(all) : '');
	K.table(K.$('#table'), [{ key: 'customer_name', label: 'Customer' }, { key: 'country_name', label: 'Country' }, { key: 'total_revenue', label: 'Revenue', num: true, fmt: (v) => K.money.format(Number(v)) }, { key: 'num_orders', label: 'Orders', num: true }], rows);
}
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [customers]);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read the title: **Customers by revenue** lists 200 of 200
2. Drag the **Revenue over** slider to **$12K**
3. Read the list: it shrinks to 16 of 200, the customers who spent more than $12k

## Other Filters patterns

- [Field filter](field-filter.md): Pick values from a list, like Vietnam and Singapore, and every chart shows only those.
- [Widget filter](scope-vs-filter.md): A rule built into one chart, like "completed orders only", that viewers can't remove.
- [Filter group](compound-filter.md): Combine conditions with AND and OR, like (Vietnam and Software) or cancelled.
- [Range filter](range-filter.md): Drag a slider to keep orders between two values, or above or below one.
- [Text filter](text-search.md): Type part of a name to find matching rows, ignoring upper and lower case.

# Range filter

> Drag a slider to keep orders between two values, or above or below one.

- Pattern id: `range-filter`
- Category: Filters (also Controls)
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#range-filter
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

A two-handled slider keeps orders worth **$500 to $2,000**: 589 orders and $622,557. Switching to **one handle, over $2,000** leaves 195 orders, $388k of them Services. Two handles from $2,000 to the top find 205: `between` keeps the 10 orders of exactly $2,000, and `>` leaves them out.

Why: Readers think in ranges: big orders, small baskets, the middle band. A slider shows the range at a glance and is quick to adjust.

## What to build

Two handles keep values between them; one handle keeps values over or under it. The charts update a moment after the reader stops dragging.

Layout: A slider with one or two handles over an order-value track, an orders KPI and revenue by category.

Instruction: Add a range slider filter on a number field in my app, with two handles for a range or one handle for over or under, plus number inputs for exact values.

Done when: The handles can't cross, the typed values and the handles agree, and the label says whether each end is included.

On the ecommerce sample: $500 to $2,000 shows 589 orders and $622,557. Over $2,000 shows 195 orders, 10 fewer than $2,000 to the top, because between includes $2,000 and over does not.

## AQL

Not run as written: the slider sets a condition on orders.order_value, a Dataset dimension.

```aql
explore { dimensions { category_name: products.category } measures { total_revenue: revenue } filters { orders.order_value between 500 and 2000 } sorts { total_revenue desc } }
```

The SDK's number operators are `between`, `greater_than` and `less_than`. `between` compiles to `>=` and `<=`, so it keeps both ends; one handle compiles to `>` or `<` and leaves its end out. There is no SDK operator for "at least".

## SDK wiring

```js
const value = app.createFilter('orderValue', {
  dataset: 'ecommerce',
  field: 'orders.order_value',
});
app.mapControl(value, byCategory, { field: 'orders.order_value' });
// two handles, or one: over or under
const condition = {
  two: { operator: 'between', values: [lo, hi] },
  min: { operator: 'greater_than', values: [lo] },
  max: { operator: 'less_than', values: [hi] },
}[mode];
// values are strings, and the drag is debounced
value.setCondition(condition);
app.execute();
```

State it touches: Predicate: one number condition on a field. Which handles show, and where they sit, is renderer state.

## Notes

- `orders.order_value` is declared once in the Dataset; the slider only sets the operator and values

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<style>
		.rs { position: relative; height: 32px; margin: 0 2px; }
		.rs .tr { position: absolute; left: 8px; right: 8px; top: 14px; height: 4px; border-radius: 2px; background: var(--sunken); }
		.rs .fl { position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; border-radius: 2px; background: var(--violet); }
		.rs input { position: absolute; left: 0; width: 100%; top: 8px; height: 16px; margin: 0; background: none; pointer-events: none; -webkit-appearance: none; appearance: none; }
		.rs input[hidden] { display: none; }
		.rs input::-webkit-slider-runnable-track { background: none; height: 16px; }
		.rs input::-webkit-slider-thumb { pointer-events: auto; -webkit-appearance: none; width: 16px; height: 16px; border-radius: 50%; background: #fff; border: 2px solid var(--violet); box-shadow: 0 1px 3px rgb(24 20 31 / 0.2); cursor: grab; }
		.rs input::-moz-range-thumb { pointer-events: auto; width: 12px; height: 12px; border-radius: 50%; background: #fff; border: 2px solid var(--violet); cursor: grab; }
		.rs input:focus-visible::-webkit-slider-thumb { outline: 2px solid var(--violet); outline-offset: 2px; }
		.ends { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; color: var(--muted); }
		.nums { display: flex; gap: 8px; align-items: center; font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted); }
		.nums label[hidden] { display: none; }
		.nums input { width: 96px; }
		.cond { font: 400 12px/16px 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; color: var(--violet-ink); }
		.cols2 { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 180px minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 12px; }
	</style>
	<div class="app">
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Order value</b><span class="seg" id="modes"></span></div>
			<div class="rs" id="rs"><div class="tr"><span class="fl" id="fl"></span></div><input type="range" id="lo" min="0" max="5500" step="50" value="500" aria-label="Lowest order value"><input type="range" id="hi" min="0" max="5500" step="50" value="2000" aria-label="Highest order value"></div>
			<div class="ends"><span>$0</span><span>$5,500</span></div>
			<div class="nums"><label id="loL">From $ <input type="number" id="loN" min="0" max="5500" step="50"></label><label id="hiL">To $ <input type="number" id="hiN" min="0" max="5500" step="50"></label><span class="cond" id="cond"></span></div>
		</div>
		<div class="cols2">
			<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Orders in range</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div class="kpi" id="kOrders">–</div><div class="hint" id="kRev"></div></div>
			<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by category</b><span class="status" id="s2"></span></div><div id="bars"></div></div>
		</div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Range filter', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const total = app.createQuery('total', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { measures { num_orders: order_count, total_revenue: revenue } }' });
const byCat = app.createQuery('byCategory', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { category_name: products.category } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const value = app.createFilter('orderValue', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'orders.order_value', label: 'Order value' });
app.mapControl(value, total, { field: 'orders.order_value' });
app.mapControl(value, byCat, { field: 'orders.order_value' });
const MAX = 5500;
const MODES = [['two', 'Two handles'], ['min', 'One: over'], ['max', 'One: under']];
let mode = 'two', t = 0;
const lo = K.$('#lo'), hi = K.$('#hi'), loN = K.$('#loN'), hiN = K.$('#hiN');
const usd = (v) => '$' + K.int.format(v);
for (const [k, label] of MODES) { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = label; b.dataset.m = k; b.onclick = () => { mode = k; sync(true); }; K.$('#modes').appendChild(b); }
// the handles can't cross: the one you move stops at the other
lo.oninput = () => { if (mode === 'two' && +lo.value > +hi.value) lo.value = hi.value; sync(); };
hi.oninput = () => { if (mode === 'two' && +hi.value < +lo.value) hi.value = lo.value; sync(); };
loN.onchange = () => { lo.value = Math.max(0, Math.min(+loN.value || 0, mode === 'two' ? +hi.value : MAX)); sync(true); };
hiN.onchange = () => { hi.value = Math.min(MAX, Math.max(+hiN.value || 0, mode === 'two' ? +lo.value : 0)); sync(true); };
function condition () {
	const a = +lo.value, b = +hi.value;
	if (mode === 'min') return a > 0 ? { operator: 'greater_than', values: [String(a)] } : null;
	if (mode === 'max') return b < MAX ? { operator: 'less_than', values: [String(b)] } : null;
	return a > 0 || b < MAX ? { operator: 'between', values: [String(a), String(b)] } : null;
}
function sync (now) {
	K.$('#modes').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.dataset.m === mode)));
	lo.hidden = mode === 'max'; hi.hidden = mode === 'min';
	K.$('#loL').hidden = mode === 'max'; K.$('#hiL').hidden = mode === 'min';
	loN.value = lo.value; hiN.value = hi.value;
	const a = mode === 'max' ? 0 : +lo.value, b = mode === 'min' ? MAX : +hi.value;
	const fl = K.$('#fl'); fl.style.left = (a / MAX * 100) + '%'; fl.style.width = ((b - a) / MAX * 100) + '%';
	const c = condition();
	K.$('#cond').textContent = !c ? 'no filter: every order' : 'orders.order_value ' + (c.operator === 'between' ? 'between ' + c.values[0] + ' and ' + c.values[1] : (c.operator === 'greater_than' ? '> ' : '< ') + c.values[0]);
	clearTimeout(t);
	t = setTimeout(() => { if (c) value.setCondition(c); else value.reset(); app.execute(); }, now ? 0 : 250);
}
app.subscribe(() => {
	K.status(total, K.$('#s1')); K.status(byCat, K.$('#s2'));
	if (total.result && total.result.rows[0]) { const r = total.result.rows[0]; K.$('#kOrders').textContent = K.int.format(Number(r.num_orders)); K.$('#kRev').textContent = K.money.format(Number(r.total_revenue || 0)) + ' revenue'; }
	if (byCat.result) K.bars(K.$('#bars'), byCat.result.rows, { label: (r) => r.category_name, value: (r) => r.total_revenue });
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [total, byCat]);
});
sync(true);
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read the slider: two handles keep orders worth **$500 to $2,000**, which is **589 orders** and $622,557
2. Drag the right handle to the end, then type **2000** in **From**: **205 orders**, with the condition `between 2000 and 5500`
3. Click **One: over**: only the left handle stays, the condition becomes `> 2000`, and the count drops to **195**, since the 10 orders of exactly $2,000 are left out
4. Click **One: under** and drag the handle: the charts follow, a quarter of a second after you stop

## Other Filters patterns

- [Field filter](field-filter.md): Pick values from a list, like Vietnam and Singapore, and every chart shows only those.
- [Widget filter](scope-vs-filter.md): A rule built into one chart, like "completed orders only", that viewers can't remove.
- [Filter group](compound-filter.md): Combine conditions with AND and OR, like (Vietnam and Software) or cancelled.
- [Metric filter](aggregate-filter.md): Filter on a total, like customers who spent more than $12k.
- [Text filter](text-search.md): Type part of a name to find matching rows, ignoring upper and lower case.

---

# Text filter

> Type part of a name to find matching rows, ignoring upper and lower case.

- Pattern id: `text-search`
- Category: Filters
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#text-search
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader types **customer 1** into a search box. The completed-orders table keeps the matching names, now sorted by order count.

Why: A search box is often the quickest way to find one customer or one product.

## What to build

Typing in the search box keeps rows whose name contains the text, ignoring case; clearing the box brings every row back.

Layout: Search box above a customer table; matching rows stay, others leave.

Instruction: Add a search box that keeps rows whose name contains the typed text, ignoring case; clearing it shows everything again.

Done when: Matches update as you type, upper and lower case both match, and an empty box shows the full list again.

On the ecommerce sample: Type customer 1: the table keeps only names that contain it, sorted by orders; clearing the box returns the full list sorted by revenue.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { customer: customers.name, country: customers.country }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count }
  filters { orders.status == 'completed' }
  sorts { total_revenue desc }
}
```

Reader input the SDK sent:

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "field": "customers.name",
      "operator": "contains",
      "values": [
        "customer 1"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "sorts": [
    {
      "field": "num_orders",
      "direction": "desc"
    }
  ]
}
```

Saved result:

| customer | country | total_revenue | num_orders |
|---|---|---|---|
| Customer 127 | Australia | 6832.78 | 10 |
| Customer 199 | United States | 8000.64 | 9 |
| Customer 14 | Australia | 7602.60 | 8 |
| Customer 101 | Singapore | 7600.60 | 8 |
| Customer 175 | Germany | 1770.03 | 8 |
| Customer 155 | Singapore | 7767.50 | 8 |
| Customer 15 | United States | 3074.15 | 8 |
| Customer 171 | Germany | 3119.01 | 8 |
| Customer 184 | Australia | 14270.00 | 7 |
| Customer 17 | Singapore | 7813.01 | 7 |
| Customer 18 | Singapore | 5743.48 | 7 |
| Customer 129 | Japan | 3052.50 | 7 |

(28 more rows)

## SDK wiring

```js
const name = app.createFilter('name', {
  dataset: 'ecommerce',
  field: 'customers.name',
});
app.mapControl(name, table, { field: 'customers.name' });
input.oninput = debounce(() => {
  name.setCondition({
    operator: 'contains',
    values: input.value ? [input.value] : [],
  });
  table.setSort([{ field: 'num_orders', direction: 'desc' }]);
  app.execute();
}, 250);
```

State it touches: Analytical: a contains condition and a sort. Runtime: the debounce and the in-flight abort.

## Notes

- `contains` is case-insensitive
- An empty value list sends nothing, so the box clears itself

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><input type="search" id="q" placeholder="Search customers…" aria-label="Search customers" style="width: 240px"><span class="hint">Contains, ignoring case. Typing waits 300 ms and cancels a run still in flight</span></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Customers with completed orders<span id="by"></span></b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="table"></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
		<style>.tw { max-height: 232px; }</style>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Text filter', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const table = app.createQuery('customers', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { customer_name: customers.name, country_name: customers.country } measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count } filters { orders.status == \'completed\' } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const name = app.createFilter('name', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.name', label: 'Customer' });
app.mapControl(name, table, { field: 'customers.name' });
const input = K.$('#q');
let t = 0, aborted = 0;
input.oninput = () => {
	clearTimeout(t);
	t = setTimeout(() => {
		const v = input.value.trim();
		if (v) { name.setCondition({ operator: 'contains', values: [v] }); table.setSort([{ field: 'num_orders', direction: 'desc' }]); }
		else { name.reset(); table.setSort([]); }
		if (table.state === 'executing') { table.abort(); aborted++; }
		app.execute();
	}, 300);
};
app.subscribe(() => {
K.status(table, K.$('#s1'));
const sorted = table.sort.length > 0;
K.$('#by').textContent = sorted ? ' · sorted by orders' : ' · sorted by revenue';
if (table.result) K.table(K.$('#table'), [{ key: 'customer_name', label: 'Customer' }, { key: 'country_name', label: 'Country' }, { key: 'total_revenue', label: 'Revenue', num: true, fmt: (v) => K.money.format(Number(v)) }, { key: 'num_orders', label: sorted ? 'Orders ▼' : 'Orders', num: true }], table.result.rows);
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [table], () => [sorted ? 'sort → num_orders desc (overrides the AQL sort)' : 'sort → the AQL default (total_revenue desc)', aborted ? 'runs cancelled while typing → ' + aborted : '']);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Click the **Search customers…** box
2. Type **customer 1**
3. Read the table: it keeps the matching names, now **sorted by orders** with **Orders ▼**
4. Clear the box to go back to the sort by revenue

## Other Filters patterns

- [Field filter](field-filter.md): Pick values from a list, like Vietnam and Singapore, and every chart shows only those.
- [Widget filter](scope-vs-filter.md): A rule built into one chart, like "completed orders only", that viewers can't remove.
- [Filter group](compound-filter.md): Combine conditions with AND and OR, like (Vietnam and Software) or cancelled.
- [Metric filter](aggregate-filter.md): Filter on a total, like customers who spent more than $12k.
- [Range filter](range-filter.md): Drag a slider to keep orders between two values, or above or below one.

# Filter mapping

> Choose which charts a filter changes, so a benchmark chart can stay unfiltered.

- Pattern id: `one-control-many`
- Category: Controls (also Filters)
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#one-control-many
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader picks **Japan**. The KPI and the trend switch to Japan. The "All countries" benchmark doesn't move, because it isn't mapped.

Why: A benchmark that follows every filter stops being a benchmark. Each mapping is declared, so nothing is wired by accident.

## What to build

Each chart is mapped to the filters that should change it; an unmapped chart ignores them and carries a label saying so.

Layout: KPI tile + trend that follow the filter, next to a benchmark panel with a "not mapped" tag.

Instruction: Choose which charts each filter changes, and label any chart that stays unfiltered, like a benchmark.

Done when: Changing the filter moves only the mapped charts, the unmapped one stays put with its label, and clearing restores them all.

On the ecommerce sample: Click Japan: the KPI and trend switch to Revenue · Japan, while Benchmark: all countries keeps its bars and still says ran 1 time.

## AQL

Not run as written: uses the trend query from "Field filter" and the country query from "Percent of total".

```aql
// trend: mapped
explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { period asc } }
// benchmark: same Dataset, deliberately not mapped
explore { dimensions { country: customers.country } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }
```

## SDK wiring

```js
for (const q of [kpi, trend])
  app.mapControl(country, q, { field: 'customers.country' });
// benchmark: no mapping, so the filter never reaches it
// the full wiring, inspectable
console.log(app.mappings.map((e) => e.id));
```

State it touches: Interaction mapping: edges from a control to queries. `app.mappings` lists every edge.

## Notes

- Every edge is declared, and there is no "filter everything" shortcut
- The Inspect panel (`_lib/inspector.js`) draws the graph

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Country</span><span class="chips" id="countries"></span></div>
		<div class="cols" style="grid-template-columns: 1.3fr 1fr">
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue · <span id="for">all countries</span></b><span class="tag on">follows Country</span></div>
			<div class="kpi" id="kpi">–</div><div class="hint" style="margin-bottom: 6px">KPI query <span class="status" id="s1"></span> · trend query <span class="status" id="s2"></span></div><div id="trend"></div></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Benchmark: all countries</b><span class="tag">not mapped</span></div><div id="bench"></div><div class="hint" style="margin-top: 6px">No mapping reaches it, so it never re-runs <span class="status" id="s3"></span></div></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
		<style>.ph { align-items: flex-start; } .tag { align-self: flex-start; font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; padding: 0 6px; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px dashed var(--rule-strong); color: var(--muted); white-space: nowrap; } .tag.on { border: 1px solid var(--violet); color: var(--violet-ink); background: var(--violet-soft); } .hint .status { font-size: 12px; } .b { grid-template-columns: 84px minmax(0, 1fr) 48px; }</style>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Filter mapping', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const kpi = app.createQuery('kpi', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { measures { total_revenue: revenue } }' });
const trend = app.createQuery('trend', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { period asc } }' });
const bench = app.createQuery('benchmark', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { country_name: customers.country } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const country = app.createFilter('country', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.country', label: 'Country' });
for (const q of [kpi, trend]) app.mapControl(country, q, { field: 'customers.country' });
let picked = null;
const runs = { kpi: 0, trend: 0, benchmark: 0 }, was = {};
const chips = K.$('#countries');
country.loadOptions().then((vals) => vals.forEach((v) => { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = v; b.dataset.v = v; b.onclick = () => { picked = picked === v ? null : v; if (picked) country.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [picked] }); else country.reset(); app.execute(); }; chips.appendChild(b); }));
const mon = (v) => new Date(v).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', year: '2-digit', timeZone: 'UTC' });
app.subscribe(() => {
for (const q of [kpi, trend, bench]) { if (q.state === 'executing' && was[q.name] !== 'executing') runs[q.name]++; was[q.name] = q.state; }
chips.querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.dataset.v === picked)));
K.status(kpi, K.$('#s1')); K.status(trend, K.$('#s2'));
K.$('#s3').textContent = '· ran ' + runs.benchmark + (runs.benchmark === 1 ? ' time' : ' times');
K.$('#for').textContent = picked || 'all countries';
if (kpi.result) K.$('#kpi').textContent = K.money.format(Number(kpi.result.rows[0]?.total_revenue || 0));
if (trend.result) K.columns(K.$('#trend'), trend.result.rows, { label: (r) => mon(r.period), value: (r) => r.total_revenue });
if (bench.result) K.bars(K.$('#bench'), bench.result.rows, { label: (r) => r.country_name, value: (r) => r.total_revenue, on: (r) => r.country_name === picked });
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [kpi, trend, bench], () => ['app.mappings → ' + app.mappings.map((e) => e.id).join(', ')]);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Click **Japan** in the **Country** row
2. Read the left panel: the KPI and the trend switch to **Revenue · Japan**
3. Read **Benchmark: all countries**: its bars don't move, and it still says ran 1 time
4. Click **Japan** again to go back to all countries

- [Parent-child filter](cascading-options.md): Picking a category limits the product list to products in that category.
- [Apply button](apply-button.md): Change several filters, then press Apply to update every chart at once.
- [Cross filter](selection-to-filter.md): Turn a clicked selection into a filter chip, so your next click narrows further.
- [Zoom / pan](zoom-pan.md): Scrolling zooms the picture, and double-clicking reloads that month week by week.
- [Legend visibility](legend-toggle.md): Click a legend item to hide its line, or Alt-click to show only that line.
- [Custom right-click menu](custom-menu.md): Right-click a data point to open a menu of actions, and choose which actions it offers.

# Parent-child filter

> Picking a category limits the product list to products in that category.

- Pattern id: `cascading-options`
- Category: Controls (also Filters)
- Status: Works with app code: anfra supplies the queries, the app adds some logic
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#cascading-options
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader picks **Category: Hardware**, and the product picker shrinks from 8 options to 3. A product that no longer fits is dropped from the selection.

Why: A picker that offers impossible combinations leads to empty charts.

## What to build

Picking a parent value reloads the child picker with only the values under it, and drops child picks that no longer fit.

Layout: Two dropdowns side by side; the second one's list animates down to the matching items.

Instruction: Make a child picker offer only the values that fit the parent pick, and drop child picks that no longer fit.

Done when: The child list shrinks to values that fit, a stale pick is dropped with a note, and clearing restores the list.

On the ecommerce sample: Product starts with 8 options; pick Analytics Pro, then Hardware: the list shrinks to Gadget, Gizmo and Widget, and a note drops Analytics Pro.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { product: products.name }
  sorts { product asc }
}
```

Reader input the SDK sent:

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "field": "products.category",
      "operator": "is",
      "values": [
        "Hardware"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Saved result:

| product |
|---|
| Gadget |
| Gizmo |
| Widget |

`loadOptions()` takes no other conditions, because the suggestions request carries only dataset, model, field and search text. So the dependent list comes from a small query mapped to the parent control.

## SDK wiring

```js
const category = app.createFilter('category', {
  dataset: 'ecommerce',
  field: 'products.category',
});
const product = app.createFilter('product', {
  dataset: 'ecommerce',
  field: 'products.name',
});
const productOptions = app.createQuery('productOptions', {
  dataset: 'ecommerce',
  aql: OPTIONS_AQL,
});
app.mapControl(category, productOptions, {
  field: 'products.category',
});
for (const q of [trend, table]) {
  app.mapControl(category, q, { field: 'products.category' });
  app.mapControl(product, q, { field: 'products.name' });
}
productOptions.subscribe(() => {
  const ok = new Set(
    productOptions.result?.rows.map((r) => r.product),
  );
  const keep =
    product.condition.values?.filter((v) => ok.has(v)) ?? [];
  if (keep.length !== (product.condition.values?.length ?? 0))
    product.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: keep });
});
```

## Notes

- The options query is a three-line `explore` that uses the same mapping
- The mapping is explicit, so the cascade shows in the Inspect panel
- Limits: Works with app code. A proposed `dependsOn` option on `createFilter` would replace the options query.

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><label class="lbl" for="cat">Category</label><select id="cat"><option value="">All categories</option></select><span class="hint" id="count"></span></div>
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Product</span><span class="chips" id="prods"></span></div>
		<div class="hint" id="note">Pick a product, then a category it isn't in</div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by product<span id="for"></span></b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="bars"></div></div>
		<div class="hint">App code: the product list comes from a small options query mapped to Category, and the app drops picks that no longer fit</div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Parent-child filter', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const category = app.createFilter('category', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'products.category', label: 'Category' });
const product = app.createFilter('product', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'products.name', label: 'Product' });
const productOptions = app.createQuery('productOptions', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { product_name: products.name } sorts { product_name asc } }' });
const byProduct = app.createQuery('byProduct', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { product_name: products.name } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
app.mapControl(category, productOptions, { field: 'products.category' });
app.mapControl(category, byProduct, { field: 'products.category' });
app.mapControl(product, byProduct, { field: 'products.name' });
const picked = new Set();
const sel = K.$('#cat'), chips = K.$('#prods');
const setProduct = () => { if (picked.size) product.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [...picked] }); else product.reset(); };
category.loadOptions().then((vals) => vals.forEach((v) => sel.add(new Option(v, v))));
sel.onchange = async () => {
	if (sel.value) category.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [sel.value] }); else category.reset();
	const run = app.execute();
	if (picked.size) byProduct.abort();   // hold the chart until the new options say which picks still fit
	await run;
	const fit = new Set((productOptions.result?.rows || []).map((r) => r.product_name));
	const dropped = [...picked].filter((p) => !fit.has(p));
	dropped.forEach((p) => picked.delete(p));
	K.$('#note').textContent = dropped.length ? 'Dropped ' + dropped.join(', ') + ': not in ' + sel.value : 'Every picked product still fits';
	setProduct();
	app.execute();
};
const runs = { productOptions: 0, byProduct: 0 }, was = {};
app.subscribe(() => {
for (const q of [productOptions, byProduct]) { if (q.state === 'success' && was[q.name] !== 'success') runs[q.name]++; was[q.name] = q.state; }
if (productOptions.result) {
	const rows = productOptions.result.rows;
	const have = [...chips.children].map((b) => b.dataset.v).join('|');
	if (have !== rows.map((r) => r.product_name).join('|')) chips.replaceChildren(...rows.map((r) => { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = r.product_name; b.dataset.v = r.product_name; b.onclick = () => { picked.has(r.product_name) ? picked.delete(r.product_name) : picked.add(r.product_name); setProduct(); K.$('#note').textContent = 'Now pick a category'; app.execute(); }; return b; }));
	K.$('#count').textContent = rows.length + ' product options';
}
chips.querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(picked.has(b.dataset.v))));
K.status(byProduct, K.$('#s1'));
const c = category.appliedCondition, p = product.appliedCondition;
K.$('#for').textContent = (c && c.values && c.values.length ? ' · ' + c.values.join(', ') : '') + (p && p.values && p.values.length ? ' · ' + p.values.join(', ') : '');
if (byProduct.result && byProduct.state !== 'executing') K.bars(K.$('#bars'), byProduct.result.rows, { label: (r) => r.product_name, value: (r) => r.total_revenue });
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [productOptions, byProduct], () => ['runs so far → productOptions ' + runs.productOptions + ', byProduct ' + runs.byProduct]);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read the hint: the **Product** row starts with 8 product options
2. Click **Analytics Pro** in the **Product** row
3. Pick **Hardware** in the **Category** list
4. Read the hint: the row shrinks to 3 product options, **Gadget**, **Gizmo** and **Widget**
5. Read the note: Dropped Analytics Pro, not in Hardware
