# Apply button

> Change several filters, then press Apply to update every chart at once.

- Pattern id: `apply-button`
- Category: Controls (also Save & share)
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#apply-button
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader changes country, status and date. Nothing runs until they press **Apply (3)**, and then every query runs once.

Why: On a slow warehouse, every click shouldn't start a query.

## What to build

Filter changes wait as drafts with a pending count; pressing Apply sends them all together, so every chart updates once.

Layout: Filter chips turn dotted while unapplied; an Apply button counts changes.

Instruction: Let readers change several filters, see how many changes are pending, and update every chart at once when they press Apply.

Done when: Charts stay put while you edit, the button counts pending changes, and one press updates every chart and clears the count.

On the ecommerce sample: Pick Japan, Completed and Jul–Sep 2026: the chart doesn't change. Press Apply (3): every query runs once and the button turns to Applied ✓.

## AQL

Not run as written: any query works; this card is about when queries run.

```aql
// unchanged: the trend query from "Field filter"
explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { period asc } }
```

Trailer frame 2 approximates Japan's completed revenue at 62% of all of Japan's revenue.

## SDK wiring

```js
app.subscribe(() => {
  const n = Object.values(app.controls).filter(
    (c) => c.isDirty,
  ).length;
  applyBtn.disabled = !app.hasChanges;
  applyBtn.textContent = n ? `Apply (${n})` : 'Applied';
});
// commits pending → applied
applyBtn.onclick = () => app.execute();
```

State it touches: Analytical: pending conditions (`condition`) and applied ones (`appliedCondition`). Runtime: `hasChanges`.

## Notes

- Pending and applied state are built in: `condition`, `appliedCondition`, `isDirty` and `hasChanges`

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><select id="country" aria-label="Country"><option value="">All countries</option></select><select id="status" aria-label="Status"><option value="">Any status</option></select>
		<select id="dates" aria-label="Dates"><option value="">All dates</option><option value="2026-01-01|2026-12-31">2026</option><option value="2026-07-01|2026-09-30">Jul–Sep 2026</option></select></div>
		<div class="row"><button type="button" id="apply" class="go">Applied</button><button type="button" id="discard" hidden>Discard</button><span class="hint" id="pend">Change any filters: nothing runs until you press Apply</span></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue: <span id="kpi">–</span> <span class="hint" id="note">showing the applied filters</span></b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="trend"></div>
		<div class="hint" id="runs"></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
		<style>select.pend { border-style: dashed; border-color: var(--violet); background: var(--violet-faint); } .go:not(:disabled) { background: var(--violet); border-color: var(--violet); color: #fff; } .go:disabled { cursor: default; color: var(--muted); }</style>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Apply button', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const AQL = 'explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { period asc } }';
const kpi = app.createQuery('kpi', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { measures { total_revenue: revenue } }' });
const trend = app.createQuery('trend', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: AQL });
const country = app.createFilter('country', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.country', label: 'Country' });
const status = app.createFilter('status', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'orders.status', label: 'Status' });
const dates = app.createFilter('dates', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'orders.ordered_at', label: 'Dates' });
for (const q of [kpi, trend]) { app.mapControl(country, q, { field: 'customers.country' }); app.mapControl(status, q, { field: 'orders.status' }); app.mapControl(dates, q, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' }); }
const C = [[country, K.$('#country')], [status, K.$('#status')], [dates, K.$('#dates')]];
country.loadOptions().then((vals) => vals.forEach((v) => K.$('#country').add(new Option(v, v))));
status.loadOptions().then((vals) => vals.forEach((v) => K.$('#status').add(new Option(v[0].toUpperCase() + v.slice(1), v))));
const toCond = (ctl, v) => !v ? null : ctl === dates ? { operator: 'between', values: v.split('|') } : { operator: 'is', values: [v] };
const fromCond = (ctl, c) => !c || !c.values || !c.values.length ? '' : ctl === dates ? c.values.join('|') : String(c.values[0]);
C.forEach(([ctl, el]) => { el.onchange = () => { const c = toCond(ctl, el.value); if (c) ctl.setCondition(c); else ctl.reset(); }; });
K.$('#apply').onclick = () => app.execute();
K.$('#discard').onclick = () => C.forEach(([ctl, el]) => { const c = ctl.appliedCondition; if (c && c.values && c.values.length) ctl.setCondition(c); else ctl.reset(); el.value = fromCond(ctl, c); });
const runs = { kpi: 0, trend: 0 }, was = {};
const mon = (v) => new Date(v).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', year: '2-digit', timeZone: 'UTC' });
app.subscribe(() => {
for (const q of [kpi, trend]) { if (q.state === 'success' && was[q.name] !== 'success') runs[q.name]++; was[q.name] = q.state; }
const dirty = C.filter(([ctl]) => ctl.isDirty);
C.forEach(([ctl, el]) => el.classList.toggle('pend', ctl.isDirty));
const btn = K.$('#apply');
btn.disabled = !app.hasChanges;
btn.textContent = dirty.length ? 'Apply (' + dirty.length + ')' : 'Applied ✓';
K.$('#discard').hidden = !dirty.length;
K.$('#pend').textContent = dirty.length ? dirty.length + (dirty.length === 1 ? ' change' : ' changes') + ' waiting: the chart still shows the applied filters' : 'Change any filters: nothing runs until you press Apply';
K.status(trend, K.$('#s1'));
if (kpi.result) K.$('#kpi').textContent = K.compact.format(Number(kpi.result.rows[0]?.total_revenue || 0));
if (trend.result) K.columns(K.$('#trend'), trend.result.rows, { label: (r) => mon(r.period), value: (r) => r.total_revenue });
K.$('#runs').textContent = 'Runs so far: kpi ' + runs.kpi + ', trend ' + runs.trend;
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [kpi, trend], () => [dirty.length ? 'pending, not sent → ' + dirty.map(([ctl]) => ctl.name + ' ' + (K.cond(ctl.condition) || 'cleared')).join('; ') : '']);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Pick **Japan** in the **All countries** list
2. Pick **Completed** in the **Any status** list
3. Pick **Jul–Sep 2026** in the **All dates** list: nothing runs, and the chart still shows the applied filters
4. Press **Apply (3)**: every query runs once, and the button turns to **Applied ✓**

## Other Controls patterns

- [Filter mapping](one-control-many.md): Choose which charts a filter changes, so a benchmark chart can stay unfiltered.
- [Parent-child filter](cascading-options.md): Picking a category limits the product list to products in that category.
- [Cross filter](selection-to-filter.md): Turn a clicked selection into a filter chip, so your next click narrows further.
- [Zoom / pan](zoom-pan.md): Scrolling zooms the picture, and double-clicking reloads that month week by week.
- [Legend visibility](legend-toggle.md): Click a legend item to hide its line, or Alt-click to show only that line.
- [Custom right-click menu](custom-menu.md): Right-click a data point to open a menu of actions, and choose which actions it offers.

# Cross filter

> Turn a clicked selection into a filter chip, so your next click narrows further.

- Pattern id: `selection-to-filter`
- Category: Controls (also Selections, Filters)
- Status: Works with app code: anfra supplies the queries, the app adds some logic
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#selection-to-filter
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader clicks **Vietnam** on the bar chart, then presses **📌 Pin**. Vietnam turns into a filter chip, and the next click (Software) starts a new selection inside Vietnam.

Why: An app holds one selection at a time. Pinning lets the reader stack questions anyway.

## What to build

Clicking a bar selects it; pressing Pin turns that selection into a filter chip, so the next click selects within it.

Layout: Country bars + category bars; a pin icon appears on the selected bar.

Instruction: Add a Pin button that turns the current chart selection into a filter chip, so readers can narrow step by step.

Done when: Pin makes a chip named for the pick, later clicks select inside it, and removing the chip widens the page again.

On the ecommerce sample: Click Vietnam, then Pin: a Country: Vietnam chip appears, and clicking Software starts a new selection inside Vietnam. Removing the chip lifts the filter.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { category: products.category }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue }
  sorts { total_revenue desc }
}
```

Reader input the SDK sent:

```json
{
  "conditions": [
    {
      "expr": "customers.country == 'Vietnam'"
    }
  ]
}
```

Saved result:

| category | total_revenue |
|---|---|
| Services | 91500.00 |
| Software | 68234.00 |
| Hardware | 23746.62 |
| Parts | 1774.15 |

The input shows how the SDK sends a selection: as a `conditions[].expr`. After pinning, the same value becomes a `filters[]` entry.

## SDK wiring

```js
pinBtn.onclick = () => {
  // { source, rows, conditions }
  const sel = app.selection;
  for (const c of sel.conditions) {
    // e.g. customers.country → country filter
    const f = filtersByField[c.field];
    f.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: c.values });
  }
  app.clearSelection();
  app.execute();
};
```

State it touches: Moves state from a selection, which can be replaced, to a control, which persists.

## Notes

- `app.selection.conditions` already holds the field and values, so pinning means copying them into a filter

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<style>#bycat .b, #bycountry .b { grid-template-columns: 100px minmax(0, 1fr) 54px; } .tag { font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; padding: 4px 10px; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px solid var(--violet); background: var(--violet-soft); color: var(--violet-ink); }</style>
		<div class="row"><span class="hint">Click a bar to select it, pin it to turn it into a filter, then click again</span></div>
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Revenue</span><span class="kpi" id="kpi">–</span><span class="status" id="s3"></span><button type="button" id="pin" hidden></button><span class="chips" id="chips"></span><span class="tag" id="seltag" hidden></span></div>
		<div class="cols"><div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by country</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="bycountry"></div></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by category<span id="cfor"></span></b><span class="status" id="s2"></span></div><div id="bycat"></div></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Cross filter', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const byCountry = app.createQuery('byCountry', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { country_name: customers.country } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const byCategory = app.createQuery('byCategory', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { category_name: products.category } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const kpi = app.createQuery('kpi', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { measures { total_revenue: revenue } }' });
for (const [a, b] of [[byCountry, byCategory], [byCountry, kpi], [byCategory, byCountry], [byCategory, kpi]]) app.mapCrossFilter(a, b);
const filtersByField = {
	'customers.country': app.createFilter('country', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.country', label: 'Country' }),
	'products.category': app.createFilter('category', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'products.category', label: 'Category' }),
};
for (const q of [byCategory, kpi]) app.mapControl(filtersByField['customers.country'], q, { field: 'customers.country' });
for (const q of [byCountry, kpi]) app.mapControl(filtersByField['products.category'], q, { field: 'products.category' });
const dim = { byCountry: 'country_name', byCategory: 'category_name' };
const pinned = (field) => { const c = filtersByField[field].condition; return c && c.values ? c.values.map(String) : []; };
K.$('#pin').onclick = () => {
	const sel = app.selection;
	for (const c of sel.conditions) filtersByField[c.field].setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: c.values });
	app.clearSelection();
	app.execute();
};
function draw (q, el, field) {
	if (!q.result) return;
	const d = dim[q.name], sel = q.selectedRows.map((r) => r[d]), pin = pinned(field);
	K.bars(K.$(el), q.result.rows, { label: (r) => r[d] + (pin.includes(r[d]) ? ' · pinned' : ''), value: (r) => r.total_revenue, on: (r) => sel.includes(r[d]) || pin.includes(r[d]),
		pick: (r) => { if (sel.length === 1 && sel[0] === r[d]) app.clearSelection(); else q.select([r]); app.execute(); } });
}
app.subscribe(() => {
K.status(byCountry, K.$('#s1')); K.status(byCategory, K.$('#s2')); K.status(kpi, K.$('#s3')); if (/row/.test(K.$('#s3').textContent)) K.$('#s3').textContent = '';
draw(byCountry, '#bycountry', 'customers.country'); draw(byCategory, '#bycat', 'products.category');
const k = kpi.result?.rows[0]; K.$('#kpi').textContent = k ? K.money.format(k.total_revenue) : '–';
const sel = app.selection, names = sel ? sel.rows.map((r) => r[dim[sel.source]]) : [];
const pin = K.$('#pin'); pin.hidden = !names.length; pin.textContent = 'Pin ' + names.join(', ');
const st = K.$('#seltag'); st.hidden = !names.length; st.textContent = 'Selected: ' + names.join(', ');
const chips = K.$('#chips'); chips.replaceChildren();
for (const [field, lab] of [['customers.country', 'Country'], ['products.category', 'Category']]) {
	const v = pinned(field); if (!v.length) continue;
	const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', 'true'); b.title = 'Remove this filter';
	b.textContent = lab + ': ' + v.join(', ') + '  ×'; b.onclick = () => { filtersByField[field].reset(); app.execute(); };
	chips.appendChild(b);
}
const cp = pinned('customers.country'); K.$('#cfor').textContent = cp.length ? ' · ' + cp.join(', ') : '';
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [kpi, byCategory, byCountry]);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Click **Vietnam** on **Revenue by country**: it becomes the selection
2. Click **Pin Vietnam**: Vietnam turns into a **Country: Vietnam** filter chip
3. Click **Software** on **Revenue by category**: a new selection starts inside Vietnam
4. Click the **Country: Vietnam ×** chip to remove the filter

- [Filter mapping](one-control-many.md): Choose which charts a filter changes, so a benchmark chart can stay unfiltered.
- [Parent-child filter](cascading-options.md): Picking a category limits the product list to products in that category.
- [Apply button](apply-button.md): Change several filters, then press Apply to update every chart at once.
- [Zoom / pan](zoom-pan.md): Scrolling zooms the picture, and double-clicking reloads that month week by week.
- [Legend visibility](legend-toggle.md): Click a legend item to hide its line, or Alt-click to show only that line.
- [Custom right-click menu](custom-menu.md): Right-click a data point to open a menu of actions, and choose which actions it offers.

# Zoom / pan

> Scrolling zooms the picture, and double-clicking reloads that month week by week.

- Pattern id: `zoom-pan`
- Category: Controls (also Dates & time)
- Status: Works with app code: anfra supplies the queries, the app adds some logic
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#zoom-pan
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

A scroll zooms the monthly chart without a new query. A double-click on September changes the question: the range becomes September and the grain becomes week, so the query runs again.

Why: Readers expect zoom to show more detail, but zooming pixels can't show detail that was never loaded.

## What to build

Scrolling zooms the loaded chart in place without a new query; double-clicking a period reloads it at a finer grain.

Layout: Monthly columns with a zoom window, then the same panel redrawn as weekly bars.

Instruction: Let scrolling zoom a time chart without reloading, and a double-click on a period reload it at a finer grain.

Done when: Zooming never adds a query, a double-click shows the finer grain with partial periods marked, and Back returns to the start.

On the ecommerce sample: Scroll to zoom: Queries run stays at 1. Double-click Sep 26: the title becomes Revenue by week · Sep 2026 and Queries run goes to 2.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count }
  sorts { period asc }
}
```

Reader input the SDK sent:

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "field": "orders.ordered_at",
      "operator": "between",
      "values": [
        "2026-09-01",
        "2026-09-30"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "dateDrills": [
    {
      "field": "orders.ordered_at",
      "grain": "week"
    }
  ]
}
```

Saved result:

| period | total_revenue | num_orders |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-31 | 25466.19 | 24 |
| 2026-09-07 | 23519.63 | 23 |
| 2026-09-14 | 10983.09 | 16 |
| 2026-09-21 | 5870.79 | 10 |

Week buckets start on Monday: the first one, which starts on 31 Aug, holds only 1–6 Sep. The hatched bars mark partial weeks.

## SDK wiring

```js
chart.on('datazoom', () => {
  /* renderer only: no execute() */
});
chart.on('dblclick', (p) => {
  const month = trend.result.rows[p.dataIndex].period;
  range.setCondition({
    operator: 'between',
    values: [month, endOfMonth(month)],
  });
  grain.setGrain('week');
  app.execute();
});
```

State it touches: Renderer: the zoom window. Analytical: the range and the grain.

## Notes

- `createDateDrill` re-buckets every dimension built on the field, and the row key (`period`) stays the same

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><span class="seg"><button type="button" id="zin" aria-label="Zoom in">＋</button><button type="button" id="zout" aria-label="Zoom out">－</button><button type="button" id="left" aria-label="Pan left">◀</button><button type="button" id="right" aria-label="Pan right">▶</button></span><button type="button" id="fit">Show all</button><button type="button" id="up" hidden>↑ Back to months</button></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b id="title">Revenue by month</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div>
		<div id="chart"></div><div class="mini" id="mini" aria-hidden="true"></div>
		<div class="hint" id="how">Scroll to zoom, drag to pan: no query. Double-click a month to load its weeks</div></div>
		<div class="row"><span class="hint" id="count"></span></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
		<style>.still .colz .cw .c { transition: none; } #chart { cursor: grab; user-select: none; } #chart .cw:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--violet); } .mini { display: flex; gap: 2px; height: 6px; margin-top: 6px; } .mini i { flex: 1; border-radius: 2px; background: var(--sunken); } .mini i.in { background: var(--violet-faint); } .colz .cw.part .c { background: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, var(--violet) 0 4px, var(--violet-faint) 4px 7px); }</style>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Zoom / pan', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const trend = app.createQuery('trend', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { period asc } }' });
const grain = app.createDateDrill('grain', { default: 'month', label: 'Grain' });
const range = app.createFilter('range', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'orders.ordered_at', label: 'Dates' });
app.mapControl(grain, trend, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });
app.mapControl(range, trend, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });
let g = 'month', label = '', a = 0, b = 0, n = 0, zooms = 0, runs = 0, was = '', lo = '', hi = '';
const chart = K.$('#chart');
const iso = (x) => x.toISOString().slice(0, 10);
const mon = (v) => new Date(v).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', year: '2-digit', timeZone: 'UTC' });
const day = (v) => 'w/c ' + new Date(v).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { day: 'numeric', month: 'short', timeZone: 'UTC' });
const clamp = () => { const w = Math.max(3, Math.min(n, b - a)); a = Math.max(0, Math.min(a, n - w)); b = a + w; };
function zoom (dir, at) { if (g !== 'month') return; const w = b - a, nw = Math.max(3, Math.min(n, w + dir * 2)); if (nw === w) return; const c = at == null ? (a + b) / 2 : at; a = Math.round(c - (c - a) * nw / w); b = a + nw; clamp(); zooms++; draw(true); }
function pan (d) { if (g !== 'month') return; const a0 = a; a += d; b += d; clamp(); if (a !== a0) { zooms++; draw(true); } }
function drill (r) {
	const s = new Date(r.period), e = new Date(s); e.setUTCMonth(e.getUTCMonth() + 1); e.setUTCDate(0);
	lo = iso(s); hi = iso(e);
	label = s.toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', year: 'numeric', timeZone: 'UTC' });
	range.setCondition({ operator: 'between', values: [lo, hi] }); grain.setGrain('week'); g = 'week'; app.execute();
}
K.$('#zin').onclick = () => zoom(-1); K.$('#zout').onclick = () => zoom(1);
K.$('#left').onclick = () => pan(-1); K.$('#right').onclick = () => pan(1);
K.$('#fit').onclick = () => { if (g === 'month' && (a || b !== n)) { a = 0; b = n; zooms++; draw(true); } };
K.$('#up').onclick = () => { range.reset(); grain.setGrain('month'); g = 'month'; label = ''; app.execute(); };
chart.addEventListener('wheel', (e) => { if (g !== 'month') return; e.preventDefault(); const r = chart.getBoundingClientRect(); const at = a + (e.clientX - r.left) / r.width * (b - a); if (e.shiftKey) pan(e.deltaY > 0 ? 1 : -1); else zoom(e.deltaY > 0 ? 1 : -1, at); }, { passive: false });
let drag = null;
chart.addEventListener('mousedown', (e) => { drag = { x: e.clientX, a }; });
addEventListener('mouseup', () => { drag = null; });
chart.addEventListener('mousemove', (e) => { if (drag && !(e.buttons & 1)) drag = null; if (!drag || g !== 'month') return; const step = chart.getBoundingClientRect().width / (b - a); const d = Math.round((drag.x - e.clientX) / step); const a0 = a, w = b - a; a = drag.a + d; b = a + w; clamp(); if (a !== a0) { zooms++; draw(true); } });
function draw (still) {
	if (!trend.result) return;
	const rows = trend.result.rows;
	const vis = g === 'month' ? rows.slice(a, b) : rows;
	chart.classList.toggle('still', !!still);
	if (!still) { const tp = document.querySelector('.tip'); if (tp) tp.style.opacity = 0; }
	K.columns(chart, vis, { label: (r) => g === 'month' ? mon(r.period) : day(r.period), value: (r) => r.total_revenue });
	chart.querySelectorAll('.cw').forEach((c, i) => {
		const r = vis[i];
		if (g === 'month') { c.tabIndex = 0; c.title = 'Double-click to reload ' + mon(r.period) + ' by week'; c.ondblclick = () => drill(r); c.onkeydown = (e) => { if (e.key === 'Enter') drill(r); }; }
		else { const s = iso(new Date(r.period)), e = new Date(r.period); e.setUTCDate(e.getUTCDate() + 6); if (s < lo || iso(e) > hi) c.classList.add('part'); }
	});
	K.$('#mini').replaceChildren(...(g === 'month' ? rows.map((r, i) => { const x = document.createElement('i'); if (i >= a && i < b) x.className = 'in'; return x; }) : []));
	K.$('#title').textContent = g === 'month' ? 'Revenue by month · ' + mon(vis[0].period) + ' to ' + mon(vis[vis.length - 1].period) : 'Revenue by week · ' + label;
	K.$('#count').textContent = 'Queries run: ' + runs + ' · zoom and pan steps: ' + zooms + ' (no query)';
}
app.subscribe(() => {
if (trend.state === 'success' && was !== 'success') { runs++; if (g === 'month' && trend.result.rows.length !== n) { n = trend.result.rows.length; a = 0; b = n; } }
was = trend.state;
K.status(trend, K.$('#s1'));
K.$('#up').hidden = g === 'month';
K.$('.seg').style.display = K.$('#fit').style.display = g === 'month' ? '' : 'none';
K.$('#how').textContent = g === 'month' ? 'Scroll to zoom, drag to pan: no query. Double-click a month to load its weeks' : 'Weeks start on Monday. Hatched weeks are cut by the month edge';
if (trend.state !== 'executing') draw(false);
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [trend]);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Scroll over the monthly chart, or click **＋**, to zoom in
2. Read the count: **Queries run** stays at 1, only the zoom steps go up
3. Double-click the **Sep 26** column
4. Read the title: **Revenue by week · Sep 2026**, and **Queries run** goes up to 2
5. Click **↑ Back to months** to return

## Other Controls patterns

- [Filter mapping](one-control-many.md): Choose which charts a filter changes, so a benchmark chart can stay unfiltered.
- [Parent-child filter](cascading-options.md): Picking a category limits the product list to products in that category.
- [Apply button](apply-button.md): Change several filters, then press Apply to update every chart at once.
- [Cross filter](selection-to-filter.md): Turn a clicked selection into a filter chip, so your next click narrows further.
- [Legend visibility](legend-toggle.md): Click a legend item to hide its line, or Alt-click to show only that line.
- [Custom right-click menu](custom-menu.md): Right-click a data point to open a menu of actions, and choose which actions it offers.

---

# Legend visibility

> Click a legend item to hide its line, or Alt-click to show only that line.

- Pattern id: `legend-toggle`
- Category: Controls (also Tables & calculations)
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#legend-toggle
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

Clicking **Services** in the legend hides its line, and the y-axis rescales without a query. Alt-clicking **Parts** filters the page to Parts, and every panel re-queries.

Why: The same gesture can mean "hide this" or "only this". The app should say which one it does.

## What to build

Clicking a legend item hides its series and rescales the chart in place; Alt-clicking it filters the whole page instead.

Layout: Four category lines with a clickable legend.

Instruction: Make a legend click hide or show a series, and an Alt-click filter the whole page to it, with a tooltip saying which.

Done when: A click hides one series with no new query, an Alt-click narrows every panel to it, and Show all brings everything back.

On the ecommerce sample: Click Services: its line hides and Queries run stays the same. Alt-click Parts: every panel re-queries and Total shows $13.7K.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { category: products.category, period: orders.ordered_at | month() }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue }
  sorts { category asc, period asc }
}
```

Saved result:

| category | period | total_revenue |
|---|---|---|
| Hardware | 2025-06-01 | 13004.19 |
| Hardware | 2025-07-01 | 12268.36 |
| Hardware | 2025-08-01 | 10002.78 |
| Hardware | 2025-09-01 | 14003.71 |
| Hardware | 2025-10-01 | 11678.16 |
| Hardware | 2025-11-01 | 12913.76 |
| Hardware | 2025-12-01 | 9702.93 |
| Hardware | 2026-01-01 | 12172.21 |
| Hardware | 2026-02-01 | 12057.99 |
| Hardware | 2026-03-01 | 10655.80 |
| Hardware | 2026-04-01 | 9702.93 |
| Hardware | 2026-05-01 | 12605.34 |

(28 more rows)

## SDK wiring

```js
chart.on('legendselectchanged', (e) => {
  /* hide: renderer only */
});
legendEl.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
  if (!e.altKey) return;
  category.setCondition({
    operator: 'is',
    values: [e.target.dataset.series],
  });
  app.execute();
});
```

State it touches: Renderer: which series are hidden. Analytical: the category filter.

## Notes

- Hiding stays in the renderer. Filtering is one `setCondition` call

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><span class="lg" id="legend"></span><button type="button" id="all" hidden>Show all</button></div>
		<div class="hint">Click hides a line (no query). Alt-click or Alt+Enter filters every panel to it</div>
		<div class="cols" style="grid-template-columns: 1fr 132px">
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by category, monthly</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="chart"></div></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Total</b><span class="status" id="s2"></span></div><div class="kpi" id="kpi">–</div><div class="hint" id="for">all categories</div></div></div>
		<div class="row"><span class="hint" id="count"></span></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
		<style>.lg { display: flex; gap: 4px; flex-wrap: wrap; } .lg button { height: 28px; padding: 0 10px; border-radius: 999px; font-size: 12px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; } .lg i { width: 10px; height: 3px; border-radius: 2px; display: inline-block; } .lg button.off { color: var(--muted); text-decoration: line-through; } .lg button.off i { opacity: 0.3; } .lg button.out { color: var(--muted); border-style: dashed; } .lg button.out i { opacity: 0.3; } #chart svg { display: block; overflow: visible; } #chart text { font-size: 12px; fill: var(--muted); font-family: inherit; } #chart path { transition: d 320ms var(--ease); }</style>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Legend visibility', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const lines = app.createQuery('lines', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { category_name: products.category, period: orders.ordered_at | month() } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { category_name asc, period asc } }' });
const kpi = app.createQuery('kpi', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { measures { total_revenue: revenue } }' });
const category = app.createFilter('category', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'products.category', label: 'Category' });
for (const q of [lines, kpi]) app.mapControl(category, q, { field: 'products.category' });
const COLORS = ['#8a51d4', '#1f9e89', '#e07b39', '#3b6fb6'];
let cats = [], only = null, hides = 0, runs = 0, was = '';
const hidden = new Set();
const legend = K.$('#legend');
const color = (c) => COLORS[Math.max(0, cats.indexOf(c)) % COLORS.length];
function filterTo (c) { only = only === c ? null : c; hidden.clear(); if (only) category.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [only] }); else category.reset(); app.execute(); }
function toggle (c) { if (only && only !== c) return; hidden.has(c) ? hidden.delete(c) : hidden.add(c); hides++; draw(); }
category.loadOptions().then((vals) => { cats = vals.map(String); legend.replaceChildren(...cats.map((c) => { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.dataset.c = c; b.innerHTML = '<i style="background:' + color(c) + '"></i>' + K.esc(c); b.onclick = (e) => { if (e.altKey) filterTo(c); else toggle(c); }; b.onkeydown = (e) => { if (e.key === 'Enter' && e.altKey) { e.preventDefault(); filterTo(c); } }; return b; })); draw(); });
K.$('#all').onclick = () => { hidden.clear(); hides++; if (only) filterTo(only); else draw(); };
const mon = (v) => new Date(v).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', year: '2-digit', timeZone: 'UTC' });
function draw () {
	legend.querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => { const c = b.dataset.c; b.classList.toggle('off', hidden.has(c)); b.classList.toggle('out', !!only && only !== c); b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(!hidden.has(c) && (!only || only === c))); b.title = only && only !== c ? 'Filtered out: Alt-click to filter to ' + c : hidden.has(c) ? 'Hidden: click to show' : 'Click to hide, Alt-click to show only this'; });
	K.$('#all').hidden = !hidden.size && !only;
	K.$('#count').textContent = 'Queries run: ' + runs + ' · legend hides: ' + hides + ' (no query)';
	if (!lines.result) return;
	const el = K.$('#chart'), W = Math.max(200, el.clientWidth), H = 170, L = 44, B = 18;
	const periods = [...new Set(lines.result.rows.map((r) => r.period))].sort();
	const series = new Map();
	lines.result.rows.forEach((r) => { if (!series.has(r.category_name)) series.set(r.category_name, new Map()); series.get(r.category_name).set(r.period, Number(r.total_revenue)); });
	const shown = [...series.keys()].filter((c) => !hidden.has(c));
	const max = Math.max(1, ...shown.flatMap((c) => [...series.get(c).values()])) * 1.08;
	const x = (i) => L + (periods.length > 1 ? i / (periods.length - 1) : 0.5) * (W - L - 4), y = (v) => (H - B) - v / max * (H - B - 6);
	let s = '<svg width="' + W + '" height="' + H + '" role="img" aria-label="Revenue by category">';
	[0, 0.5, 1].forEach((t) => { const v = max / 1.08 * t, yy = y(v); s += '<line x1="' + L + '" x2="' + W + '" y1="' + yy + '" y2="' + yy + '" stroke="rgb(24 20 31 / 0.08)"/><text x="' + (L - 6) + '" y="' + (yy + 4) + '" text-anchor="end">' + K.compact.format(v) + '</text>'; });
	[0, Math.floor((periods.length - 1) / 2), periods.length - 1].forEach((i, k) => { if (periods[i]) s += '<text x="' + x(i) + '" y="' + H + '" text-anchor="' + ['start', 'middle', 'end'][k] + '">' + mon(periods[i]) + '</text>'; });
	shown.forEach((c) => { const m = series.get(c); s += '<path fill="none" stroke="' + color(c) + '" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round" d="' + periods.map((p, i) => (i ? 'L' : 'M') + x(i).toFixed(1) + ' ' + y(m.get(p) || 0).toFixed(1)).join(' ') + '"><title>' + K.esc(c) + '</title></path>'; });
	el.innerHTML = s + '</svg>';
}
app.subscribe(() => {
if (lines.state === 'success' && was !== 'success') runs++;
was = lines.state;
K.status(lines, K.$('#s1')); K.status(kpi, K.$('#s2'));
if (kpi.result) K.$('#kpi').textContent = K.compact.format(Number(kpi.result.rows[0]?.total_revenue || 0));
K.$('#for').textContent = only || 'all categories';
draw();
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [lines, kpi], () => [hidden.size ? 'hidden in the renderer, not sent → ' + [...hidden].join(', ') : '']);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Click **Services** in the legend: its line hides and the y-axis rescales
2. Read the count: the legend hides go up, and **Queries run** stays the same
3. Hold Alt and click **Parts**: every panel re-queries for Parts only
4. Read **Total**: it shows Parts, $13.7K
5. Click **Show all** to bring every line back

## Other Controls patterns

- [Filter mapping](one-control-many.md): Choose which charts a filter changes, so a benchmark chart can stay unfiltered.
- [Parent-child filter](cascading-options.md): Picking a category limits the product list to products in that category.
- [Apply button](apply-button.md): Change several filters, then press Apply to update every chart at once.
- [Cross filter](selection-to-filter.md): Turn a clicked selection into a filter chip, so your next click narrows further.
- [Zoom / pan](zoom-pan.md): Scrolling zooms the picture, and double-clicking reloads that month week by week.
- [Custom right-click menu](custom-menu.md): Right-click a data point to open a menu of actions, and choose which actions it offers.

# Custom right-click menu

> Right-click a data point to open a menu of actions, and choose which actions it offers.

- Pattern id: `custom-menu`
- Category: Controls (also Drilling, Filters)
- Status: Works with app code: anfra supplies the queries, the app adds some logic
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#custom-menu
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

Right-clicking **Germany** opens a menu at the pointer: **Keep only**, **Exclude**, **Drill to customers** and **View orders**. The app author turns items on or off and adds their own, such as **Copy as AQL filter**. Exclude Germany and the chart drops to five countries; Drill to customers lists Customer 92 first, at $13,118.

Why: One click target can do many things. A menu says what each click will do, and the author keeps it to the actions that make sense for that chart.

## What to build

Right-clicking a data point opens a small menu at the pointer instead of the browser's. Each item sets a filter on the clicked value, on the same chart or on a detail query; the author decides which items appear.

Layout: Country bars with a right-click menu at the pointer, and a strip of menu items the author can toggle.

Instruction: Add a right-click menu to the data points in my chart, with Keep only, Exclude, a drill and View records, a list where I choose which items show, and room for my own items.

Done when: Right-click opens the menu at the pointer (the Menu key or Shift+F10 opens it from the keyboard), it lists only the items the author turned on, and Escape or a click elsewhere closes it.

On the ecommerce sample: Excluding Germany leaves five countries; Drill to customers in Germany lists Customer 92 first, at $13,118.

## AQL

Not run as written: each menu item is a filter on the clicked value, sent to the chart or to a detail query.

```aql
explore { dimensions { customer_name: customers.name } measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count } filters { customers.country is 'Germany' } sorts { total_revenue desc } }
```

## SDK wiring

```js
// the author's menu: a label and what it does with the row
const MENU = [
  { label: 'Keep only', run: (row) =>
      country.setCondition({ operator: 'is',
        values: [row.country_name] }) },
  { label: 'Exclude', run: (row) =>
      country.setCondition({ operator: 'is_not',
        values: [row.country_name] }) },
  { label: 'Drill to customers', run: (row) =>
      point.setCondition({ operator: 'is',
        values: [row.country_name] }) },
  // the author's own item
  { label: 'Copy as AQL filter', run: (row) =>
      navigator.clipboard.writeText(
        "customers.country is '" + row.country_name + "'") },
];
bar.oncontextmenu = (e) => {
  e.preventDefault(); // instead of the browser's menu
  openMenu(e.clientX, e.clientY, row, MENU.filter(isOn));
};
// each item ends the same way
const pick = (item, row) => { item.run(row); app.execute(); };
```

State it touches: Interaction mapping: which items the menu offers is renderer state. What each item does is a filter condition on the clicked value, so it shows up in the AQL.

## Notes

- Each item is `setCondition` on a filter that is already mapped to the right queries
- Limits: Works with app code: the app draws the menu and maps each item to an SDK call. A proposed `app.createMenu(query, items)` would offer the standard items, built from the Dataset's drill paths and fields.

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<style>.cfg { display: grid; gap: 6px; padding: 8px 10px; border-radius: 10px; background: var(--sunken); } .cfg .chips button[aria-pressed='false'] { color: var(--muted); text-decoration: line-through; text-decoration-color: rgb(24 20 31 / 0.35); } .cfg .chips .own { border-style: dashed; } #main { position: relative; } .mbar { position: absolute; z-index: 2; display: grid; min-width: 180px; gap: 2px; padding: 4px; border-radius: 10px; background: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong); box-shadow: 0 6px 20px rgb(24 20 31 / 0.14); } .mbar[hidden] { display: none; } .mbar button { height: 28px; padding: 0 10px; border: 0; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 12px; white-space: nowrap; text-align: left; justify-content: flex-start; } .mbar button:hover { background: var(--violet-soft); color: var(--violet-ink); } .mbar .own { color: var(--violet-ink); } .fchips { display: flex; gap: 4px; flex-wrap: wrap; min-height: 24px; align-items: center; font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted); } .fchips button { height: 24px; padding: 0 8px; border-radius: 999px; font-size: 12px; background: var(--violet-soft); border-color: var(--violet); color: var(--violet-ink); } #detail[hidden], #toast[hidden], #nudge[hidden] { display: none; } #toast { font: 400 12px/16px 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; color: var(--violet-ink); }</style>
	<div class="app">
		<div class="cfg"><span class="hint">Menu items: the app author picks these, and can add their own</span><span class="chips" id="cfg"></span></div>
		<div class="panel" id="main"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by country · right-click a bar</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div>
		<div class="fchips" id="fchips"></div><div id="bars"></div><div class="mbar" id="mbar" role="menu" hidden></div><div class="hint" id="nudge" hidden>Right-click a bar to open its menu</div></div>
		<div class="panel" id="detail" hidden><div class="ph"><b id="dt"></b><span class="status" id="s2"></span></div><div id="dbody"></div></div>
		<div id="toast" hidden></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Custom right-click menu', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const byCountry = app.createQuery('byCountry', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { country_name: customers.country } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const customers = app.createQuery('customers', { dataset: 'ecommerce', pageSize: 5, aql: 'explore { dimensions { customer_name: customers.name } measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const orders = app.createQuery('orders', { dataset: 'ecommerce', pageSize: 5, aql: 'explore { dimensions { order_id: orders.id, ordered_on: orders.ordered_at, order_status: orders.status } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { ordered_on desc, order_id desc } }' });
// keep only and exclude filter the chart; drill and view orders filter the detail queries
const country = app.createFilter('country', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.country', label: 'Country' });
const point = app.createFilter('point', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.country', label: 'Clicked country' });
app.mapControl(country, byCountry, { field: 'customers.country' });
app.mapControl(point, customers, { field: 'customers.country' });
app.mapControl(point, orders, { field: 'customers.country' });
let kept = null, out = [], view = null, at = null, toast = '';
const run = () => { menu(null); app.execute(); };
const applyCountry = () => { if (kept) country.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [kept] }); else if (out.length) country.setCondition({ operator: 'is_not', values: out }); else country.reset(); };
const detail = (kind, r) => { view = { kind, name: r.country_name }; point.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [r.country_name] }); run(); };
// the menu: each item is a label and what it does with the clicked row
const ITEMS = [
	{ id: 'keep', label: 'Keep only', on: true, act: (r) => { kept = r.country_name; out = []; applyCountry(); run(); } },
	{ id: 'exclude', label: 'Exclude', on: true, act: (r) => { kept = null; out = out.concat(r.country_name); applyCountry(); run(); } },
	{ id: 'drill', label: 'Drill to customers', on: true, act: (r) => detail('customers', r) },
	{ id: 'orders', label: 'View orders', on: true, act: (r) => detail('orders', r) },
	{ id: 'copy', label: 'Copy as AQL filter', on: false, own: true, act: (r) => { const t = "customers.country is '" + r.country_name + "'"; toast = 'Copied: ' + t; (navigator.clipboard ? navigator.clipboard.writeText(t) : Promise.reject()).catch(() => { toast = 'Copy it: ' + t; draw(); }); menu(null); draw(); } },
];
const cfg = K.$('#cfg');
for (const it of ITEMS) { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = (it.own ? '+ ' : '') + it.label; if (it.own) b.className = 'own'; b.onclick = () => { it.on = !it.on; b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(it.on)); menu(null); draw(); }; b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(it.on)); cfg.appendChild(b); }
const mb = K.$('#mbar');
// right-click (or the Menu key / Shift+F10 on a focused bar) opens the menu at the pointer
function menu (r, x, y) {
	at = r; mb.hidden = !r;
	if (!r) return;
	mb.replaceChildren(...ITEMS.filter((it) => it.on).map((it) => { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.setAttribute('role', 'menuitem'); b.textContent = it.label; if (it.own) b.className = 'own'; b.onclick = (e) => { e.stopPropagation(); it.act(r); }; return b; }));
	if (!mb.children.length) mb.innerHTML = '<span class="hint" style="padding: 6px 8px">No menu items: turn some on above</span>';
	const box = K.$('#main').getBoundingClientRect();
	mb.style.left = Math.max(4, Math.min(x - box.left, box.width - mb.offsetWidth - 4)) + 'px';
	mb.style.top = (y - box.top + 2) + 'px';
}
let nudge = 0;
document.addEventListener('click', (e) => { if (at && !mb.contains(e.target)) { menu(null); draw(); } });
document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => { if (e.key === 'Escape' && at) { menu(null); draw(); } });
const dd = (v) => { const x = new Date(String(v).slice(0, 10) + 'T00:00:00Z'); return x.getUTCDate() + ' ' + ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec'][x.getUTCMonth()] + ' ' + String(x.getUTCFullYear()).slice(2); };
function draw () {
	K.status(byCountry, K.$('#s1'));
	const fc = K.$('#fchips');
	fc.innerHTML = kept ? 'Country is ' : out.length ? 'Country is not ' : 'No filter yet';
	for (const v of kept ? [kept] : out) { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = v + ' ×'; b.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Remove ' + v); b.onclick = () => { if (kept) kept = null; else out = out.filter((x) => x !== v); applyCountry(); run(); }; fc.appendChild(b); }
	if (byCountry.result) K.bars(K.$('#bars'), byCountry.result.rows, { label: (r) => r.country_name, value: (r) => r.total_revenue, on: (r) => !!at && r.country_name === at.country_name, pick: () => { if (at) return; nudge = Date.now(); draw(); setTimeout(draw, 1600); } });
	if (byCountry.result) [...K.$('#bars').children].forEach((el, i) => {
		const r = byCountry.result.rows[i];
		const open = (x, y) => { menu(r, x, y); draw(); const first = mb.querySelector('button'); if (first) first.focus(); };
		el.oncontextmenu = (e) => { e.preventDefault(); open(e.clientX, e.clientY); };
		el.onkeydown = (e) => { if (e.key === 'ContextMenu' || (e.shiftKey && e.key === 'F10')) { e.preventDefault(); const b = el.getBoundingClientRect(); open(b.left + 96, b.bottom); } };
	});
	K.$('#nudge').hidden = Date.now() - nudge > 1500;
	const box = K.$('#detail'); box.hidden = !view;
	if (view) {
		const q = view.kind === 'customers' ? customers : orders;
		K.status(q, K.$('#s2'));
		K.$('#dt').textContent = (view.kind === 'customers' ? 'Top customers in ' : 'Latest orders in ') + view.name;
		if (q.result) K.table(K.$('#dbody'), view.kind === 'customers'
			? [{ key: 'customer_name', label: 'Customer' }, { key: 'num_orders', label: 'Orders', num: true }, { key: 'total_revenue', label: 'Revenue', num: true, fmt: (v) => K.money.format(v) }]
			: [{ key: 'order_id', label: 'Order', fmt: (v) => '#' + v }, { key: 'ordered_on', label: 'Date', fmt: dd }, { key: 'order_status', label: 'Status' }, { key: 'total_revenue', label: 'Revenue', num: true, fmt: (v) => K.money.format(v) }], q.result.rows);
	}
	K.$('#toast').hidden = !toast; K.$('#toast').textContent = toast;
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, view ? [byCountry, view.kind === 'customers' ? customers : orders] : [byCountry], () => ['menu → ' + (ITEMS.filter((it) => it.on).map((it) => it.label).join(' · ') || 'empty') + ' (app code)']);
}
app.subscribe(draw);
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Right-click **Germany**: a menu opens at the pointer, with **Keep only**, **Exclude**, **Drill to customers** and **View orders**
2. Click **Exclude**: the chart drops to five countries, and the chip reads **Country is not Germany**
3. In the menu items strip, turn off **Exclude** and turn on **+ Copy as AQL filter**, then right-click **Singapore**: the menu has the new set
4. Click **Germany ×** to clear the filter, right-click **Germany** again and pick **Drill to customers**: Customer 92 leads, at $13,118

## Other Controls patterns

- [Filter mapping](one-control-many.md): Choose which charts a filter changes, so a benchmark chart can stay unfiltered.
- [Parent-child filter](cascading-options.md): Picking a category limits the product list to products in that category.
- [Apply button](apply-button.md): Change several filters, then press Apply to update every chart at once.
- [Cross filter](selection-to-filter.md): Turn a clicked selection into a filter chip, so your next click narrows further.
- [Zoom / pan](zoom-pan.md): Scrolling zooms the picture, and double-clicking reloads that month week by week.
- [Legend visibility](legend-toggle.md): Click a legend item to hide its line, or Alt-click to show only that line.

---

# Cross-filtering

> Click one or more bars, a country on the map or heatmap cells, and other charts show only those.

- Pattern id: `single-select`
- Category: Selections (also Controls)
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#single-select
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader clicks **Singapore**. The other bars dim, and the monthly trend re-queries for Singapore. Each further click adds or removes a country: with **Germany + Japan** picked, the trend shows their combined revenue. A map works the same way: clicking **Australia** re-queries the category mix for Australia. A heatmap cell selects a pair: picking **(Vietnam, Jan)** and **(Japan, Mar)** shows **$21.1k** from exactly those two country-month pairs, not all four combinations.

Why: Clicking a chart is the most natural question a reader can ask. A cell click means "this cell", so the filter keeps each pair.

## What to build

Each click adds or removes a pick; the other charts filter to all picks together, and a grid cell keeps its exact row and column pair.

Layout: Country bars (source) beside a monthly trend (target), country tiles laid out like a map, and a country × month heatmap beside category bars.

Instruction: Let a click on a bar, map shape or grid cell filter the other charts to it, with more clicks adding picks and a second click removing one.

Done when: The other charts show only the picks, a second click removes one, and two grid cells give only their own pairs, not every mix.

On the ecommerce sample: Click Germany, then Japan: the trend shows both combined. In the heatmap, Vietnam under Jan plus Japan under Mar give $21.1k by category, not four combinations.

## AQL

Not run as written: the source is the "Percent of total" query and the target is the trend query.

```aql
// source
explore { dimensions { country: customers.country } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }
// target
explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { period asc } }
```

## SDK wiring

```js
app.mapCrossFilter(byCountry, trend);
// each click adds or removes a row; picks OR together
chart.on('click', (p) => {
  const row = byCountry.result.rows[p.dataIndex];
  const s = byCountry.selectedRows;
  byCountry.select(
    s.includes(row) ? s.filter((r) => r !== row) : [...s, row],
  );
  app.execute();
});
// highlight: byCountry.selectedRows (the source is never filtered
// by its own selection)

// a map is just another renderer for the same source query
map.on('click', (p) => {
  byCountry.select([
    byCountry.result.rows.find((r) => r.country === p.name),
  ]);
  app.execute();
});

// heatmap cells: select the picked rows; anfra filters to
// exactly those country-month pairs (the month comes from a
// date drill, so each cell is a month range)
app.mapCrossFilter(heat, byCategory);
heat.select([vietnamJan, japanMar]);
app.execute();
```

State it touches: Analytical: `app.selection`. Renderer: the dimmed bars.

## Notes

- One edge and one `select()` call. The SDK builds the condition from the row
- The source never filters itself
- The same call works for bars, maps and tables

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<style>
		.heat { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 74px repeat(6, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 2px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; }
		.heat .rl { color: var(--weak); white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; align-self: center; }
		.heat .cl { color: var(--muted); text-align: center; }
		.heat button.cell { height: 28px; padding: 0; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 12px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--ink); }
		.heat button.cell[aria-pressed='true'] { border: 2px solid var(--violet-ink); color: var(--violet-ink); font-weight: 600; }
		.heat.some button.cell[aria-pressed='false'] { opacity: 0.45; }
		#bycat .b { grid-template-columns: 64px minmax(0, 1fr) 52px; }
		#v-bars[hidden], #v-cells[hidden] { display: none; }
		</style>
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Click a</span><span class="seg" id="mode"><button type="button" data-m="bars">Country bar</button><button type="button" data-m="cells">Heatmap cell</button></span><span class="hint" id="hint"></span><button type="button" id="clear" hidden>Clear</button></div>
		<div id="v-bars" class="cols" style="grid-template-columns: 1fr 1.3fr"><div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by country</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="bycountry"></div></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Monthly revenue: <span id="kpi1">–</span></b><span class="status" id="s2"></span></div><div class="hint" id="for">All countries</div><div id="trend"></div></div></div>
		<div id="v-cells" class="cols" style="grid-template-columns: 1.55fr 1fr" hidden><div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue: country × month, 2026</b><span class="status" id="s3"></span></div><div class="heat" id="heat"></div></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>By category</b><span class="status" id="s4"></span></div><div class="kpi" id="kpi">–</div><div class="hint" id="cfor">All cells</div><div id="bycat" style="margin-top:6px"></div></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Cross-filtering', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
// bars: the picked countries cross-filter the trend
const byCountry = app.createQuery('byCountry', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { country_name: customers.country } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const AQL = 'explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { period asc } }';
const trend = app.createQuery('trend', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: AQL });
const all = app.createQuery('allCountries', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: AQL });
app.mapCrossFilter(byCountry, trend);
// a heatmap cell: a country-month pair cross-filters the categories
const heat = app.createQuery('heat', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { country_name: customers.country, period: orders.ordered_at } measures { total_revenue: revenue } filters { orders.ordered_at matches @(2026-01-01 until 2026-07-01) } }' });
const byCategory = app.createQuery('byCategory', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { category_name: products.category } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } filters { orders.ordered_at matches @(2026-01-01 until 2026-07-01) } }' });
const grain = app.createDateDrill('grain', { default: 'month', label: 'Grain' });
app.mapControl(grain, heat, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });
app.mapCrossFilter(heat, byCategory);
let mode = 'bars';
const mon = (v) => new Date(v).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', year: '2-digit', timeZone: 'UTC' });
const mon1 = (v) => new Date(v).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', timeZone: 'UTC' });
const key = (r) => r.country_name + '|' + String(r.period).slice(0, 10);
const HINT = { bars: 'Click countries to add them, click one again to remove it', cells: 'Click cells to pick exact country-month pairs, click again to remove one' };
// one live selection per app, so switching the source clears it
K.$('#mode').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.onclick = () => { if (mode === b.dataset.m) return; mode = b.dataset.m; app.clearSelection(); app.execute(); render(); });
K.$('#clear').onclick = () => { app.clearSelection(); app.execute(); };
function toggle (r) {
	const s = heat.selectedRows; const has = s.some((x) => key(x) === key(r));
	const next = has ? s.filter((x) => key(x) !== key(r)) : [...s, r];
	if (next.length) heat.select(next); else app.clearSelection();
	app.execute();
}
function drawHeat (rows) {
	const el = K.$('#heat'); const sel = new Set(heat.selectedRows.map(key));
	const countries = [...new Set(rows.map((r) => r.country_name))].sort();
	const months = [...new Set(rows.map((r) => String(r.period).slice(0, 10)))].sort();
	const at = new Map(rows.map((r) => [key(r), r]));
	const max = Math.max(...rows.map((r) => Number(r.total_revenue)), 1);
	el.className = 'heat' + (sel.size ? ' some' : '');
	el.replaceChildren();
	const add = (n) => el.appendChild(n);
	const div = (cls, t) => { const d = document.createElement('div'); d.className = cls; d.textContent = t; return d; };
	add(div('cl', ''));
	months.forEach((m) => add(div('cl', mon1(m))));
	countries.forEach((c) => {
		add(div('rl', c));
		months.forEach((m) => {
			const r = at.get(c + '|' + m); const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.className = 'cell';
			if (!r) { b.disabled = true; add(b); return; }
			const v = Number(r.total_revenue); const a = 0.08 + 0.72 * v / max;
			b.style.background = 'rgb(138 81 212 / ' + a.toFixed(2) + ')'; if (a > 0.62) b.style.color = '#fff';
			b.textContent = Math.round(v / 1000) + 'k';
			b.title = c + ', ' + mon1(m) + ' 2026: ' + K.money.format(v);
			b.setAttribute('aria-label', c + ' ' + mon1(m) + ' 2026 ' + K.money.format(v));
			b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(sel.has(key(r))));
			b.onclick = () => toggle(r);
			add(b);
		});
	});
}
// the mode switch redraws on its own: with nothing selected, no query re-runs
function render () {
K.$('#mode').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.dataset.m === mode)));
K.$('#v-bars').hidden = mode !== 'bars'; K.$('#v-cells').hidden = mode !== 'cells';
K.$('#hint').textContent = HINT[mode];
if (mode === 'bars') {
	const names = byCountry.selectedRows.map((r) => r.country_name);
	K.$('#clear').hidden = !names.length;
	K.status(byCountry, K.$('#s1')); K.status(trend, K.$('#s2'));
	if (byCountry.result) K.bars(K.$('#bycountry'), byCountry.result.rows, { label: (r) => r.country_name, value: (r) => r.total_revenue, on: (r) => names.includes(r.country_name),
		pick: (r) => { const s = byCountry.selectedRows; const has = s.some((x) => x.country_name === r.country_name); const next = has ? s.filter((x) => x.country_name !== r.country_name) : [...s, r]; if (next.length) byCountry.select(next); else app.clearSelection(); app.execute(); } });
	K.$('#for').textContent = names.length ? names.join(' + ') : 'All countries';
	const ghost = new Map((all.result?.rows || []).map((r) => [r.period, r.total_revenue]));
	if (trend.result) { K.$('#kpi1').textContent = K.money.format(trend.result.rows.reduce((t, r) => t + Number(r.total_revenue), 0));
		K.columns(K.$('#trend'), trend.result.rows, { label: (r) => mon(r.period), value: (r) => r.total_revenue, ghost: names.length ? (r) => ghost.get(r.period) : null }); }
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [trend]);
} else {
	const s = heat.selectedRows;
	K.$('#clear').hidden = !s.length;
	K.status(heat, K.$('#s3')); K.status(byCategory, K.$('#s4'));
	K.$('#cfor').textContent = s.length ? s.map((r) => '(' + r.country_name + ', ' + mon1(r.period) + ')').join(' OR ') : 'All cells, Jan–Jun 2026';
	if (heat.result) drawHeat(heat.result.rows);
	if (byCategory.result) { K.$('#kpi').textContent = K.money.format(byCategory.result.rows.reduce((t, r) => t + Number(r.total_revenue), 0));
		K.bars(K.$('#bycat'), byCategory.result.rows, { label: (r) => r.category_name, value: (r) => r.total_revenue }); }
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [byCategory]);
}
}
app.subscribe(render);
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Click **Germany** on **Revenue by country**: the other bars dim and **Monthly revenue** re-queries, with all countries in grey behind
2. Click **Japan** to add it: the trend shows Germany + Japan combined
3. Click **Japan** again to remove it, or **Clear** to start over
4. Click **Heatmap cell**, then the **Vietnam** cell under **Jan** and the **Japan** cell under **Mar**
5. Read **By category**: it shows $21.1k from (Vietnam, Jan) OR (Japan, Mar), not all four combinations

## Other Selections patterns

- [Range brushing](range-brush.md): Drag across months on a chart, and other charts show only that period.
- [Histogram brushing](numeric-brush.md): Drag across a range of order sizes, like $1,000 to $2,000.
- [Cross-highlighting](cross-highlight.md): Hover a country, and other charts keep their totals but highlight its share.
- [Multiple cross-filters](two-selections.md): Keep a selection in two charts at once, like Germany in one and Software in the other.
- [Selection cohort](selection-cohort.md): Select some customers and compare what they buy with everyone else.

# Range brushing

> Drag across months on a chart, and other charts show only that period.

- Pattern id: `range-brush`
- Category: Selections (also Dates & time)
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#range-brush
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader drags a brush across **Feb–Apr 2026**. The months inside it become the selection. Revenue in the range is $225k.

Why: Dragging across a period is quicker than typing two dates.

## What to build

Dragging across a time chart marks a period; the KPIs and other charts then count only the rows inside it.

Layout: Monthly columns with a translucent brush, and a KPI that follows.

Instruction: Let readers drag across a time chart to pick a period, and filter the other charts to it.

Done when: The title names the brushed period, the KPIs and other charts match it, and clearing the brush restores the full totals.

On the ecommerce sample: Drag from Feb 26 to Apr 26: the title reads Feb 26 – Apr 26 brushed, and In range shows $225,090 from 263 orders.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count }
  sorts { period asc }
}
```

Reader input the SDK sent:

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "field": "orders.ordered_at",
      "operator": "matches",
      "values": [
        "2026-02-01 - 2026-04-30"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Saved result:

| period | total_revenue | num_orders |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-02-01 | 86602.09 | 87 |
| 2026-03-01 | 61464.65 | 97 |
| 2026-04-01 | 77023.03 | 79 |

The input shows the same range as a date filter. A brushed selection becomes date ranges only when the source chart's month comes from a date drill; with `| month()` in the AQL, the SDK matches exact days and the targets fail to compile (seen live on 15 Oct).

## SDK wiring

```js
app.mapCrossFilter(trend, kpis);
chart.on('brushEnd', (e) => {
  const [a, b] = e.areas[0].coordRange;
  trend.select(trend.result.rows.slice(a, b + 1));
  app.execute();
});
```

State it touches: Analytical: a selection of contiguous rows.

## Notes

- Select the rows under the brush, and the SDK writes the date condition at the applied grain

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<style>
		.bb { position: relative; height: 104px; display: flex; align-items: flex-end; gap: 2px; cursor: crosshair; user-select: none; touch-action: none; }
		.bb .c { flex: 1; min-width: 2px; background: var(--violet); border-radius: 2px 2px 0 0; transition: background-color 160ms var(--ease); pointer-events: none; }
		.bb.some .c:not(.in) { background: var(--violet-faint); }
		.bb .br { position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; background: rgb(138 81 212 / 0.1); border: 1px solid var(--violet); border-radius: 4px; pointer-events: none; }
		.bx { display: flex; gap: 2px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; color: var(--muted); margin-top: 4px; }
		.bx span { flex: 1; min-width: 2px; white-space: nowrap; overflow: visible; }
		#bycat .b { grid-template-columns: 72px minmax(0, 1fr) 52px; }
		</style>
		<div class="row"><span class="hint">Drag across the columns to brush a period, or click one month</span><button type="button" id="clear" hidden>Clear brush</button></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by month<span id="rng"></span></b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div class="bb" id="bb"></div><div class="bx" id="bx"></div></div>
		<div class="cols" style="grid-template-columns: 1fr 1.4fr">
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>In range</b><span class="status" id="s2"></span></div><div class="lbl">Revenue</div><div class="kpi" id="rev">–</div><div class="lbl">Orders</div><div class="kpi" id="ord">–</div></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>By category</b><span class="status" id="s3"></span></div><div id="bycat"></div></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Range brushing', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const trend = app.createQuery('trend', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { period asc } }' });
const kpis = app.createQuery('kpis', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count } }' });
const byCategory = app.createQuery('byCategory', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { category_name: products.category } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const grain = app.createDateDrill('grain', { default: 'month', label: 'Grain' });
app.mapControl(grain, trend, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });
app.mapCrossFilter(trend, kpis);
app.mapCrossFilter(trend, byCategory);
const mon = (v) => new Date(v).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', year: '2-digit', timeZone: 'UTC' });
const box = K.$('#bb');
let drag = null, live = null;
const idx = (e) => { const r = box.getBoundingClientRect(); const n = trend.result.rows.length; return Math.max(0, Math.min(n - 1, Math.floor((e.clientX - r.left) / r.width * n))); };
function drawBrush (a, b) {
	let br = box.querySelector('.br');
	if (a == null) { if (br) br.remove(); return; }
	if (!br) { br = document.createElement('div'); br.className = 'br'; box.appendChild(br); }
	const n = trend.result.rows.length, lo = Math.min(a, b), hi = Math.max(a, b);
	br.style.left = (lo / n * 100) + '%'; br.style.width = ((hi - lo + 1) / n * 100) + '%';
	box.querySelectorAll('.c').forEach((c, i) => c.classList.toggle('in', i >= lo && i <= hi));
	box.classList.add('some');
}
box.onpointerdown = (e) => { if (!trend.result) return; box.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId); const i = idx(e); drag = [i, i]; drawBrush(i, i); };
box.onpointermove = (e) => { if (!drag) return; drag[1] = idx(e); drawBrush(drag[0], drag[1]); };
box.onpointerup = () => { if (!drag) return; const lo = Math.min(...drag), hi = Math.max(...drag); drag = null; live = [lo, hi];
	trend.select(trend.result.rows.slice(lo, hi + 1)); app.execute(); };
K.$('#clear').onclick = () => { live = null; app.clearSelection(); app.execute(); };
app.subscribe(() => {
K.status(trend, K.$('#s1')); K.status(kpis, K.$('#s2')); K.status(byCategory, K.$('#s3'));
const s = trend.selectedRows;
if (!s.length) live = null;
K.$('#clear').hidden = !live;
K.$('#rng').textContent = live && s.length ? ': ' + mon(s[0].period) + (s.length > 1 ? ' – ' + mon(s[s.length - 1].period) : '') + ' brushed' : '';
if (trend.result && !drag) {
	const rows = trend.result.rows, max = Math.max(...rows.map((r) => Number(r.total_revenue)), 1);
	box.className = 'bb';
	box.replaceChildren(...rows.map((r) => { const c = document.createElement('div'); c.className = 'c'; c.style.height = (Number(r.total_revenue) / max * 100) + '%'; c.title = mon(r.period) + ' · ' + K.money.format(r.total_revenue); return c; }));
	K.$('#bx').replaceChildren(...rows.map((r, i) => { const sp = document.createElement('span'); sp.textContent = i % 3 === 0 ? mon(r.period) : ''; return sp; }));
	if (live) drawBrush(live[0], live[1]);
}
const k = kpis.result?.rows[0];
K.$('#rev').textContent = k ? K.money.format(k.total_revenue) : '–';
K.$('#ord').textContent = k ? K.int.format(k.num_orders) : '–';
if (byCategory.result) K.bars(K.$('#bycat'), byCategory.result.rows, { label: (r) => r.category_name, value: (r) => r.total_revenue });
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [kpis, byCategory]);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Drag across **Revenue by month** from **Feb 26** to **Apr 26**
2. Read the title: **Feb 26 – Apr 26 brushed**
3. Read **In range**: revenue is $225,090 from 263 orders
4. Click **Clear brush** to drop the selection

## Other Selections patterns

- [Cross-filtering](single-select.md): Click one or more bars, a country on the map or heatmap cells, and other charts show only those.
- [Histogram brushing](numeric-brush.md): Drag across a range of order sizes, like $1,000 to $2,000.
- [Cross-highlighting](cross-highlight.md): Hover a country, and other charts keep their totals but highlight its share.
- [Multiple cross-filters](two-selections.md): Keep a selection in two charts at once, like Germany in one and Software in the other.
- [Selection cohort](selection-cohort.md): Select some customers and compare what they buy with everyone else.
