# Histogram brushing

> Drag across a range of order sizes, like $1,000 to $2,000.

- Pattern id: `numeric-brush`
- Category: Selections (also Scenarios & analyses)
- Status: Works with app code: anfra supplies the queries, the app adds some logic
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#numeric-brush
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader brushes the order-value histogram from $1,000 to $2,000. The brush becomes a `between` filter on `orders.order_value`, and the category chart shows those 295 orders (between includes both ends, so 10 orders of exactly $2,000 count): $218k of Software, $166k of Services.

Why: Readers often ask about big orders or small baskets.

## What to build

Dragging across the bins sets a value range; every other chart then counts only the rows inside it.

Layout: Order-value histogram ($250 bins) with a brush, and the category chart it filters.

Instruction: Let readers drag across a histogram to pick a range of values, shown as a clearable chip, and filter the other charts to it.

Done when: The brushed range shows as a chip, the other charts' totals match that range, and clearing the chip restores everything.

On the ecommerce sample: Brush $1,000 to $2,000: the chip reads Order value: $1,000 – $2,000, In range shows 295 orders, and Software shows $218k, Services $166k.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { category: products.category }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count }
  sorts { total_revenue desc }
}
```

Reader input the SDK sent:

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "field": "orders.order_value",
      "operator": "between",
      "values": [
        "1000",
        "2000"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Saved result:

| category | total_revenue | num_orders |
|---|---|---|
| Software | 218268.00 | 194 |
| Services | 165500.00 | 134 |
| Hardware | 35133.52 | 151 |
| Parts | 1678.65 | 82 |

`orders.order_value` is now a Dataset dimension (an order's revenue, added to the ecommerce sample for this card), so any query can filter on it. The $250 bins are still declared in the query, and "query-local computed dimensions are skipped when cross-filtering" (AQL.md), so the brush sends a `between` filter rather than a selection.

## SDK wiring

```js
const value = app.createFilter('value', {
  dataset: 'ecommerce',
  field: 'orders.order_value',
});
for (const q of [byCategory, trend])
  app.mapControl(value, q, { field: 'orders.order_value' });
chart.on('brushEnd', (e) => {
  // e.g. 1000, 2000
  const [lo, hi] = binRange(e);
  value.setCondition({
    operator: 'between',
    values: [String(lo), String(hi)],
  });
  app.execute();
});
```

## Notes

- `order_value` lives in the Dataset once, so a brush is one `between` condition every query understands
- Limits: Works with app code: the brush becomes a filter, not a cross-filter selection, because the bins are computed in the query.

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<style>
		.bb { position: relative; height: 104px; display: flex; align-items: flex-end; gap: 2px; cursor: crosshair; user-select: none; touch-action: none; }
		.bb .c { flex: 1; min-width: 2px; background: var(--violet); border-radius: 2px 2px 0 0; pointer-events: none; }
		.bb.some .c:not(.in) { background: var(--violet-faint); }
		.bb .br { position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; background: rgb(138 81 212 / 0.1); border: 1px solid var(--violet); border-radius: 4px; pointer-events: none; }
		.bx { display: flex; gap: 2px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; color: var(--muted); margin-top: 4px; }
		.bx span { flex: 1; min-width: 2px; white-space: nowrap; overflow: visible; }
		#bycat .b { grid-template-columns: 72px minmax(0, 1fr) 52px; }
		</style>
		<div class="row"><span class="hint">Drag across the histogram to pick a range of order values</span><span class="chips"><button type="button" id="chip" aria-pressed="true" hidden></button></span></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Orders by order value, $250 bins<span id="rng"></span></b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div class="bb" id="bb"></div><div class="bx" id="bx"></div></div>
		<div class="cols" style="grid-template-columns: 1fr 1.4fr">
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>In range</b><span class="status" id="s2"></span></div><div class="lbl">Orders</div><div class="kpi" id="ord">–</div><div class="lbl">Revenue</div><div class="kpi" id="rev">–</div><div class="hint" id="edge"></div></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by category</b><span class="status" id="s3"></span></div><div id="bycat"></div></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Histogram brushing', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const hist = app.createQuery('histogram', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'dimension orders.value_bin = floor(orders.order_value / 250) * 250;\nexplore { dimensions { bin_start: orders.value_bin } measures { num_orders: order_count } sorts { bin_start asc } }' });
const kpis = app.createQuery('kpis', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { measures { num_orders: order_count, total_revenue: revenue } }' });
const byCategory = app.createQuery('byCategory', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { category_name: products.category } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const value = app.createFilter('orderValue', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'orders.order_value', label: 'Order value' });
for (const q of [kpis, byCategory]) app.mapControl(value, q, { field: 'orders.order_value' });
const W = 250;
const box = K.$('#bb');
let bins = [], drag = null, live = null;
const usd = (v) => '$' + K.int.format(v);
const idx = (e) => { const r = box.getBoundingClientRect(); return Math.max(0, Math.min(bins.length - 1, Math.floor((e.clientX - r.left) / r.width * bins.length))); };
function drawBrush (a, b) {
	let br = box.querySelector('.br');
	if (a == null) { if (br) br.remove(); return; }
	if (!br) { br = document.createElement('div'); br.className = 'br'; box.appendChild(br); }
	const n = bins.length, lo = Math.min(a, b), hi = Math.max(a, b);
	br.style.left = (lo / n * 100) + '%'; br.style.width = ((hi - lo + 1) / n * 100) + '%';
	box.querySelectorAll('.c').forEach((c, i) => c.classList.toggle('in', i >= lo && i <= hi));
	box.classList.add('some');
}
box.onpointerdown = (e) => { if (!bins.length) return; box.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId); const i = idx(e); drag = [i, i]; drawBrush(i, i); };
box.onpointermove = (e) => { if (!drag) return; drag[1] = idx(e); drawBrush(drag[0], drag[1]); };
box.onpointerup = () => { if (!drag) return; live = [Math.min(...drag), Math.max(...drag)]; drag = null;
	value.setCondition({ operator: 'between', values: [String(bins[live[0]].lo), String(bins[live[1]].lo + W)] }); app.execute(); };
K.$('#chip').onclick = () => { live = null; value.reset(); app.execute(); };
app.subscribe(() => {
K.status(hist, K.$('#s1')); K.status(kpis, K.$('#s2')); K.status(byCategory, K.$('#s3'));
if (hist.result && !drag) {
	const got = new Map(hist.result.rows.map((r) => [Number(r.bin_start), Number(r.num_orders)]));
	const top = Math.max(...got.keys());
	bins = []; for (let lo = 0; lo <= top; lo += W) bins.push({ lo, n: got.get(lo) || 0 });
	const max = Math.max(...bins.map((b) => b.n), 1);
	box.className = 'bb';
	box.replaceChildren(...bins.map((b) => { const c = document.createElement('div'); c.className = 'c'; c.style.height = Math.max(0.5, b.n / max * 100) + '%'; c.title = usd(b.lo) + '–' + usd(b.lo + W) + ' · ' + K.int.format(b.n) + ' orders'; return c; }));
	K.$('#bx').replaceChildren(...bins.map((b, i) => { const sp = document.createElement('span'); sp.textContent = i % 4 === 0 ? usd(b.lo) : ''; return sp; }));
	if (live) drawBrush(live[0], live[1]);
}
const inBins = live ? bins.slice(live[0], live[1] + 1).reduce((t, b) => t + b.n, 0) : 0;
const chip = K.$('#chip'); chip.hidden = !live; chip.textContent = live ? 'Order value: ' + usd(bins[live[0]].lo) + ' – ' + usd(bins[live[1]].lo + W) + '  ×' : '';
K.$('#rng').textContent = live ? ': ' + K.int.format(inBins) + ' orders brushed' : '';
const k = kpis.result?.rows[0];
K.$('#ord').textContent = k ? K.int.format(k.num_orders) : '–';
K.$('#rev').textContent = k ? K.money.format(k.total_revenue) : '–';
const extra = k && live ? Number(k.num_orders) - inBins : 0;
K.$('#edge').textContent = extra > 0 ? 'between includes both ends: ' + extra + ' orders of exactly ' + usd(bins[live[1]].lo + W) + ' count too' : '';
if (byCategory.result) K.bars(K.$('#bycat'), byCategory.result.rows, { label: (r) => r.category_name, value: (r) => r.total_revenue });
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [kpis, byCategory]);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Drag across the histogram from **$1,000** to **$2,000**
2. Read the chip: **Order value: $1,000 – $2,000**, a `between` filter on `orders.order_value`
3. Read **In range**: 295 orders, and the hint says 10 orders of exactly $2,000 count too
4. Read **Revenue by category**: $218k of Software, $166k of Services

## Other Selections patterns

- [Cross-filtering](single-select.md): Click one or more bars, a country on the map or heatmap cells, and other charts show only those.
- [Range brushing](range-brush.md): Drag across months on a chart, and other charts show only that period.
- [Cross-highlighting](cross-highlight.md): Hover a country, and other charts keep their totals but highlight its share.
- [Multiple cross-filters](two-selections.md): Keep a selection in two charts at once, like Germany in one and Software in the other.
- [Selection cohort](selection-cohort.md): Select some customers and compare what they buy with everyone else.

# Cross-highlighting

> Hover a country, and other charts keep their totals but highlight its share.

- Pattern id: `cross-highlight`
- Category: Selections (also Controls)
- Status: Works with app code: anfra supplies the queries, the app adds some logic
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#cross-highlight
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader hovers **Vietnam** (a click keeps it). The category chart keeps the full totals as grey bars and overlays Vietnam's part in violet: $91.5k of Services' $578k.

Why: A filter hides the context. A highlight keeps it, so the reader sees "how much of the whole".

## What to build

Hovering an item overlays its share on the other charts, while their full totals stay visible underneath; a click pins it.

Layout: Category bars with a grey total and a violet overlay for the selection.

Instruction: Make hovering an item in one chart highlight its share in the other charts, keeping their full totals visible; a click keeps the highlight.

Done when: The highlight follows the pointer, each bar keeps its full total with the share on top, and a pinned item stays after the pointer leaves.

On the ecommerce sample: Hover Vietnam: Revenue by category keeps the full totals in grey with Vietnam's part on top, and Services shows $91.5k of $578k.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { category: products.category }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue }
  sorts { total_revenue desc }
}
```

Reader input the SDK sent:

```json
{
  "conditions": [
    {
      "expr": "customers.country == 'Vietnam'"
    }
  ]
}
```

Saved result:

| category | total_revenue |
|---|---|
| Services | 91500.00 |
| Software | 68234.00 |
| Hardware | 23746.62 |
| Parts | 1774.15 |

## SDK wiring

```js
// two copies of the same AQL: one is a cross-filter target, the
// other is not
const catAll = app.createQuery('catAll', {
  dataset: 'ecommerce',
  aql: CAT_AQL,
});
const catSel = app.createQuery('catSel', {
  dataset: 'ecommerce',
  aql: CAT_AQL,
});
// only the overlay follows the selection
app.mapCrossFilter(byCountry, catSel);
// draw catAll as grey bars, catSel on top in the accent colour
```

## Notes

- Same AQL, two declarations, one edge. The highlight is a second query that is mapped
- Limits: Works with app code: two queries. A proposed `mapCrossFilter(from, to, { mode: 'highlight' })` would return both in one result.

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<style>
		.hl { display: grid; gap: 6px; }
		.hl .r { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 64px minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 8px; align-items: center; font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; }
		.hl .t { position: relative; height: 14px; border-radius: 3px; }
		.hl .g, .hl .o { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; bottom: 0; border-radius: 3px; transition: width 320ms var(--ease); }
		.hl .g { background: rgb(24 20 31 / 0.12); }
		.hl .o { background: var(--violet); }
		.hl .v { grid-column: 2; color: var(--weak); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; margin-top: -4px; }
		.hl .v b { color: var(--violet-ink); font-weight: 600; }
		</style>
		<div class="row"><span class="hint">Hover a country to highlight its part of each category. Click to keep it highlighted, click again to let go</span></div>
		<div class="cols" style="grid-template-columns: 1fr 1.15fr"><div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by country</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="bycountry"></div></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by category<span id="for"></span></b><span class="status" id="s2"></span></div><div class="hl" id="cat"></div>
		<div class="legend" style="margin-top:8px"><span><i style="background:rgb(24 20 31 / 0.12)"></i>All countries</span><span><i style="background:var(--violet)"></i><span id="lg">Selected</span></span></div></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Cross-highlighting', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const byCountry = app.createQuery('byCountry', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { country_name: customers.country } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const CAT = 'explore { dimensions { category_name: products.category } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }';
const catAll = app.createQuery('catAll', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: CAT });
const catSel = app.createQuery('catSel', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: CAT });
app.mapCrossFilter(byCountry, catSel);
const kc = (v) => K.compact.format(Number(v));
// hover previews a country, a click pins it; either way it is the selection the overlay query follows
let hovered = null, pinned = null, t = 0;
const apply = () => { clearTimeout(t); t = setTimeout(() => {
	const want = hovered || pinned, now = byCountry.selectedRows[0] || null;
	if ((want && want.country_name) === (now && now.country_name)) return;
	if (want) byCountry.select([want]); else app.clearSelection();
	app.execute();
}, 90); };
K.$('#bycountry').addEventListener('mouseleave', () => { hovered = null; apply(); });
// leaving the app's frame straight from a bar fires no mouseleave on the list
document.addEventListener('mouseout', (e) => { if (!e.relatedTarget) { hovered = null; apply(); } });
window.addEventListener('message', (e) => { if (e.data && e.data.gallery === 'pointer-left') { hovered = null; apply(); } });
K.$('#bycountry').addEventListener('focusout', (e) => { if (!K.$('#bycountry').contains(e.relatedTarget)) { hovered = null; apply(); } });
app.subscribe(() => {
K.status(byCountry, K.$('#s1')); K.status(catSel, K.$('#s2'));
const picked = byCountry.selectedRows[0]?.country_name || null;
if (byCountry.result) {
	const rows = byCountry.result.rows;
	K.bars(K.$('#bycountry'), rows, { label: (r) => r.country_name, value: (r) => r.total_revenue, on: (r) => !!pinned && r.country_name === pinned.country_name,
		pick: (r) => { pinned = pinned && pinned.country_name === r.country_name ? null : r; hovered = null; apply(); } });
	K.$('#bycountry').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b, i) => { const r = rows[i]; if (!r) return; b.onmouseenter = () => { hovered = r; apply(); }; b.onfocus = () => { hovered = r; apply(); }; });
}
K.$('#for').textContent = picked ? ': ' + picked + ' of total' : '';
K.$('#lg').textContent = picked || 'Selected';
if (catAll.result) {
	const sel = new Map((catSel.result?.rows || []).map((r) => [r.category_name, Number(r.total_revenue)]));
	const max = Math.max(...catAll.result.rows.map((r) => Number(r.total_revenue)), 1);
	const el = K.$('#cat');
	el.replaceChildren(...catAll.result.rows.map((r) => {
		const tot = Number(r.total_revenue), part = picked ? (sel.get(r.category_name) || 0) : tot;
		const d = document.createElement('div'); d.className = 'r';
		d.innerHTML = '<span>' + K.esc(r.category_name) + '</span><span class="t"><span class="g" style="width:' + (tot / max * 100) + '%"></span><span class="o" style="width:' + (part / max * 100) + '%"></span></span>'
			+ '<span class="v">' + (picked ? '<b>' + kc(part) + '</b> of ' + kc(tot) + ' · ' + Math.round(part / tot * 100) + '%' : kc(tot)) + '</span>';
		return d;
	}));
}
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [catAll, catSel]);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Hover **Vietnam** on **Revenue by country**
2. Read **Revenue by category**: the grey bars keep the full totals, and Vietnam's part sits on top in violet
3. Read **Services**: $91.5k of $578k
4. Move to another country to compare, or click **Vietnam** to keep it highlighted after the pointer leaves

- [Cross-filtering](single-select.md): Click one or more bars, a country on the map or heatmap cells, and other charts show only those.
- [Range brushing](range-brush.md): Drag across months on a chart, and other charts show only that period.
- [Histogram brushing](numeric-brush.md): Drag across a range of order sizes, like $1,000 to $2,000.

# Multiple cross-filters

> Keep a selection in two charts at once, like Germany in one and Software in the other.

- Pattern id: `two-selections`
- Category: Selections (also Controls)
- Status: Works with app code: anfra supplies the queries, the app adds some logic
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#two-selections
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

A plain click on **Germany** filters the page to Germany. A **Ctrl+click** (Cmd on Mac) on **Software** in another chart adds it: the page shows Germany's Software, $65,236. A plain click anywhere starts over.

Why: Readers expect each chart to keep its pick, the way spreadsheet slicers do. anfra holds one selection per app, so the app turns the earlier pick into a filter.

## What to build

A plain click selects and starts over; a Ctrl or Cmd click on another chart keeps the first pick and adds one.

Layout: Country bars and category bars; the earlier pick stays highlighted while the new one is added.

Instruction: Let readers keep picks in two charts at once with Ctrl+click, so the page shows both together, while a plain click starts over.

Done when: Both picks show as labels, the totals match both picks together, and a plain click anywhere drops back to one pick.

On the ecommerce sample: Click Germany, then Ctrl+click Software: Revenue on this page shows $65,236, with Country: Germany (kept) and Selected: Software.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { category: products.category }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue }
  sorts { total_revenue desc }
}
```

Reader input the SDK sent:

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "field": "customers.country",
      "operator": "is",
      "values": [
        "Germany"
      ]
    },
    {
      "field": "products.category",
      "operator": "is",
      "values": [
        "Software"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Saved result:

| category | total_revenue |
|---|---|
| Software | 65236.00 |

This is what a third chart receives after the Ctrl+click: the kept pick arrives as an ordinary filter (country is Germany) and the new selection as its condition (category is Software). They are ANDed. Checked live on 15 Oct: click Germany $205,890, Ctrl+click Software $65,236, Ctrl+click Services in the same chart $169,236 (Software OR Services), plain click Japan $118,326.

## SDK wiring

```js
// every chart cross-filters the others
for (const [a, b] of [
  [byCountry, byCategory],
  [byCountry, trend],
  [byCategory, byCountry],
  [byCategory, trend],
])
  app.mapCrossFilter(a, b);

// one hidden "kept pick" filter per chart, mapped to every query
// EXCEPT that chart,
// so the chart still shows all its bars and can highlight the kept
// ones
const keep = {
  byCountry: app.createFilter('keepCountry', {
    dataset: 'ecommerce',
    field: 'customers.country',
  }),
  byCategory: app.createFilter('keepCategory', {
    dataset: 'ecommerce',
    field: 'products.category',
  }),
};
for (const q of [byCategory, trend])
  app.mapControl(keep.byCountry, q, { field: 'customers.country' });
for (const q of [byCountry, trend])
  app.mapControl(keep.byCategory, q, {
    field: 'products.category',
  });

function onBarClick(query, row, event) {
  // Ctrl, or Cmd on Mac
  const add = event.ctrlKey || event.metaKey;
  const sel = app.selection;
  // plain click: start over
  if (!add) {
    Object.values(keep).forEach((f) => f.reset());
    query.select([row]);
    // Ctrl+click on another chart: keep the old pick as a filter
  } else if (sel && sel.source !== query.name) {
    keep[sel.source].setCondition({
      operator: 'is',
      values: sel.conditions[0].values,
    });
    query.select([row]);
    // Ctrl+click on the same chart: toggle (OR)
  } else {
    const s = query.selectedRows;
    query.select(
      s.includes(row) ? s.filter((r) => r !== row) : [...s, row],
    );
  }
  app.execute();
}
// highlight kept picks yourself: keep[name].condition.values;
// selectedRows only knows the current selection
```

State it touches: Analytical: one live selection plus one kept-pick filter per chart. Both are ordinary SDK state, so bookmarks and undo work as usual.

## Notes

- Each pick is either the one selection or a kept-pick filter; the SDK ANDs them for every query
- Plain click, Ctrl+click and toggle are about 15 lines of app code
- Limits: Works with app code. Each chart must break down by one field: a two-field chart (a country × month heatmap) sends its selection as one combined expression, which can't be copied into a single filter. An SDK that held named selections itself would remove this bookkeeping (proposed).

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<style>#bycat .b, #bycountry .b { grid-template-columns: 96px minmax(0, 1fr) 54px; } .tag { font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; padding: 4px 10px; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong); } .tag.kept { border-style: dashed; color: var(--violet-ink); border-color: var(--violet); } .tag.sel { background: var(--violet-soft); color: var(--violet-ink); border-color: var(--violet); }</style>
		<div class="row"><span class="hint">Click a bar to start over, Ctrl+click (Cmd) to add to your picks</span><button type="button" id="add" aria-pressed="false" title="Acts like holding Ctrl">Add mode</button><button type="button" id="clear">Clear all</button></div>
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Revenue on this page</span><span class="kpi" id="kpi">–</span><span class="status" id="s3"></span><span class="row" id="tags"></span></div>
		<div class="cols"><div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by country</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="bycountry"></div></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by category</b><span class="status" id="s2"></span></div><div id="bycat"></div></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Multiple cross-filters', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const byCountry = app.createQuery('byCountry', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { country_name: customers.country } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const byCategory = app.createQuery('byCategory', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { category_name: products.category } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const kpi = app.createQuery('kpi', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { measures { total_revenue: revenue } }' });
for (const [a, b] of [[byCountry, byCategory], [byCountry, kpi], [byCategory, byCountry], [byCategory, kpi]]) app.mapCrossFilter(a, b);
const keep = {
	byCountry: app.createFilter('keepCountry', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.country', label: 'Kept country' }),
	byCategory: app.createFilter('keepCategory', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'products.category', label: 'Kept category' }),
};
for (const q of [byCategory, kpi]) app.mapControl(keep.byCountry, q, { field: 'customers.country' });
for (const q of [byCountry, kpi]) app.mapControl(keep.byCategory, q, { field: 'products.category' });
const dim = { byCountry: 'country_name', byCategory: 'category_name' };
let addMode = false;
const kept = (name) => { const c = keep[name].condition; return c && c.values ? c.values.map(String) : []; };
function onBar (q, row, e) {
	const add = addMode || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey;
	const sel = app.selection, d = dim[q.name];
	if (!add) {
		Object.values(keep).forEach((f) => f.reset());
		const only = q.selectedRows.length === 1 && q.selectedRows[0][d] === row[d];
		if (only) app.clearSelection(); else q.select([row]);
	} else if (sel && sel.source !== q.name) {
		keep[sel.source].setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: sel.conditions[0].values });
		const mine = kept(q.name); keep[q.name].reset();
		q.select(q.result.rows.filter((r) => mine.includes(r[d]) || r[d] === row[d]));
	} else {
		const s = q.selectedRows, has = s.some((r) => r[d] === row[d]);
		const next = has ? s.filter((r) => r[d] !== row[d]) : [...s, row];
		if (next.length) q.select(next); else app.clearSelection();
	}
	app.execute();
}
K.$('#add').onclick = () => { addMode = !addMode; K.$('#add').setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(addMode)); };
K.$('#clear').onclick = () => { Object.values(keep).forEach((f) => f.reset()); app.clearSelection(); app.execute(); };
function draw (q, el) {
	if (!q.result) return;
	const d = dim[q.name], sel = q.selectedRows.map((r) => r[d]), k = kept(q.name);
	K.bars(K.$(el), q.result.rows, { label: (r) => r[d] + (k.includes(r[d]) ? ' · kept' : ''), value: (r) => r.total_revenue, on: (r) => sel.includes(r[d]) || k.includes(r[d]), pick: (r, e) => onBar(q, r, e) });
}
app.subscribe(() => {
K.status(byCountry, K.$('#s1')); K.status(byCategory, K.$('#s2')); K.status(kpi, K.$('#s3')); if (/row/.test(K.$('#s3').textContent)) K.$('#s3').textContent = '';
draw(byCountry, '#bycountry'); draw(byCategory, '#bycat');
const k = kpi.result?.rows[0]; K.$('#kpi').textContent = k ? K.money.format(k.total_revenue) : '–';
const tags = [];
for (const [name, lab] of [['byCountry', 'Country'], ['byCategory', 'Category']]) { const v = kept(name); if (v.length) tags.push('<span class="tag kept">' + lab + ': ' + K.esc(v.join(', ')) + ' (kept)</span>'); }
const sel = app.selection; if (sel && sel.rows.length) tags.push('<span class="tag sel">Selected: ' + K.esc(sel.rows.map((r) => r[dim[sel.source]]).join(', ')) + '</span>');
K.$('#tags').innerHTML = tags.join('');
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [kpi, byCountry, byCategory]);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Click **Germany** on **Revenue by country**: the page filters to Germany
2. Hold Ctrl (Cmd on Mac) and click **Software** on **Revenue by category**
3. Read **Revenue on this page**: $65,236, Germany's Software, with **Country: Germany (kept)** and **Selected: Software**
4. Click any bar without Ctrl to start over

## Other Selections patterns

- [Cross-filtering](single-select.md): Click one or more bars, a country on the map or heatmap cells, and other charts show only those.
- [Range brushing](range-brush.md): Drag across months on a chart, and other charts show only that period.
- [Histogram brushing](numeric-brush.md): Drag across a range of order sizes, like $1,000 to $2,000.
- [Cross-highlighting](cross-highlight.md): Hover a country, and other charts keep their totals but highlight its share.
- [Selection cohort](selection-cohort.md): Select some customers and compare what they buy with everyone else.

# Selection cohort

> Select some customers and compare what they buy with everyone else.

- Pattern id: `selection-cohort`
- Category: Selections (also Scenarios & analyses)
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#selection-cohort
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader lassoes customers 1–5 in a table and presses **Make cohort**. Two bar charts compare the cohort's category mix with the rest: 195 other customers.

Why: A "what do these people do differently?" question deserves a comparison, not just a filter.

## What to build

Selecting rows in a table and pressing a button saves them as a cohort; the charts then compare it with everyone else.

Layout: Paired bars: cohort vs rest, by category.

Instruction: Let readers select records in a table, turn them into a cohort, and compare the cohort with everyone else side by side.

Done when: The cohort and the rest are labelled with their counts, together they make up everyone, and Reset clears the cohort.

On the ecommerce sample: Click customers 1 to 5, then Make cohort: Category share of revenue shows Cohort: 5 in violet against Rest: 195 in grey.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { category: products.category }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_customers: count_distinct(orders.customer_id) }
  sorts { total_revenue desc }
}
```

Reader input the SDK sent:

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "field": "customers.id",
      "operator": "is_not",
      "values": [
        "1",
        "2",
        "3",
        "4",
        "5"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Saved result:

| category | total_revenue | num_customers |
|---|---|---|
| Services | 569500.00 | 157 |
| Software | 487238.00 | 187 |
| Hardware | 188234.76 | 193 |
| Parts | 13264.55 | 186 |

IDs travel as strings (`"1"`, not `1`). anfra rejected the JS numbers: "send \"1\", not 1".

## SDK wiring

```js
const inCohort = app.createFilter('inCohort', {
  dataset: 'ecommerce',
  field: 'customers.id',
});
const outCohort = app.createFilter('outCohort', {
  dataset: 'ecommerce',
  field: 'customers.id',
});
app.mapControl(inCohort, cohortMix, { field: 'customers.id' });
app.mapControl(outCohort, restMix, { field: 'customers.id' });
makeBtn.onclick = () => {
  const ids = table.selectedRows.map((r) => r.id); // strings
  inCohort.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: ids });
  outCohort.setCondition({ operator: 'is_not', values: ids });
  app.execute();
};
```

State it touches: Parameter set: a named list of IDs, used by two controls with opposite operators.

## Notes

- The same AQL is declared twice, with two controls on `customers.id` using `is` and `is_not`

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<style>
		.pair { display: grid; gap: 8px; }
		.pair .r { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 60px minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 2px 8px; align-items: center; font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; }
		.pair .r > span:first-child { grid-row: span 2; }
		.pair .ln { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) 96px; gap: 6px; align-items: center; }
		.pair .t { height: 10px; border-radius: 3px; background: var(--sunken); overflow: hidden; }
		.pair .t i { display: block; height: 100%; border-radius: 3px; transition: width 320ms var(--ease); }
		.pair .v { text-align: right; white-space: nowrap; color: var(--weak); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
		#tbl .tw { max-height: 232px; }
		</style>
		<div class="row"><span class="hint">Click customers to pick them, then make them a cohort</span><button type="button" id="make" disabled>Make cohort</button><button type="button" id="reset" hidden>Reset</button></div>
		<div class="cols" style="grid-template-columns: 1fr 1.15fr">
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Customers<span id="npick"></span></b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="tbl"></div></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Category share of revenue</b><span class="status" id="s2"></span></div>
		<div class="legend" style="margin-bottom:8px"><span><i style="background:var(--violet)"></i><span id="lc">Cohort</span></span><span><i style="background:rgb(24 20 31 / 0.3)"></i><span id="lr">Everyone</span></span></div>
		<div class="pair" id="mix"></div></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Selection cohort', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const table = app.createQuery('customers', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { customer_id: customers.id, customer_name: customers.name, country_name: customers.country } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { customer_id asc } }' });
const MIX = 'explore { dimensions { category_name: products.category } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }';
const TOT = 'explore { measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_customers: count_distinct(orders.customer_id) } }';
const cohortMix = app.createQuery('cohortMix', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: MIX });
const restMix = app.createQuery('restMix', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: MIX });
const cohortTot = app.createQuery('cohortTotal', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: TOT });
const restTot = app.createQuery('restTotal', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: TOT });
const inCohort = app.createFilter('inCohort', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.id', label: 'In cohort' });
const outCohort = app.createFilter('outCohort', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.id', label: 'Not in cohort' });
for (const q of [cohortMix, cohortTot]) app.mapControl(inCohort, q, { field: 'customers.id' });
for (const q of [restMix, restTot]) app.mapControl(outCohort, q, { field: 'customers.id' });
let made = false;
const id = (r) => String(r.customer_id);
K.$('#make').onclick = () => {
	const ids = table.selectedRows.map(id);
	inCohort.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: ids });
	outCohort.setCondition({ operator: 'is_not', values: ids });
	made = true; app.execute();
};
K.$('#reset').onclick = () => { inCohort.reset(); outCohort.reset(); app.clearSelection(); made = false; app.execute(); };
function pick (r) {
	const s = table.selectedRows, has = s.some((x) => id(x) === id(r));
	const next = has ? s.filter((x) => id(x) !== id(r)) : [...s, r];
	if (next.length) table.select(next); else app.clearSelection();
	draw();
}
function line (share, val, col) { return '<span class="ln"><span class="t"><i style="width:' + (share * 100).toFixed(1) + '%;background:' + col + '"></i></span><span class="v">' + Math.round(share * 100) + '% · ' + K.compact.format(val) + '</span></span>'; }
function draw () {
	K.status(table, K.$('#s1')); K.status(made ? cohortMix : restMix, K.$('#s2'));
	const picked = new Set(table.selectedRows.map(id));
	if (table.result) K.table(K.$('#tbl'), [{ key: 'customer_id', label: 'ID', num: true }, { key: 'customer_name', label: 'Customer' }, { key: 'country_name', label: 'Country' }], table.result.rows, { on: (r) => picked.has(id(r)), pick });
	K.$('#npick').textContent = picked.size ? ': ' + picked.size + ' picked' : '';
	K.$('#make').disabled = !picked.size; K.$('#reset').hidden = !made;
	const ct = cohortTot.result?.rows[0], rt = restTot.result?.rows[0];
	K.$('#lc').textContent = made && ct ? 'Cohort: ' + K.int.format(ct.num_customers) : 'Cohort';
	K.$('#lr').textContent = made && rt ? 'Rest: ' + K.int.format(rt.num_customers) : 'Everyone';
	K.$('#lc').parentElement.style.display = made ? '' : 'none';
	const rest = restMix.result?.rows || [], coh = cohortMix.result?.rows || [];
	const sum = (rows) => rows.reduce((t, r) => t + Number(r.total_revenue), 0) || 1;
	const cm = new Map(coh.map((r) => [r.category_name, Number(r.total_revenue)])), rs = sum(rest), cs = sum(coh);
	K.$('#mix').innerHTML = rest.map((r) => '<div class="r"><span>' + K.esc(r.category_name) + '</span>'
		+ (made ? line((cm.get(r.category_name) || 0) / cs, cm.get(r.category_name) || 0, 'var(--violet)') : '')
		+ line(Number(r.total_revenue) / rs, Number(r.total_revenue), 'rgb(24 20 31 / 0.3)') + '</div>').join('');
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [cohortMix, restMix]);
}
app.subscribe(draw);
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Click customers 1 to 5 in the **Customers** table
2. Click **Make cohort**
3. Read **Category share of revenue**: **Cohort: 5** in violet against **Rest: 195** in grey
4. Click **Reset** to start over

- [Cross-filtering](single-select.md): Click one or more bars, a country on the map or heatmap cells, and other charts show only those.
- [Range brushing](range-brush.md): Drag across months on a chart, and other charts show only that period.
- [Histogram brushing](numeric-brush.md): Drag across a range of order sizes, like $1,000 to $2,000.
- [Cross-highlighting](cross-highlight.md): Hover a country, and other charts keep their totals but highlight its share.

# Date filter

> Pick exact dates, a range like "last 3 months", or a phrase like "last quarter".

- Pattern id: `date-filter`
- Category: Dates & time
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#date-filter
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

One date chip moves through exact dates (**1 Jan – 30 Jun 2026**), the phrase **last 3 months** (Jul–Sep) and **last 30 days**, which warns that data stops on 23 Sep, so only the days up to then count. Every chart mapped to it redraws. Calendar phrases like "last quarter" work the same way.

Why: People ask for dates in all three ways. They are one control that sends a different condition each time, not three features.

## What to build

One date control takes exact dates, presets or a typed phrase, turns it into a date range, and every mapped chart redraws.

Layout: A date chip with presets above the monthly chart.

Instruction: Add one date filter for the whole page with exact dates, presets and typed phrases, showing the dates each choice means.

Done when: Each choice shows the exact dates it means, every chart follows it, and a warning appears when the data ends early.

On the ecommerce sample: Last 30 days warns that data stops on 23 Sep 2026; typing last q and pressing Tab picks Last quarter: 272 orders, 1 Jul to 30 Sep 2026.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count }
  sorts { period asc }
}
```

Reader input the SDK sent:

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "field": "orders.ordered_at",
      "operator": "last",
      "values": [
        30
      ],
      "modifier": "day"
    }
  ]
}
```

Saved result:

| period | total_revenue | num_orders |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-01 | 13791.92 | 23 |

The AQL never changes; only the condition the SDK sends does. All three ran on ecommerce: `between` (runs 08 and 35), `last 30 day` (above, run 07b), `matches 'last 3 months'` (run 07) and `matches 'this year'` (run 07c). In fixed AQL the same ranges are literals: `@(2026-01-01 - 2026-06-30)`, `@(last 3 months)`, `@(last quarter)`.

## SDK wiring

```js
const range = app.createFilter('range', {
  type: 'date',
  label: 'Dates',
});
for (const q of [kpis, trend, table])
  app.mapControl(range, q, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });

// exact dates
range.setCondition({
  operator: 'between',
  values: ['2026-01-01', '2026-06-30'],
});
// relative
range.setCondition({
  operator: 'last',
  values: [30],
  modifier: 'day',
});
// calendar phrase
range.setCondition({
  operator: 'matches',
  values: ['last quarter'],
});
app.execute();
```

## Notes

- One control, three conditions. The server understands phrases like `last quarter` in the app's time zone
- In fixed AQL they are literals: `@(last quarter)`

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<style>.warn { color: #8a4b00; } .rng { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } input[type=date] { width: 140px; }
	.typein { position: relative; display: inline-block; }
	.typein input { width: 200px; padding-right: 30px; background: transparent; position: relative; z-index: 1; }
	.typein .clear { position: absolute; right: 4px; top: 4px; z-index: 2; width: 24px; height: 24px; padding: 0; border: 0; border-radius: 6px; background: none; color: var(--muted); font-size: 16px; line-height: 24px; cursor: pointer; }
	.typein .clear:hover { background: var(--sunken); color: var(--ink); }
	.typein .ghost { position: absolute; left: 11px; top: 0; height: 32px; line-height: 32px; font-size: 14px; color: var(--muted); white-space: pre; pointer-events: none; z-index: 0; }
	.typein .ghost i { font-style: normal; visibility: hidden; }
	.typein .bg { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: #fff; border-radius: 10px; z-index: 0; }
	.sugg { position: absolute; right: 0; top: 36px; z-index: 5; width: 280px; margin: 0; padding: 4px; list-style: none; background: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 10px; box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgb(24 20 31 / 0.12); }
	.sugg li { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 8px; padding: 6px 8px; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px; cursor: pointer; }
	.sugg li .r { color: var(--muted); font-size: 12px; white-space: nowrap; }
	.sugg li[aria-selected=true] { background: var(--violet-faint); color: var(--violet-ink); }
	.sugg li b { font-weight: 600; }
	.snap { animation: snap 420ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); }
	@keyframes snap { 0% { box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 var(--violet-soft); } 40% { box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px var(--violet-soft); } 100% { box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 transparent; } }
	@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .snap { animation: none; } }</style>
	<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><span class="chips" id="presets"></span></div>
		<div class="row"><input type="date" id="from" aria-label="From" value="2026-01-01"><span class="hint">to</span><input type="date" id="to" aria-label="To" value="2026-06-30"><span class="typein"><span class="bg"></span><span class="ghost" id="ghost" aria-hidden="true"></span><input type="text" id="phrase" aria-label="Date phrase" placeholder="or type: last quarter" autocomplete="off" spellcheck="false" role="combobox" aria-autocomplete="both" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="sugg"><button type="button" class="clear" id="clear" aria-label="Clear the date phrase" title="Clear" hidden>×</button><ul class="sugg" id="sugg" role="listbox" aria-label="Date phrases" hidden></ul></span></div>
		<div class="hint rng" id="resolved"></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue <span id="kpi">–</span> · <span id="n">–</span> orders</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="trend"></div>
		<div class="legend"><span><i style="background:var(--violet)"></i>In the range</span><span><i style="background:rgb(24 20 31 / 0.07)"></i>All dates</span></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Date filter', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const AQL = 'explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() } measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count } sorts { period asc } }';
const trend = app.createQuery('trend', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: AQL });
const all = app.createQuery('allDates', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: AQL });
const anchor = app.createQuery('dataEnd', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { measures { latest: orders | max(orders.ordered_at) } }' });
const range = app.createFilter('range', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'orders.ordered_at', label: 'Dates' });
app.mapControl(range, trend, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });
const P = [
	{ k: 'h1', t: '1 Jan – 30 Jun 2026', c: { operator: 'between', values: ['2026-01-01', '2026-06-30'] } },
	{ k: 'l3m', t: 'Last 3 months', c: { operator: 'matches', values: ['last 3 months'] } },
	{ k: 'l30', t: 'Last 30 days', c: { operator: 'last', values: [30], modifier: 'day' } },
	{ k: 'ty', t: 'This year', c: { operator: 'matches', values: ['this year'] } },
	{ k: 'lq', t: 'Last quarter', c: { operator: 'matches', values: ['last quarter'] } },
];
let cur = 'h1';
const iso = (x) => x.toISOString().slice(0, 10);
const D = (s) => new Date(s + 'T00:00:00Z');
const MN = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec'];
const day = (s, y) => { const x = D(s); return x.getUTCDate() + ' ' + MN[x.getUTCMonth()] + (y === false ? '' : ' ' + x.getUTCFullYear()); };
const now = new Date(); const Y = now.getUTCFullYear(), M = now.getUTCMonth();
const ymd = (y, m, d) => iso(new Date(Date.UTC(y, m, d)));
const today = ymd(Y, M, now.getUTCDate());
function resolve (c) {
	if (!c) return null;
	if (c.operator === 'between') return c.values;
	if (c.operator === 'last') return [ymd(Y, M, now.getUTCDate() - c.values[0]), ymd(Y, M, now.getUTCDate() - 1)];
	const p = String(c.values[0]).trim().toLowerCase();
	if (p === 'last 3 months') return [ymd(Y, M - 3, 1), ymd(Y, M, 0)];
	if (p === 'this year') return [ymd(Y, 0, 1), ymd(Y, 11, 31)];
	if (p === 'last quarter') { const q = Math.floor(M / 3) * 3; return [ymd(Y, q - 3, 1), ymd(Y, q, 0)]; }
	if (p === 'this month') return [ymd(Y, M, 1), ymd(Y, M + 1, 0)];
	if (p === 'last month') return [ymd(Y, M - 1, 1), ymd(Y, M, 0)];
	if (p === 'last year') return [ymd(Y - 1, 0, 1), ymd(Y - 1, 11, 31)];
	if (p === 'year to date') return [ymd(Y, 0, 1), today];
	let m = p.match(/^last (\d+) months$/);
	if (m) return [ymd(Y, M - Number(m[1]), 1), ymd(Y, M, 0)];
	m = p.match(/^last (\d+) days$/);
	if (m) return [ymd(Y, M, now.getUTCDate() - Number(m[1])), ymd(Y, M, now.getUTCDate() - 1)];
	m = p.match(/^q([1-4]) (\d{4})$/);
	if (m) return [ymd(Number(m[2]), (m[1] - 1) * 3, 1), ymd(Number(m[2]), m[1] * 3, 0)];
	m = p.match(/^(\d{4})$/);
	if (m) return [m[1] + '-01-01', m[1] + '-12-31'];
	return null;
}
const seg = K.$('#presets'), from = K.$('#from'), to = K.$('#to'), phrase = K.$('#phrase');
function choose (k, c) {
	cur = k;
	if (c) range.setCondition(c); else range.reset();
	app.execute();
}
for (const p of P) { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = p.t; b.dataset.k = p.k; b.onclick = () => { const ex = p.c.operator === 'between'; from.value = ex ? p.c.values[0] : ''; to.value = ex ? p.c.values[1] : ''; phrase.value = ''; typed = ''; snapped = ''; choose(p.k, p.c); }; seg.appendChild(b); }
const exact = () => { if (from.value && to.value) { phrase.value = ''; choose(from.value === '2026-01-01' && to.value === '2026-06-30' ? 'h1' : 'exact', { operator: 'between', values: [from.value, to.value] }); } };
from.onchange = exact; to.onchange = exact;
// the type-in: phrases anfra resolves; typing completes inline, and a phrase that is also a chip snaps to it
const PH = ['last month', 'last quarter', 'last 3 months', 'last 6 months', 'last 12 months', 'last 30 days', 'this year', 'year to date', 'last year', 'Q2 2026', '2026'];
const REDUCED = matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;
const ghost = K.$('#ghost'), sugg = K.$('#sugg');
let typed = '', snapped = '', pick = 0, list = [];
const cs = getComputedStyle(phrase);
Object.assign(ghost.style, { font: cs.font, letterSpacing: cs.letterSpacing, left: (parseFloat(cs.paddingLeft) + parseFloat(cs.borderLeftWidth)) + 'px', lineHeight: phrase.offsetHeight + 'px', height: phrase.offsetHeight + 'px' });
const norm = (v) => v.toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, ' ').replace(/^(past|previous|prev) /, 'last ').replace(/^ytd$/, 'year to date').replace(/^q([1-4])$/, 'q$1 2026');
const span = (p) => { const r = resolve({ operator: 'matches', values: [p] }); return r ? day(r[0], r[0].slice(0, 4) !== r[1].slice(0, 4)) + ' – ' + day(r[1]) : ''; };
function matchesFor (v) {
	const n = norm(v.trimStart());
	if (!n) return PH.slice();
	const starts = PH.filter((p) => p.toLowerCase().startsWith(n));
	return starts.concat(PH.filter((p) => !starts.includes(p) && p.toLowerCase().includes(n)));
}
function drawList () {
	sugg.hidden = !list.length || document.activeElement !== phrase;
	phrase.setAttribute('aria-expanded', String(!sugg.hidden));
	sugg.innerHTML = '';
	list.forEach((p, i) => {
		const li = document.createElement('li');
		li.id = 'opt' + i; li.setAttribute('role', 'option'); li.setAttribute('aria-selected', String(i === pick));
		const n = norm(phrase.value.trimStart()), at = n ? p.toLowerCase().indexOf(n) : -1;
		li.innerHTML = '<span>' + (at >= 0 ? K.esc(p.slice(0, at)) + '<b>' + K.esc(p.slice(at, at + n.length)) + '</b>' + K.esc(p.slice(at + n.length)) : K.esc(p)) + '</span><span class="r">' + K.esc(span(p)) + '</span>';
		li.onmousedown = (e) => { e.preventDefault(); accept(p); };
		sugg.appendChild(li);
	});
	if (!sugg.hidden) phrase.setAttribute('aria-activedescendant', 'opt' + pick); else phrase.removeAttribute('aria-activedescendant');
}
// inline completion: the rest of the first phrase that starts with what was typed, in grey
function drawGhost () {
	const v = phrase.value, p = list[pick];
	const ok = v && p && p.toLowerCase().startsWith(norm(v)) && norm(v) === v.toLowerCase();
	ghost.innerHTML = ok ? '<i>' + K.esc(v) + '</i>' + K.esc(p.slice(v.length)) : '';
}
phrase.oninput = () => { typed = phrase.value; list = matchesFor(phrase.value); pick = 0; drawList(); drawGhost(); };
phrase.onfocus = () => { stopHint(); list = matchesFor(phrase.value); drawList(); drawGhost(); };
phrase.onblur = () => { sugg.hidden = true; phrase.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false'); ghost.innerHTML = ''; startHint(); };
phrase.onkeydown = (e) => {
	if (e.key === 'ArrowDown' || e.key === 'ArrowUp') { if (!list.length) return; e.preventDefault(); pick = (pick + (e.key === 'ArrowDown' ? 1 : list.length - 1)) % list.length; drawList(); drawGhost(); return; }
	if ((e.key === 'Tab' || e.key === 'ArrowRight') && ghost.textContent && phrase.selectionStart === phrase.value.length) { e.preventDefault(); accept(list[pick]); return; }
	if (e.key === 'Enter') { e.preventDefault(); const v = phrase.value.trim(); if (list.length && (!v || norm(v) !== v.toLowerCase() || list[pick].toLowerCase().startsWith(norm(v)) || list[pick].toLowerCase().includes(norm(v)))) accept(list[pick]); else apply(v); return; }
	if (e.key === 'Escape') { sugg.hidden = true; ghost.innerHTML = ''; }
};
// snap: the rest of the phrase types itself in, the box pulses, and a matching chip takes over
function accept (p) {
	if (!p) return;
	typed = phrase.value || typed;
	const start = phrase.value.toLowerCase() && p.toLowerCase().startsWith(phrase.value.toLowerCase()) ? phrase.value.length : 0;
	ghost.innerHTML = ''; sugg.hidden = true;
	const done = () => { phrase.value = p; syncClear(); apply(p); pulse(phrase.parentElement); };
	if (REDUCED) { done(); return; }
	let i = start;
	const step = () => { i++; phrase.value = p.slice(0, i); if (i < p.length) setTimeout(step, 16); else done(); };
	if (start >= p.length) done(); else { phrase.value = p.slice(0, start); step(); }
}
function pulse (el) { el.classList.remove('snap'); void el.offsetWidth; el.classList.add('snap'); }
function apply (v) {
	from.value = ''; to.value = '';
	if (!v) { snapped = ''; choose('all', null); return; }
	snapped = v;
	const chip = P.find((x) => x.t.toLowerCase() === v.toLowerCase());
	if (chip) { choose(chip.k, chip.c); requestAnimationFrame(() => pulse(seg.querySelector('[data-k="' + chip.k + '"]'))); }
	else choose('phrase', { operator: 'matches', values: [v] });
}
phrase.onchange = null;
// × empties the box and drops the phrase, so every order counts again
const clearBtn = K.$('#clear');
const syncClear = () => { clearBtn.hidden = !phrase.value; };
clearBtn.onmousedown = (e) => e.preventDefault();
clearBtn.onclick = () => { phrase.value = ''; typed = ''; ghost.innerHTML = ''; syncClear(); if (cur === 'phrase' || P.some((x) => x.k === cur && x.t.toLowerCase() === snapped.toLowerCase())) apply(''); phrase.focus(); };
phrase.addEventListener('input', syncClear);
// while the box is empty, its placeholder types out a few of the phrases
let hintT = null, hintI = 0;
function startHint () {
	if (REDUCED || phrase.value || hintT) return;
	const run = () => {
		const p = PH[hintI++ % PH.length];
		let i = 0;
		const type = () => { i++; phrase.placeholder = 'or type: ' + p.slice(0, i); if (i < p.length) hintT = setTimeout(type, 45); else hintT = setTimeout(run, 1800); };
		type();
	};
	hintT = setTimeout(run, 1200);
}
function stopHint () { clearTimeout(hintT); hintT = null; phrase.placeholder = 'or type: last quarter'; }
startHint();
range.setCondition(P[0].c);
const mon = (v) => new Date(v).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', year: '2-digit', timeZone: 'UTC' });
app.subscribe(() => {
syncClear();
K.status(trend, K.$('#s1'));
seg.querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.dataset.k === cur)));
const ac = range.appliedCondition;
const c = ac && ac.operator && ac.values && ac.values.length ? ac : null;
const r = resolve(c);
const end = anchor.result ? String(anchor.result.rows[0].latest).slice(0, 10) : null;
let txt = !c ? 'Every order: no date condition' : r ? 'Resolved: ' + day(r[0], r[0].slice(0, 4) !== r[1].slice(0, 4)) + ' – ' + day(r[1]) : 'anfra resolved "' + c.values[0] + '" on the server, in the app time zone (UTC)';
let warn = '';
if (end && c && (r ? r[1] > end : (/^(last|this|today|yesterday|past)/i.test(String(c.values[0])) && today > end))) warn = 'Data stops on ' + day(end) + ', so only days up to then count';
K.$('#resolved').innerHTML = K.esc(txt) + (warn ? ' · <span class="warn">⚠ ' + K.esc(warn) + '</span>' : '');
if (!trend.result) return;
const rows = trend.result.rows;
K.$('#kpi').textContent = K.money.format(rows.reduce((t, x) => t + Number(x.total_revenue), 0));
K.$('#n').textContent = K.int.format(rows.reduce((t, x) => t + Number(x.num_orders), 0));
const got = new Map(rows.map((x) => [x.period, x.total_revenue]));
const base = all.result ? all.result.rows : rows;
K.columns(K.$('#trend'), base, { label: (x) => mon(x.period), value: (x) => got.get(x.period) || 0, ghost: (x) => x.total_revenue });
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [trend], () => [c && c.modifier ? 'modifier: ' + c.modifier + ' (last ' + c.values[0] + ' ' + c.modifier + 's)' : '', snapped && typed && typed.toLowerCase() !== snapped.toLowerCase() ? 'typed "' + typed + '" → snapped to "' + snapped + '"' : '']);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read the chart: the **1 Jan – 30 Jun 2026** chip is on, with exact dates
2. Click **Last 3 months**: the range moves to Jul–Sep
3. Click **Last 30 days**: a warning says data stops on 23 Sep 2026, so only days up to then count
4. Type **last q** in the **or type: last quarter** box, then press Tab to accept the grey **uarter**
5. Read the chart: **Last quarter** lights up, with 272 orders from 1 Jul to 30 Sep 2026

- [Date drill](date-drill.md): Switch the time detail between day, week, month and quarter, or click a period to see it in more detail.
- [Fiscal calendar](fiscal-calendar.md): Report by a fiscal year that starts in July instead of January.
- [As-of anchor](as-of-anchor.md): Count "last 30 days" back from the newest data instead of from today.
- [Incomplete periods](partial-period.md): Mark a month that isn't over yet, so its short bar doesn't look like a drop.
- [Period comparison](period-compare.md): Show each month next to the month before and the same month last year.
- [Custom period comparison](custom-compare.md): Compare any two date ranges side by side, like H1 2026 and H2 2025.
- [Period to date & trailing period](to-date.md): Show a year-to-date total and a rolling 3-month total for each month.

# Date drill

> Switch the time detail between day, week, month and quarter, or click a period to see it in more detail.

- Pattern id: `date-drill`
- Category: Dates & time (also Drilling, Tables & calculations)
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#date-drill
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader switches **Month → Quarter**, and 16 bars become 6. Then they click **Q2 2026**: the range narrows to April–June and the grain steps down to month.

Why: The right level of time detail depends on the question, and time is the hierarchy every reader already knows.

## What to build

Clicking a period swaps the time grain one level finer and keeps that period as a filter.

Layout: A grain switch above a column chart that rebuckets, then drills into the clicked quarter.

Instruction: Let the reader switch the time detail of the chart and click a period to zoom into it, with a way back out.

Done when: The finer periods add up to the period clicked, and a breadcrumb takes the reader back up.

On the ecommerce sample: Switching to Quarter turns 16 month bars into 6; clicking Q2 2026 shows only April to June by month, and All dates returns every month.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count }
  sorts { period asc }
}
```

Reader input the SDK sent:

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "field": "orders.ordered_at",
      "operator": "between",
      "values": [
        "2026-01-01",
        "2026-12-31"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "dateDrills": [
    {
      "field": "orders.ordered_at",
      "grain": "quarter"
    }
  ]
}
```

Saved result:

| period | total_revenue | num_orders |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-01-01 | 230676.95 | 291 |
| 2026-04-01 | 263475.80 | 289 |
| 2026-07-01 | 233648.41 | 272 |

The input shows the quarter grain within 2026. Run 08 drilled September 2026 to weeks: weeks start on Monday, so the first bucket (31 Aug) holds only 1–6 Sep.

## SDK wiring

```js
const grain = app.createDateDrill('grain', { default: 'month' });
// the field, not the alias
app.mapControl(grain, trend, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });
grainButtons.onclick = (e) => {
  grain.setGrain(e.target.value);
  app.execute();
};

// click a period to drill into it: narrow the range, step the grain
// down
chart.on('click', (p) => {
  const start = trend.result.rows[p.dataIndex].period;
  range.setCondition({
    operator: 'between',
    values: [start, endOf(start, currentGrain)],
  });
  grain.setGrain(nextFiner[currentGrain]);
  app.execute();
});
```

## Notes

- One date drill rebuckets every dimension built on `orders.ordered_at`
- The row key stays `period`, so the renderer doesn't change
- Drilling in is two controls, a range and a grain, applied in one run

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Grain</span><span class="seg" id="grains"></span><button type="button" id="up" hidden>↑ All dates</button></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by <span id="g">month</span><span id="range"></span></b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="trend"></div>
		<div class="hint">Click a column to drill into that period</div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Date drill', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const trend = app.createQuery('trend', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { period asc } }' });
const grain = app.createDateDrill('grain', { default: 'month', label: 'Grain' });
const range = app.createFilter('range', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'orders.ordered_at', label: 'Dates' });
app.mapControl(grain, trend, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });
app.mapControl(range, trend, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });
const G = ['year', 'quarter', 'month', 'week', 'day'];
let g = 'month', label = '';
const d = (v) => new Date(v);
const fmt = (v, k = g) => { const x = d(v); return k === 'year' ? String(x.getUTCFullYear()) : k === 'quarter' ? 'Q' + (Math.floor(x.getUTCMonth() / 3) + 1) + ' ' + x.getUTCFullYear() : k === 'month' ? x.toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', year: 'numeric', timeZone: 'UTC' }) : x.toLocaleDateString('en-US', { day: 'numeric', month: 'short', year: 'numeric', timeZone: 'UTC' }); };
const iso = (x) => x.toISOString().slice(0, 10);
function end (start, k) { const x = new Date(start); if (k === 'year') x.setUTCFullYear(x.getUTCFullYear() + 1); else if (k === 'quarter') x.setUTCMonth(x.getUTCMonth() + 3); else if (k === 'month') x.setUTCMonth(x.getUTCMonth() + 1); else if (k === 'week') x.setUTCDate(x.getUTCDate() + 7); else x.setUTCDate(x.getUTCDate() + 1); x.setUTCDate(x.getUTCDate() - 1); return x; }
const setGrain = (k) => { g = k; grain.setGrain(k); };
const seg = K.$('#grains');
for (const x of G) { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = x[0].toUpperCase() + x.slice(1); b.dataset.g = x; b.onclick = () => { setGrain(x); app.execute(); }; seg.appendChild(b); }
K.$('#up').onclick = () => { range.reset(); label = ''; setGrain('month'); app.execute(); };
app.subscribe(() => {
K.status(trend, K.$('#s1'));
seg.querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.dataset.g === g)));
K.$('#g').textContent = g; K.$('#range').textContent = label ? ' in ' + label : ''; K.$('#up').hidden = !label;
const next = G[G.indexOf(g) + 1];
if (trend.result) K.columns(K.$('#trend'), trend.result.rows, { label: (r) => fmt(r.period), value: (r) => r.total_revenue,
	pick: next ? (r) => { const s = d(r.period); label = fmt(r.period); range.setCondition({ operator: 'between', values: [iso(s), iso(end(s, g))] }); setGrain(next); app.execute(); } : null });
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [trend]);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Click **Quarter** next to **Grain**: the 16 month bars become 6 quarter bars
2. Click the **Q2 2026** column: the range narrows to April–June and the grain steps down to **Month**
3. Click **↑ All dates** to go back to every month

# Fiscal calendar

> Report by a fiscal year that starts in July instead of January.

- Pattern id: `fiscal-calendar`
- Category: Dates & time
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#fiscal-calendar
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader picks **Fiscal (July start)**. The quarters relabel: Jul–Sep 2026 becomes **FY27 Q1** at $234k.

Why: Finance teams report in fiscal periods, and calendar quarters confuse them.

## What to build

Switching to Fiscal regroups dates by a year that starts in a chosen month, and period labels change to match.

Layout: Quarter columns that relabel from calendar to fiscal.

Instruction: Let the reader switch the chart between calendar periods and our fiscal periods.

Done when: Each period keeps the same months and total under its new fiscal label, and the toggle switches back cleanly.

On the ecommerce sample: On Calendar, Jul to Sep 2026 reads Q3 2026 at $234k; after picking Fiscal (July start) it reads FY27 Q1 at the same $234k.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { fiscal_year: orders.fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter: orders.fiscal_quarter }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue }
  sorts { fiscal_year asc, fiscal_quarter asc }
}
```

Saved result:

| fiscal_year | fiscal_quarter | total_revenue |
|---|---|---|
| 2025 | 4 | 97537.24 |
| 2026 | 1 | 231777.15 |
| 2026 | 2 | 225937.40 |
| 2026 | 3 | 230676.95 |
| 2026 | 4 | 263475.80 |
| 2027 | 1 | 233648.41 |

`orders.fiscal_year` and `orders.fiscal_quarter` are defined once in `models/ecommerce/orders.model.aml` (added for this card), so every query and every reader can use them. A date drill still can't regrain them, so the toggle switches between two queries; a fiscal-aware date drill is proposed.

## SDK wiring

```js
// two declared queries, calendar and fiscal; the toggle picks which
// one to show
const calQ = app.createQuery('cal', {
  dataset: 'ecommerce',
  aql: CALENDAR_AQL,
});
const fyQ = app.createQuery('fy', {
  dataset: 'ecommerce',
  aql: FISCAL_AQL,
});
for (const q of [calQ, fyQ])
  app.mapControl(country, q, { field: 'customers.country' });
toggle.onchange = () =>
  show(toggle.value === 'fiscal' ? fyQ : calQ);
```

## Notes

- Fiscal year and quarter are model fields: one definition, used by name everywhere

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<style>
	.qr { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 64px 96px minmax(0, 1fr) 52px; gap: 8px; align-items: center; height: 26px; padding: 0 4px; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; }
	.qr .m { color: var(--muted); } .qr .v { text-align: right; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--weak); }
	.qr .t { height: 14px; border-radius: 3px; background: var(--sunken); overflow: hidden; }
	.qr .f { display: block; height: 100%; background: var(--violet-faint); border-radius: 3px; transition: width 320ms var(--ease); }
	.qr.on { background: var(--violet-soft); } .qr.on .f { background: var(--violet); } .qr.on b { color: var(--violet-ink); }
	.qr b { font-weight: 600; }
	</style>
	<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Quarters</span><span class="seg" id="mode"><button type="button" data-m="cal">Calendar</button><button type="button" data-m="fy">Fiscal (July start)</button></span>
		<label class="lbl" for="country">Country</label><select id="country"><option value="">All countries</option></select></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by <span id="what">calendar quarter</span></b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="qs"></div>
		<div class="hint" id="note"></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Fiscal calendar', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const cal = app.createQuery('calendarQuarters', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | quarter() } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { period asc } }' });
const fy = app.createQuery('fiscalQuarters', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { fy: orders.fiscal_year, fq: orders.fiscal_quarter } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { fy asc, fq asc } }' });
const country = app.createFilter('country', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.country', label: 'Country' });
for (const q of [cal, fy]) app.mapControl(country, q, { field: 'customers.country' });
const sel = K.$('#country');
country.loadOptions().then((vals) => vals.forEach((v) => sel.add(new Option(v, v))));
sel.onchange = () => { if (sel.value) country.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [sel.value] }); else country.reset(); app.execute(); };
let mode = 'cal';
K.$('#mode').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => { b.onclick = () => { mode = b.dataset.m; draw(); }; });
const MN = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec'];
const FIRST = 2025 * 12 + 5;
function months (y, m0) { const a = Math.max(y * 12 + m0, FIRST), b = y * 12 + m0 + 2; const s = (k) => MN[k % 12]; return a === b ? s(a) + ' ' + Math.floor(a / 12) : s(a) + '–' + s(b) + ' ' + Math.floor(b / 12); }
function rows () {
	if (mode === 'cal') return cal.result ? cal.result.rows.map((r) => { const d = new Date(r.period), y = d.getUTCFullYear(), m = d.getUTCMonth(); return { k: 'Q' + (m / 3 + 1) + ' ' + y, m: months(y, m), v: Number(r.total_revenue), y, m0: m }; }) : null;
	return fy.result ? fy.result.rows.map((r) => { const Y = Number(r.fy), q = Number(r.fq), y = Y - 1 + Math.floor((6 + (q - 1) * 3) / 12), m = (6 + (q - 1) * 3) % 12; return { k: 'FY' + String(Y).slice(2) + ' Q' + q, m: months(y, m), v: Number(r.total_revenue), y, m0: m }; }) : null;
}
function draw () {
	const q = mode === 'cal' ? cal : fy;
	K.status(q, K.$('#s1'));
	K.$('#mode').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.dataset.m === mode)));
	K.$('#what').textContent = mode === 'cal' ? 'calendar quarter' : 'fiscal quarter (FY ends 30 Jun)';
	const rs = rows();
	if (rs) {
		const max = Math.max(1, ...rs.map((r) => r.v));
		const box = K.$('#qs'); box.innerHTML = '';
		for (const r of rs) {
			const d = document.createElement('div'); const on = r.y === 2026 && r.m0 === 6;
			d.className = 'qr' + (on ? ' on' : '');
			d.innerHTML = '<b>' + K.esc(r.k) + '</b><span class="m">' + K.esc(r.m) + '</span><span class="t"><span class="f" style="width:0"></span></span><span class="v">' + K.compact.format(r.v) + '</span>';
			box.appendChild(d);
			requestAnimationFrame(() => { d.querySelector('.f').style.width = (r.v / max * 100) + '%'; });
		}
		const j = rs.find((r) => r.y === 2026 && r.m0 === 6);
		K.$('#note').textContent = j ? 'Jul–Sep 2026 is ' + j.k + ' at ' + K.compact.format(j.v) + (mode === 'cal' ? '; switch to Fiscal to see it relabel' : ', the first quarter of fiscal 2027') : '';
	}
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [q], () => ['showing ' + q.name + ' (toggle picks the query; renderer state)']);
}
app.subscribe(draw);
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read the **Calendar** quarters: Jul–Sep 2026 is **Q3 2026** at $234k
2. Click **Fiscal (July start)**: the quarters relabel
3. Read the highlighted row: Jul–Sep 2026 is now **FY27 Q1** at $234k
