# As-of anchor

> Count "last 30 days" back from the newest data instead of from today.

- Pattern id: `as-of-anchor`
- Category: Dates & time
- Status: Works with app code: anfra supplies the queries, the app adds some logic
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#as-of-anchor
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

An anchor query finds the newest order: **23 Sep 2026**. "Last 30 days" now means 25 Aug–23 Sep, and a chip shows the anchor.

Why: With batch data, "today" is often after the newest data, and relative ranges come back empty.

## What to build

The page looks up the newest date in the data and counts relative ranges, like last 30 days, back from it.

Layout: Anchor chip, then range chips that resolve against it.

Instruction: Count relative date ranges back from the newest data instead of today, and show the as-of date.

Done when: Every day in the range has data, the range ends on the newest date, and a chip shows that as-of date.

On the ecommerce sample: With Newest order, a chip reads As of 23 Sep 2026, Last 30 days covers 25 Aug to 23 Sep, and every day has data.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore { measures { latest: orders | max(orders.ordered_at), earliest: orders | min(orders.ordered_at) } }
```

Saved result:

| latest | earliest |
|---|---|
| 2026-09-23 | 2025-06-01 |

The `bi-apps/drill.html` app in this repo already does this: it runs a `maxTime` query and works out its ranges from it.

## SDK wiring

```js
const anchor = app.createQuery('anchor', {
  dataset: 'ecommerce',
  aql: `
    explore {
      measures { latest: orders | max(orders.ordered_at) }
    }
  `,
});
await app.execute();
// '2026-09-23'
const end = anchor.result.rows[0].latest;
range.setCondition({
  operator: 'between',
  values: [minusDays(end, 29), end],
});
await app.execute();
```

## Notes

- One tiny anchor query, then ordinary `between` conditions
- Limits: Works with app code. A proposed AQL phrase such as `@(last 30 days as of latest)` would make it one line.

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<style>.anc[hidden] { display: none; } .anc { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; height: 24px; padding: 0 8px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--violet-soft); color: var(--violet-ink); font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; } .warn { color: #8a4b00; }</style>
	<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Count back from</span><span class="seg" id="mode"><button type="button" data-m="today">Today</button><button type="button" data-m="anchor">Newest order</button></span><span class="anc" id="chip" hidden></span></div>
		<div class="row"><span class="chips" id="ranges"></span><span class="hint" id="resolved"></span></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue <span id="kpi">–</span> · <span id="n">–</span> orders</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="days"></div>
		<div class="hint" id="note"></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'As-of anchor', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const anchor = app.createQuery('anchor', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { measures { latest: orders | max(orders.ordered_at) } }' });
const daily = app.createQuery('daily', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { day: orders.ordered_at } measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count } sorts { day asc } }' });
const range = app.createFilter('range', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'orders.ordered_at', label: 'Dates' });
app.mapControl(range, daily, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });
let mode = 'today', N = 30;
const MN = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec'];
const D = (s) => new Date(String(s).slice(0, 10) + 'T00:00:00Z');
const iso = (x) => x.toISOString().slice(0, 10);
const add = (s, n) => { const x = D(s); x.setUTCDate(x.getUTCDate() + n); return iso(x); };
const day = (s, y) => { const x = D(s); return x.getUTCDate() + ' ' + MN[x.getUTCMonth()] + (y === false ? '' : ' ' + x.getUTCFullYear()); };
const today = iso(new Date());
const latest = () => anchor.result ? String(anchor.result.rows[0].latest).slice(0, 10) : null;
// the dates each choice covers: anfra's 'last N day' ends yesterday; the anchored range ends on the newest order
const span = () => mode === 'today' ? [add(today, -N), add(today, -1)] : [add(latest(), -(N - 1)), latest()];
function apply () {
	if (mode === 'today') range.setCondition({ operator: 'last', values: [N], modifier: 'day' });
	else if (latest()) { const s = span(); range.setCondition({ operator: 'between', values: s }); }
	app.execute();
}
K.$('#mode').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => { b.onclick = () => { mode = b.dataset.m; apply(); }; });
const rs = K.$('#ranges');
for (const n of [7, 30, 90]) { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = 'Last ' + n + ' days'; b.dataset.n = n; b.onclick = () => { N = n; apply(); }; rs.appendChild(b); }
const sameY = (a, b) => a.slice(0, 4) === b.slice(0, 4);
app.subscribe(() => {
K.status(daily, K.$('#s1'));
K.$('#mode').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.dataset.m === mode)));
rs.querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(Number(b.dataset.n) === N)));
const L = latest();
K.$('#mode').children[0].textContent = 'Today · ' + day(today, false);
K.$('#mode').children[1].textContent = L ? 'Newest order · ' + day(L, false) : 'Newest order';
K.$('#chip').hidden = mode !== 'anchor' || !L; K.$('#chip').textContent = L ? '⚓ As of ' + day(L) : '';
if (mode === 'anchor' && !L) return;
const s = span();
K.$('#resolved').textContent = s[0] && s[1] ? day(s[0], !sameY(s[0], s[1])) + ' – ' + day(s[1]) : '';
if (!daily.result) return;
const got = new Map(daily.result.rows.map((r) => [String(r.day).slice(0, 10), r]));
const rows = []; for (let d = s[0]; d <= s[1]; d = add(d, 1)) rows.push({ d, r: got.get(d) });
const rev = daily.result.rows.reduce((t, r) => t + Number(r.total_revenue), 0), n = daily.result.rows.reduce((t, r) => t + Number(r.num_orders), 0);
K.$('#kpi').textContent = K.money.format(rev); K.$('#n').textContent = K.int.format(n);
K.columns(K.$('#days'), rows, { label: (x) => day(x.d), value: (x) => x.r ? x.r.total_revenue : 0 });
const empty = L && s[1] > L ? Math.round((D(s[1]) - D(L > s[0] ? L : add(s[0], -1))) / 864e5) : 0;
K.$('#note').innerHTML = empty ? '<span class="warn">⚠ ' + empty + ' of ' + N + ' days come after the newest order (' + K.esc(day(L)) + '), so they are empty</span>' : 'App code: the range ends on the newest order, so no day is past the data';
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [daily], () => [mode === 'anchor' ? 'anchor ← max(orders.ordered_at) = ' + L + ' (app code turns it into between)' : (range.appliedCondition && range.appliedCondition.modifier ? 'modifier: day · anfra counts back from today' : '')]);
});
apply();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read the chart on **Today** with **Last 30 days**: some of the 30 days come after the newest order, so they are empty
2. Click **Newest order**: the anchor query finds 23 Sep 2026 and a chip shows **⚓ As of 23 Sep 2026**
3. Read the range next to the chips: 25 Aug – 23 Sep 2026, 30 days that all have data
4. Click **Last 7 days** or **Last 90 days**: each range still ends on 23 Sep

# Incomplete periods

> Mark a month that isn't over yet, so its short bar doesn't look like a drop.

- Pattern id: `partial-period`
- Category: Dates & time
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#partial-period
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The chart adds `last_order_day` to each month. September 2026 ends on the 23rd, so its bar is hatched and labelled "23 of 30 days".

Why: A short final bar looks like a collapse. Most false alarms on dashboards start here.

## What to build

The page checks the last date with data in each period and marks periods that end early as incomplete.

Layout: Columns with the last bar hatched and a footnote.

Instruction: Mark periods that aren't complete yet, so a partial period doesn't read as a drop.

Done when: Only the unfinished period is marked, its note says how many days it has, and complete periods look normal.

On the ecommerce sample: The Sep 2026 bar is hatched with a note of 23 of 30 days, and turning off Mark incomplete periods makes it read as a drop.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() }
  measures {
    total_revenue: revenue,
    last_order_day: orders | max(orders.ordered_at),
    days_with_orders: orders | count_distinct(orders.ordered_at),
  }
  sorts { period asc }
}
```

Saved result:

| period | total_revenue | last_order_day | days_with_orders |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-06-01 | 97537.24 | 2025-06-30 | 29 |
| 2025-07-01 | 66278.66 | 2025-07-31 | 27 |
| 2025-08-01 | 70722.63 | 2025-08-31 | 28 |
| 2025-09-01 | 94775.86 | 2025-09-30 | 30 |
| 2025-10-01 | 85563.86 | 2025-10-31 | 31 |
| 2025-11-01 | 74836.51 | 2025-11-29 | 28 |
| 2025-12-01 | 65537.03 | 2025-12-31 | 30 |
| 2026-01-01 | 82610.21 | 2026-01-31 | 31 |
| 2026-02-01 | 86602.09 | 2026-02-28 | 26 |
| 2026-03-01 | 61464.65 | 2026-03-30 | 30 |
| 2026-04-01 | 77023.03 | 2026-04-30 | 27 |
| 2026-05-01 | 88378.49 | 2026-05-31 | 31 |

(4 more rows)

## SDK wiring

```js
trend.subscribe(() => {
  for (const r of trend.result?.rows ?? [])
    r._partial = r.last_order_day < endOfMonth(r.period);
});
```

## Notes

- One extra measure. The app compares it with the end of the period

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<style>.cb { position: relative; } .cbc { display: flex; align-items: flex-end; height: 100%; } .cbw { flex: 1; min-width: 2px; height: 100%; position: relative; padding: 0; border: 0; border-radius: 0; background: none; display: block; } .cbw.click { cursor: pointer; } .cbw.click:hover .cbb { background: var(--violet-ink); } .cbb { position: absolute; left: 1px; right: 1px; bottom: 0; background: var(--violet); border-radius: 2px 2px 0 0; transition: height 320ms var(--ease); } .cbw.on .cbb { background: var(--violet-ink); } .cbw.hatch .cbb { background: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, var(--violet) 0 3px, #fff 3px 6px); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--violet); } .cb svg { position: absolute; inset: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; pointer-events: none; overflow: visible; } .cbd { position: absolute; width: 6px; height: 6px; margin: 0 0 -3px -3px; border-radius: 50%; pointer-events: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1.5px #fff; }  .fn { font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; color: var(--weak); } .fn i { display: inline-block; width: 10px; height: 10px; vertical-align: -1px; margin-right: 4px; background: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, var(--violet) 0 2px, #fff 2px 4px); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--violet); }</style>
	<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Grain</span><span class="seg" id="grains"></span><button type="button" id="mark" aria-pressed="true">Mark incomplete periods</button></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by <span id="g">month</span></b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="trend"></div>
		<div class="fn" id="fn"></div></div>
		<div class="hint">last_order_day = max(orders.ordered_at) per period; app code compares it with the period end</div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Incomplete periods', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const trend = app.createQuery('trend', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at } measures { total_revenue: revenue, last_order_day: orders | max(orders.ordered_at) } sorts { period asc } }' });
const grain = app.createDateDrill('grain', { default: 'month', label: 'Grain' });
app.mapControl(grain, trend, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });
function combo (el, rows, o) {
	const n = rows.length, vals = rows.map((r) => Number(o.value(r)) || 0), ls = o.lines || [];
	let max = Math.max(1, ...vals);
	for (const l of ls) for (const r of rows) { const v = l.value(r); if (v != null && isFinite(Number(v))) max = Math.max(max, Number(v)); }
	el.innerHTML = '<div class="cb" style="height:' + (o.height || 150) + 'px"><div class="cbc"></div><svg viewBox="0 0 ' + Math.max(n, 1) + ' 100" preserveAspectRatio="none"></svg></div><div class="axis"><span></span><span></span></div>';
	const box = el.querySelector('.cbc'), svg = el.querySelector('svg'), wrap = el.querySelector('.cb');
	let tip = document.querySelector('.tip'); if (!tip) { tip = document.createElement('div'); tip.className = 'tip'; document.body.appendChild(tip); }
	rows.forEach((r, i) => {
		const c = document.createElement(o.pick ? 'button' : 'div');
		c.className = 'cbw' + (o.hatch && o.hatch(r) ? ' hatch' : '') + (o.on && o.on(r) ? ' on' : '') + (o.pick ? ' click' : '');
		if (o.pick) { c.type = 'button'; c.setAttribute('aria-label', o.label(r)); c.onclick = () => { tip.style.opacity = 0; o.pick(r); }; }
		c.innerHTML = '<span class="cbb" style="height:' + Math.max(0.5, vals[i] / max * 100) + '%"></span>';
		c.onmousemove = (e) => { tip.textContent = o.tip ? o.tip(r) : o.label(r); tip.style.left = Math.max(4, Math.min(e.clientX + 10, innerWidth - tip.offsetWidth - 4)) + 'px'; tip.style.top = (e.clientY - 30) + 'px'; tip.style.opacity = 1; };
		c.onmouseleave = () => { tip.style.opacity = 0; };
		box.appendChild(c);
	});
	for (const l of ls) {
		let seg = [];
		const flush = () => { if (seg.length > 1) { const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'polyline'); p.setAttribute('points', seg.join(' ')); p.setAttribute('fill', 'none'); p.setAttribute('stroke', l.color); p.setAttribute('stroke-width', '2'); p.setAttribute('vector-effect', 'non-scaling-stroke'); if (l.dash) p.setAttribute('stroke-dasharray', '5 3'); svg.appendChild(p); } seg = []; };
		rows.forEach((r, i) => {
			const v = l.value(r);
			if (v == null || !isFinite(Number(v))) { flush(); return; }
			seg.push((i + 0.5) + ',' + (100 - Number(v) / max * 100));
			const d = document.createElement('span'); d.className = 'cbd'; d.style.background = l.color; d.style.left = ((i + 0.5) / n * 100) + '%'; d.style.bottom = (Number(v) / max * 100) + '%'; wrap.appendChild(d);
		});
		flush();
	}
	const ax = el.querySelectorAll('.axis span');
	ax[0].textContent = n ? o.label(rows[0]) : ''; ax[1].textContent = n > 1 ? o.label(rows[n - 1]) : '';
}
let g = 'month', mark = true;
const MN = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec'];
const D = (s) => new Date(String(s).slice(0, 10) + 'T00:00:00Z');
const day = (s) => { const x = D(s); return x.getUTCDate() + ' ' + MN[x.getUTCMonth()] + ' ' + x.getUTCFullYear(); };
const lab = (s) => { const x = D(s); return g === 'quarter' ? 'Q' + (Math.floor(x.getUTCMonth() / 3) + 1) + ' ' + x.getUTCFullYear() : g === 'month' ? MN[x.getUTCMonth()] + ' ' + x.getUTCFullYear() : 'Week of ' + day(s); };
function endOf (s) { const x = D(s); if (g === 'quarter') x.setUTCMonth(x.getUTCMonth() + 3); else if (g === 'month') x.setUTCMonth(x.getUTCMonth() + 1); else x.setUTCDate(x.getUTCDate() + 7); x.setUTCDate(x.getUTCDate() - 1); return x; }
const days = (a, b) => Math.round((b - a) / 864e5) + 1;
const seg = K.$('#grains');
for (const x of ['quarter', 'month', 'week']) { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = x[0].toUpperCase() + x.slice(1); b.dataset.g = x; b.onclick = () => { g = x; grain.setGrain(x); app.execute(); }; seg.appendChild(b); }
K.$('#mark').onclick = () => { mark = !mark; draw(); };
function draw () {
	K.status(trend, K.$('#s1'));
	seg.querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.dataset.g === g)));
	K.$('#mark').setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(mark));
	K.$('#g').textContent = g;
	if (trend.result && trend.result.rows.length) {
		const rows = trend.result.rows, last = rows[rows.length - 1];
		const lastDay = D(last.last_order_day), end = endOf(last.period);
		const partial = lastDay < end;
		const isP = (r) => mark && partial && r === last;
		combo(K.$('#trend'), rows, { label: (r) => lab(r.period), value: (r) => r.total_revenue, hatch: isP,
			tip: (r) => lab(r.period) + ' · ' + K.compact.format(Number(r.total_revenue)) + ' · last order ' + day(r.last_order_day) });
		if (partial && mark) {
			const had = days(D(last.period), lastDay), all = days(D(last.period), end);
			K.$('#fn').innerHTML = '<i></i>' + K.esc(lab(last.period) + ': ' + had + ' of ' + all + ' days, data through ' + day(last.last_order_day).slice(0, -5) + ' · on pace for ' + K.compact.format(Number(last.total_revenue) / had * all));
		} else K.$('#fn').textContent = partial ? 'Marking is off: the last bar reads as a drop' : 'Every period is complete';
	}
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [trend], () => ['hatching: ' + (mark ? 'on' : 'off') + ' (renderer state)']);
}
app.subscribe(draw);
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read the last bar, **Sep 2026**: it is hatched
2. Read the note under the chart: Sep 2026 has 23 of 30 days, data through 23 Sep
3. Click **Mark incomplete periods** to turn it off: the last bar now reads as a drop
4. Click **Quarter** next to **Grain**: the last quarter is marked the same way

## Other Dates & time patterns

- [Date filter](date-filter.md): Pick exact dates, a range like "last 3 months", or a phrase like "last quarter".
- [Date drill](date-drill.md): Switch the time detail between day, week, month and quarter, or click a period to see it in more detail.
- [Fiscal calendar](fiscal-calendar.md): Report by a fiscal year that starts in July instead of January.
- [As-of anchor](as-of-anchor.md): Count "last 30 days" back from the newest data instead of from today.
- [Period comparison](period-compare.md): Show each month next to the month before and the same month last year.
- [Custom period comparison](custom-compare.md): Compare any two date ranges side by side, like H1 2026 and H2 2025.
- [Period to date & trailing period](to-date.md): Show a year-to-date total and a rolling 3-month total for each month.

---

# Period comparison

> Show each month next to the month before and the same month last year.

- Pattern id: `period-compare`
- Category: Dates & time
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#period-compare
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader turns on **Compare: previous month** and **same month last year**. Lines appear over the bars. Sep 2026 shows −26% month on month and −31% year on year.

Why: A number means little without something to compare it with.

## What to build

Each toggle adds a line for the same measure shifted back one period or one year, with the percent change per period.

Layout: Columns (this period) with a dark line (previous month) and a green line (last year).

Instruction: Let the reader overlay the previous period and the same period last year, with the % change.

Done when: For any period, the line shows the earlier period's value, and the percent change matches those two numbers.

On the ecommerce sample: With both toggles on, Sep 2026 shows −26% against Aug 2026 and −31% against Sep 2025.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
metric revenue_prev_month = revenue | relative_period(orders.ordered_at, interval(-1 month));
metric revenue_prev_year = revenue | relative_period(orders.ordered_at, interval(-1 year));
explore {
  dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() }
  measures {
    total_revenue: revenue,
    prev_month: revenue_prev_month,
    prev_year: revenue_prev_year,
    mom_pct: (revenue - revenue_prev_month) * 100.0 / revenue_prev_month,
  }
  filters { orders.ordered_at matches @(2026-01-01 - 2026-09-30) }
  sorts { period asc }
}
```

Saved result:

| period | total_revenue | prev_month | prev_year | mom_pct |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-01-01 | 82610.21 | 65537.03 |  | 26.051195789616955 |
| 2026-02-01 | 86602.09 | 82610.21 |  | 4.832187207852394 |
| 2026-03-01 | 61464.65 | 86602.09 |  | -29.02636645374263 |
| 2026-04-01 | 77023.03 | 61464.65 |  | 25.312728535833198 |
| 2026-05-01 | 88378.49 | 77023.03 |  | 14.742941169673538 |
| 2026-06-01 | 98074.28 | 88378.49 | 97537.24 | 10.970757703599597 |
| 2026-07-01 | 78472.43 | 98074.28 | 66278.66 | -19.98673862301105 |
| 2026-08-01 | 89336.28 | 78472.43 | 70722.63 | 13.844161573689002 |
| 2026-09-01 | 65839.70 | 89336.28 | 94775.86 | -26.301274241551138 |

The `transform_pop_*` control operators fail on anfra, which is documented in API.md. Comparisons go in the AQL. The filter limits the base months, and `relative_period` still reads Dec 2025 for January's comparison.

## SDK wiring

```js
// toggles pick which measures to draw; one query returns all of
// them
compareMonth.onchange = () =>
  chart.setOption(
    series(trend.result, { prevMonth: compareMonth.checked }),
  );
```

State it touches: Renderer: which comparison lines are shown. Analytical: the comparison measures in the AQL.

## Notes

- `revenue | relative_period(orders.ordered_at, interval(-1 year))`, one line per comparison

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<style>.cb { position: relative; } .cbc { display: flex; align-items: flex-end; height: 100%; } .cbw { flex: 1; min-width: 2px; height: 100%; position: relative; padding: 0; border: 0; border-radius: 0; background: none; display: block; } .cbw.click { cursor: pointer; } .cbw.click:hover .cbb { background: var(--violet-ink); } .cbb { position: absolute; left: 1px; right: 1px; bottom: 0; background: var(--violet); border-radius: 2px 2px 0 0; transition: height 320ms var(--ease); } .cbw.on .cbb { background: var(--violet-ink); } .cbw.hatch .cbb { background: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, var(--violet) 0 3px, #fff 3px 6px); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--violet); } .cb svg { position: absolute; inset: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; pointer-events: none; overflow: visible; } .cbd { position: absolute; width: 6px; height: 6px; margin: 0 0 -3px -3px; border-radius: 50%; pointer-events: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1.5px #fff; }  .ro { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 8px; margin-top: 8px; } .ro div { font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; color: var(--muted); } .ro b { display: block; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px; color: var(--ink); font-weight: 600; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .up { color: #1f7a4d; } .dn { color: #b42318; } .sw { display: inline-block; width: 12px; height: 2px; vertical-align: 3px; margin-right: 4px; }</style>
	<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Compare</span><span class="chips"><button type="button" id="pm" aria-pressed="false"><span class="sw" style="background:var(--ink)"></span>vs previous month</button><button type="button" id="py" aria-pressed="false"><span class="sw" style="background:#1f8a5b"></span>vs same month last year</button></span>
		<select id="country" aria-label="Country"><option value="">All countries</option></select></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue 2026 by month</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="trend"></div>
		<div class="ro" id="ro"></div></div>
		<div class="hint">Click a month to read it. The AQL's relative_period measures hold both comparisons; the toggles only draw them</div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Period comparison', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const AQL = 'metric revenue_prev_month = revenue | relative_period(orders.ordered_at, interval(-1 month));\nmetric revenue_prev_year = revenue | relative_period(orders.ordered_at, interval(-1 year));\nexplore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() } measures { total_revenue: revenue, prev_month: revenue_prev_month, prev_year: revenue_prev_year } filters { orders.ordered_at matches @(2026-01-01 - 2026-09-30) } sorts { period asc } }';
const trend = app.createQuery('trend', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: AQL });
const country = app.createFilter('country', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.country', label: 'Country' });
app.mapControl(country, trend, { field: 'customers.country' });
const sel = K.$('#country');
country.loadOptions().then((vals) => vals.forEach((v) => sel.add(new Option(v, v))));
sel.onchange = () => { if (sel.value) country.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [sel.value] }); else country.reset(); app.execute(); };
function combo (el, rows, o) {
	const n = rows.length, vals = rows.map((r) => Number(o.value(r)) || 0), ls = o.lines || [];
	let max = Math.max(1, ...vals);
	for (const l of ls) for (const r of rows) { const v = l.value(r); if (v != null && isFinite(Number(v))) max = Math.max(max, Number(v)); }
	el.innerHTML = '<div class="cb" style="height:' + (o.height || 150) + 'px"><div class="cbc"></div><svg viewBox="0 0 ' + Math.max(n, 1) + ' 100" preserveAspectRatio="none"></svg></div><div class="axis"><span></span><span></span></div>';
	const box = el.querySelector('.cbc'), svg = el.querySelector('svg'), wrap = el.querySelector('.cb');
	let tip = document.querySelector('.tip'); if (!tip) { tip = document.createElement('div'); tip.className = 'tip'; document.body.appendChild(tip); }
	rows.forEach((r, i) => {
		const c = document.createElement(o.pick ? 'button' : 'div');
		c.className = 'cbw' + (o.hatch && o.hatch(r) ? ' hatch' : '') + (o.on && o.on(r) ? ' on' : '') + (o.pick ? ' click' : '');
		if (o.pick) { c.type = 'button'; c.setAttribute('aria-label', o.label(r)); c.onclick = () => { tip.style.opacity = 0; o.pick(r); }; }
		c.innerHTML = '<span class="cbb" style="height:' + Math.max(0.5, vals[i] / max * 100) + '%"></span>';
		c.onmousemove = (e) => { tip.textContent = o.tip ? o.tip(r) : o.label(r); tip.style.left = Math.max(4, Math.min(e.clientX + 10, innerWidth - tip.offsetWidth - 4)) + 'px'; tip.style.top = (e.clientY - 30) + 'px'; tip.style.opacity = 1; };
		c.onmouseleave = () => { tip.style.opacity = 0; };
		box.appendChild(c);
	});
	for (const l of ls) {
		let seg = [];
		const flush = () => { if (seg.length > 1) { const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'polyline'); p.setAttribute('points', seg.join(' ')); p.setAttribute('fill', 'none'); p.setAttribute('stroke', l.color); p.setAttribute('stroke-width', '2'); p.setAttribute('vector-effect', 'non-scaling-stroke'); if (l.dash) p.setAttribute('stroke-dasharray', '5 3'); svg.appendChild(p); } seg = []; };
		rows.forEach((r, i) => {
			const v = l.value(r);
			if (v == null || !isFinite(Number(v))) { flush(); return; }
			seg.push((i + 0.5) + ',' + (100 - Number(v) / max * 100));
			const d = document.createElement('span'); d.className = 'cbd'; d.style.background = l.color; d.style.left = ((i + 0.5) / n * 100) + '%'; d.style.bottom = (Number(v) / max * 100) + '%'; wrap.appendChild(d);
		});
		flush();
	}
	const ax = el.querySelectorAll('.axis span');
	ax[0].textContent = n ? o.label(rows[0]) : ''; ax[1].textContent = n > 1 ? o.label(rows[n - 1]) : '';
}
let pm = false, py = false, pick = null;
const MN = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec'];
const lab = (v, dy) => { const x = new Date(v); return MN[(x.getUTCMonth() + 12 + (dy === 'm' ? -1 : 0)) % 12] + ' ' + (x.getUTCFullYear() - (dy === 'y' || (dy === 'm' && x.getUTCMonth() === 0) ? 1 : 0)); };
const num = (v) => v == null ? null : Number(v);
const pct = (a, b) => b == null || !b ? null : (a - b) / b * 100;
const chg = (p) => p == null ? '<span class="hint">no data</span>' : '<span class="' + (p >= 0 ? 'up' : 'dn') + '">' + (p >= 0 ? '+' : '−') + Math.abs(p).toFixed(0) + '%</span>';
K.$('#pm').onclick = () => { pm = !pm; draw(); };
K.$('#py').onclick = () => { py = !py; draw(); };
function draw () {
	K.status(trend, K.$('#s1'));
	K.$('#pm').setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(pm)); K.$('#py').setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(py));
	if (trend.result && trend.result.rows.length) {
		const rows = trend.result.rows;
		const r = rows.find((x) => x.period === pick) || rows[rows.length - 1];
		combo(K.$('#trend'), rows, { label: (x) => lab(x.period), value: (x) => x.total_revenue, on: (x) => x === r, pick: (x) => { pick = x.period; draw(); },
			lines: [pm ? { value: (x) => num(x.prev_month), color: 'var(--ink)', dash: true } : null, py ? { value: (x) => num(x.prev_year), color: '#1f8a5b' } : null].filter(Boolean),
			tip: (x) => lab(x.period) + ' · ' + K.compact.format(Number(x.total_revenue)) + (pm && x.prev_month != null ? ' · prev ' + K.compact.format(Number(x.prev_month)) : '') + (py && x.prev_year != null ? ' · last year ' + K.compact.format(Number(x.prev_year)) : '') });
		const v = Number(r.total_revenue);
		K.$('#ro').innerHTML = '<div>' + K.esc(lab(r.period)) + '<b>' + K.compact.format(v) + '</b></div>'
			+ '<div>vs ' + K.esc(lab(r.period, 'm')) + (pm ? '' : ' (off)') + '<b>' + (pm ? (r.prev_month == null ? '–' : K.compact.format(Number(r.prev_month))) + ' ' + chg(pct(v, num(r.prev_month))) : '–') + '</b></div>'
			+ '<div>vs ' + K.esc(lab(r.period, 'y')) + (py ? '' : ' (off)') + '<b>' + (py ? (r.prev_year == null ? '–' : K.compact.format(Number(r.prev_year))) + ' ' + chg(pct(v, num(r.prev_year))) : '–') + '</b></div>';
	}
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [trend], () => ['lines: ' + ([pm ? 'previous month' : '', py ? 'last year' : ''].filter(Boolean).join(', ') || 'none') + ' (renderer state)']);
}
app.subscribe(draw);
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Click **vs previous month**: a dashed line for the month before appears over the bars
2. Click **vs same month last year**: a green line for last year appears
3. Read the numbers under the chart for **Sep 2026**: −26% vs Aug 2026 and −31% vs Sep 2025
4. Click another month to read its two changes

- [Date filter](date-filter.md): Pick exact dates, a range like "last 3 months", or a phrase like "last quarter".
- [Date drill](date-drill.md): Switch the time detail between day, week, month and quarter, or click a period to see it in more detail.
- [Fiscal calendar](fiscal-calendar.md): Report by a fiscal year that starts in July instead of January.
- [As-of anchor](as-of-anchor.md): Count "last 30 days" back from the newest data instead of from today.
- [Incomplete periods](partial-period.md): Mark a month that isn't over yet, so its short bar doesn't look like a drop.
- [Custom period comparison](custom-compare.md): Compare any two date ranges side by side, like H1 2026 and H2 2025.

# Custom period comparison

> Compare any two date ranges side by side, like H1 2026 and H2 2025.

- Pattern id: `custom-compare`
- Category: Dates & time
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#custom-compare
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader picks two ranges. Each country gets a pair of bars. Singapore grew from $82k to $113k, and Australia slipped from $119k to $113k.

Why: Launches, campaigns and seasons rarely line up with calendar periods.

## What to build

The reader picks two date ranges, and each item gets a pair of bars, one per range, with the percent change.

Layout: Paired horizontal bars per country.

Instruction: Let the reader pick two date ranges and compare them side by side.

Done when: Each pair matches that item's total in each range, and editing a date updates its bars right away.

On the ecommerce sample: With H2 2025 vs H1 2026, Singapore grows from $82k to $113k and Australia slips from $119k to $113k.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { country: customers.country }
  measures {
    h1_2026: revenue | exact_period(orders.ordered_at, @(2026-01-01 - 2026-06-30)),
    h2_2025: revenue | exact_period(orders.ordered_at, @(2025-07-01 - 2025-12-31)),
  }
  sorts { h1_2026 desc }
}
```

Saved result:

| country | h1_2026 | h2_2025 |
|---|---|---|
| Singapore | 113022.11 | 82176.18 |
| Australia | 112928.21 | 118664.80 |
| Vietnam | 88800.00 | 59959.90 |
| Germany | 72327.34 | 75832.27 |
| United States | 66426.54 | 79302.53 |
| Japan | 40648.55 | 41778.87 |

## SDK wiring

```js
// reader-chosen ranges: two date controls on two copies of the
// query (see bi-apps/drill.html)
app.mapControl(rangeA, queryA, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });
app.mapControl(rangeB, queryB, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });
```

## Notes

- `exact_period` for fixed ranges, or two date controls for ranges the reader picks

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<style>
	.rg { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 20px 132px 136px 12px 136px; gap: 6px; align-items: center; }
	.rg b { font-size: 12px; text-align: center; border-radius: 6px; line-height: 20px; } .rg .ta { background: rgb(24 20 31 / 0.12); } .rg .tb { background: var(--violet); color: #fff; }
	.rg input[type=date] { width: 136px; padding: 0 6px; } .rg select { padding: 0 6px; }
	.pr { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 92px minmax(0, 1fr) 128px; gap: 8px; align-items: center; padding: 3px 4px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; }
	.pr .t { display: grid; gap: 2px; } .pr .t span { display: block; height: 8px; border-radius: 2px; transition: width 320ms var(--ease); }
	.pr .a { background: rgb(24 20 31 / 0.18); } .pr .b { background: var(--violet); }
	.pr .v { text-align: right; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--weak); white-space: nowrap; } .up { color: #1f7a4d; } .dn { color: #b42318; }
	</style>
	<div class="app">
		<div class="rg"><b class="ta">A</b><select id="pa" aria-label="Range A preset"></select><input type="date" id="fa" aria-label="A from"><span class="hint">–</span><input type="date" id="ta" aria-label="A to"></div>
		<div class="rg"><b class="tb">B</b><select id="pb" aria-label="Range B preset"></select><input type="date" id="fb" aria-label="B from"><span class="hint">–</span><input type="date" id="tb" aria-label="B to"></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by country: <span id="la"></span> (grey) vs <span id="lb"></span></b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="pairs"></div></div>
		<div class="hint">One query declared twice, each copy with its own date control</div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Custom period comparison', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const AQL = 'explore { dimensions { country_name: customers.country } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }';
const qa = app.createQuery('byCountryA', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: AQL });
const qb = app.createQuery('byCountryB', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: AQL });
const ra = app.createFilter('rangeA', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'orders.ordered_at', label: 'Range A' });
const rb = app.createFilter('rangeB', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'orders.ordered_at', label: 'Range B' });
app.mapControl(ra, qa, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });
app.mapControl(rb, qb, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });
const P = [['H2 2025', '2025-07-01', '2025-12-31'], ['H1 2026', '2026-01-01', '2026-06-30'], ['Q3 2025', '2025-07-01', '2025-09-30'], ['Q3 2026', '2026-07-01', '2026-09-30'], ['Q2 2026', '2026-04-01', '2026-06-30'], ['Jun–Sep 2025', '2025-06-01', '2025-09-30'], ['Jun–Sep 2026', '2026-06-01', '2026-09-30']];
const MN = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec'];
const short = (a, b) => { const p = P.find((x) => x[1] === a && x[2] === b); if (p) return p[0]; const f = (s) => { const x = new Date(s + 'T00:00:00Z'); return x.getUTCDate() + ' ' + MN[x.getUTCMonth()] + ' ' + String(x.getUTCFullYear()).slice(2); }; return f(a) + '–' + f(b); };
function wire (f, sel, from, to, def) {
	for (const p of P) sel.add(new Option(p[0], p[0]));
	sel.add(new Option('Custom dates', ''));
	const set = (a, b) => { from.value = a; to.value = b; f.setCondition({ operator: 'between', values: [a, b] }); };
	sel.onchange = () => { const p = P.find((x) => x[0] === sel.value); if (p) { set(p[1], p[2]); app.execute(); } };
	const typed = () => { if (from.value && to.value) { const p = P.find((x) => x[1] === from.value && x[2] === to.value); sel.value = p ? p[0] : ''; set(from.value, to.value); app.execute(); } };
	from.onchange = typed; to.onchange = typed;
	sel.value = def; const p = P.find((x) => x[0] === def); set(p[1], p[2]);
}
wire(ra, K.$('#pa'), K.$('#fa'), K.$('#ta'), 'H2 2025');
wire(rb, K.$('#pb'), K.$('#fb'), K.$('#tb'), 'H1 2026');
app.subscribe(() => {
const s = [qa, qb].find((q) => q.state === 'error' || q.state === 'executing') || qb; K.status(s, K.$('#s1'));
const ca = ra.appliedCondition, cb = rb.appliedCondition;
K.$('#la').textContent = ca && ca.values ? short(ca.values[0], ca.values[1]) : '';
K.$('#lb').textContent = cb && cb.values ? short(cb.values[0], cb.values[1]) : '';
if (qa.result && qb.result) {
	const A = new Map(qa.result.rows.map((r) => [r.country_name, Number(r.total_revenue)]));
	const B = new Map(qb.result.rows.map((r) => [r.country_name, Number(r.total_revenue)]));
	const names = [...new Set([...B.keys(), ...A.keys()])].sort((x, y) => (B.get(y) || 0) - (B.get(x) || 0));
	const max = Math.max(1, ...A.values(), ...B.values());
	const box = K.$('#pairs'); box.innerHTML = '';
	for (const n of names) {
		const a = A.get(n) || 0, b = B.get(n) || 0, p = a ? (b - a) / a * 100 : null;
		const d = document.createElement('div'); d.className = 'pr';
		d.innerHTML = '<span>' + K.esc(n) + '</span><span class="t"><span class="a" style="width:0"></span><span class="b" style="width:0"></span></span><span class="v">' + K.compact.format(a) + ' → ' + K.compact.format(b) + ' ' + (p == null ? '' : '<span class="' + (p >= 0 ? 'up' : 'dn') + '">' + (p >= 0 ? '+' : '−') + Math.abs(p).toFixed(0) + '%</span>') + '</span>';
		box.appendChild(d);
		requestAnimationFrame(() => { d.querySelector('.a').style.width = (a / max * 100) + '%'; d.querySelector('.b').style.width = (b / max * 100) + '%'; });
	}
}
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [qa, qb]);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Pick **H2 2025** in the **A** menu
2. Pick **H1 2026** in the **B** menu: each country gets a grey A bar and a violet B bar
3. Read **Singapore**: it grew from $82k to $113k
4. Read **Australia**: it slipped from $119k to $113k
5. Type your own dates in the date boxes to compare any two ranges

## Other Dates & time patterns

- [Date filter](date-filter.md): Pick exact dates, a range like "last 3 months", or a phrase like "last quarter".
- [Date drill](date-drill.md): Switch the time detail between day, week, month and quarter, or click a period to see it in more detail.
- [Fiscal calendar](fiscal-calendar.md): Report by a fiscal year that starts in July instead of January.
- [As-of anchor](as-of-anchor.md): Count "last 30 days" back from the newest data instead of from today.
- [Incomplete periods](partial-period.md): Mark a month that isn't over yet, so its short bar doesn't look like a drop.
- [Period comparison](period-compare.md): Show each month next to the month before and the same month last year.
- [Period to date & trailing period](to-date.md): Show a year-to-date total and a rolling 3-month total for each month.

---

# Period to date & trailing period

> Show a year-to-date total and a rolling 3-month total for each month.

- Pattern id: `to-date`
- Category: Dates & time (also Tables & calculations)
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#to-date
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

Toggles add **YTD**, which climbs and resets in January, and **Trailing 3 months**, a rolling total.

Why: Executives ask "where are we for the year?" and "what's the run rate?" more often than "what happened in March?".

## What to build

Each toggle adds a line over the trend: one sums from the start of each year, one sums a rolling window.

Layout: Monthly columns with a YTD line and a trailing-3-month line.

Instruction: Add toggles for a year-to-date line and a trailing-period total on the trend.

Done when: The year-to-date line climbs and resets at each year start, and the trailing line sums the last few periods.

On the ecommerce sample: The YTD line climbs through each year and resets in January, and a month's trailing 3-month total equals its revenue plus the two months before.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() }
  measures {
    total_revenue: revenue,
    ytd: revenue | period_to_date('year', orders.ordered_at),
    trailing_3m: revenue | trailing_period(orders.ordered_at, interval(3 months)),
  }
  sorts { period asc }
}
```

Saved result:

| period | total_revenue | ytd | trailing_3m |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-06-01 | 97537.24 | 97537.24 | 97537.24 |
| 2025-07-01 | 66278.66 | 163815.90 | 163815.90 |
| 2025-08-01 | 70722.63 | 234538.53 | 234538.53 |
| 2025-09-01 | 94775.86 | 329314.39 | 231777.15 |
| 2025-10-01 | 85563.86 | 414878.25 | 251062.35 |
| 2025-11-01 | 74836.51 | 489714.76 | 255176.23 |
| 2025-12-01 | 65537.03 | 555251.79 | 225937.40 |
| 2026-01-01 | 82610.21 | 82610.21 | 222983.75 |
| 2026-02-01 | 86602.09 | 169212.30 | 234749.33 |
| 2026-03-01 | 61464.65 | 230676.95 | 230676.95 |
| 2026-04-01 | 77023.03 | 307699.98 | 225089.77 |
| 2026-05-01 | 88378.49 | 396078.47 | 226866.17 |

(4 more rows)

## SDK wiring

```js
// one query, three measures; toggles are renderer state
ytdToggle.onchange = () => redraw();
```

## Notes

- `period_to_date` and `trailing_period` are built-in functions

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<style>.cb { position: relative; } .cbc { display: flex; align-items: flex-end; height: 100%; } .cbw { flex: 1; min-width: 2px; height: 100%; position: relative; padding: 0; border: 0; border-radius: 0; background: none; display: block; } .cbw.click { cursor: pointer; } .cbw.click:hover .cbb { background: var(--violet-ink); } .cbb { position: absolute; left: 1px; right: 1px; bottom: 0; background: var(--violet); border-radius: 2px 2px 0 0; transition: height 320ms var(--ease); } .cbw.on .cbb { background: var(--violet-ink); } .cbw.hatch .cbb { background: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, var(--violet) 0 3px, #fff 3px 6px); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--violet); } .cb svg { position: absolute; inset: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; pointer-events: none; overflow: visible; } .cbd { position: absolute; width: 6px; height: 6px; margin: 0 0 -3px -3px; border-radius: 50%; pointer-events: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1.5px #fff; }  .ro { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 8px; margin-top: 8px; } .ro div { font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; color: var(--muted); } .ro b { display: block; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px; color: var(--ink); font-weight: 600; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .sw { display: inline-block; width: 12px; height: 2px; vertical-align: 3px; margin-right: 4px; }</style>
	<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Add</span><span class="chips"><button type="button" id="ytd" aria-pressed="false"><span class="sw" style="background:var(--ink)"></span>YTD</button><button type="button" id="t3" aria-pressed="false"><span class="sw" style="background:#1f8a5b"></span>Trailing 3 months</button></span>
		<select id="country" aria-label="Country"><option value="">All countries</option></select></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Monthly revenue</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="trend"></div>
		<div class="ro" id="ro"></div></div>
		<div class="hint">Click a month to read it. One query returns all three measures; the toggles only draw the lines</div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Period to date & trailing period', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const trend = app.createQuery('trend', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() } measures { total_revenue: revenue, ytd: revenue | period_to_date(\'year\', orders.ordered_at), trailing_3m: revenue | trailing_period(orders.ordered_at, interval(3 months)) } sorts { period asc } }' });
const country = app.createFilter('country', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.country', label: 'Country' });
app.mapControl(country, trend, { field: 'customers.country' });
const sel = K.$('#country');
country.loadOptions().then((vals) => vals.forEach((v) => sel.add(new Option(v, v))));
sel.onchange = () => { if (sel.value) country.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [sel.value] }); else country.reset(); app.execute(); };
function combo (el, rows, o) {
	const n = rows.length, vals = rows.map((r) => Number(o.value(r)) || 0), ls = o.lines || [];
	let max = Math.max(1, ...vals);
	for (const l of ls) for (const r of rows) { const v = l.value(r); if (v != null && isFinite(Number(v))) max = Math.max(max, Number(v)); }
	el.innerHTML = '<div class="cb" style="height:' + (o.height || 150) + 'px"><div class="cbc"></div><svg viewBox="0 0 ' + Math.max(n, 1) + ' 100" preserveAspectRatio="none"></svg></div><div class="axis"><span></span><span></span></div>';
	const box = el.querySelector('.cbc'), svg = el.querySelector('svg'), wrap = el.querySelector('.cb');
	let tip = document.querySelector('.tip'); if (!tip) { tip = document.createElement('div'); tip.className = 'tip'; document.body.appendChild(tip); }
	rows.forEach((r, i) => {
		const c = document.createElement(o.pick ? 'button' : 'div');
		c.className = 'cbw' + (o.hatch && o.hatch(r) ? ' hatch' : '') + (o.on && o.on(r) ? ' on' : '') + (o.pick ? ' click' : '');
		if (o.pick) { c.type = 'button'; c.setAttribute('aria-label', o.label(r)); c.onclick = () => { tip.style.opacity = 0; o.pick(r); }; }
		c.innerHTML = '<span class="cbb" style="height:' + Math.max(0.5, vals[i] / max * 100) + '%"></span>';
		c.onmousemove = (e) => { tip.textContent = o.tip ? o.tip(r) : o.label(r); tip.style.left = Math.max(4, Math.min(e.clientX + 10, innerWidth - tip.offsetWidth - 4)) + 'px'; tip.style.top = (e.clientY - 30) + 'px'; tip.style.opacity = 1; };
		c.onmouseleave = () => { tip.style.opacity = 0; };
		box.appendChild(c);
	});
	for (const l of ls) {
		let seg = [];
		const flush = () => { if (seg.length > 1) { const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'polyline'); p.setAttribute('points', seg.join(' ')); p.setAttribute('fill', 'none'); p.setAttribute('stroke', l.color); p.setAttribute('stroke-width', '2'); p.setAttribute('vector-effect', 'non-scaling-stroke'); if (l.dash) p.setAttribute('stroke-dasharray', '5 3'); svg.appendChild(p); } seg = []; };
		rows.forEach((r, i) => {
			const v = l.value(r);
			if (v == null || !isFinite(Number(v))) { flush(); return; }
			seg.push((i + 0.5) + ',' + (100 - Number(v) / max * 100));
			const d = document.createElement('span'); d.className = 'cbd'; d.style.background = l.color; d.style.left = ((i + 0.5) / n * 100) + '%'; d.style.bottom = (Number(v) / max * 100) + '%'; wrap.appendChild(d);
		});
		flush();
	}
	const ax = el.querySelectorAll('.axis span');
	ax[0].textContent = n ? o.label(rows[0]) : ''; ax[1].textContent = n > 1 ? o.label(rows[n - 1]) : '';
}
let ytd = false, t3 = false, pick = null;
const MN = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec'];
const lab = (v) => { const x = new Date(v); return MN[x.getUTCMonth()] + ' ' + x.getUTCFullYear(); };
const span3 = (v) => { const x = new Date(v); const a = new Date(Date.UTC(x.getUTCFullYear(), x.getUTCMonth() - 2, 1)); return MN[a.getUTCMonth()] + '–' + MN[x.getUTCMonth()]; };
K.$('#ytd').onclick = () => { ytd = !ytd; draw(); };
K.$('#t3').onclick = () => { t3 = !t3; draw(); };
function draw () {
	K.status(trend, K.$('#s1'));
	K.$('#ytd').setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(ytd)); K.$('#t3').setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(t3));
	if (trend.result && trend.result.rows.length) {
		const rows = trend.result.rows;
		const r = rows.find((x) => x.period === pick) || rows[rows.length - 1];
		combo(K.$('#trend'), rows, { label: (x) => lab(x.period), value: (x) => x.total_revenue, on: (x) => x === r, pick: (x) => { pick = x.period; draw(); },
			lines: [ytd ? { value: (x) => x.ytd, color: 'var(--ink)', dash: true } : null, t3 ? { value: (x) => x.trailing_3m, color: '#1f8a5b' } : null].filter(Boolean),
			tip: (x) => lab(x.period) + ' · ' + K.compact.format(Number(x.total_revenue)) + (ytd ? ' · YTD ' + K.compact.format(Number(x.ytd)) : '') + (t3 ? ' · 3m ' + K.compact.format(Number(x.trailing_3m)) : '') });
		const y = new Date(r.period).getUTCFullYear();
		K.$('#ro').innerHTML = '<div>' + K.esc(lab(r.period)) + '<b>' + K.compact.format(Number(r.total_revenue)) + '</b></div>'
			+ '<div>YTD, Jan–' + K.esc(lab(r.period)) + (ytd ? '' : ' (off)') + '<b>' + (ytd ? K.compact.format(Number(r.ytd)) : '–') + '</b></div>'
			+ '<div>Trailing 3m, ' + K.esc(span3(r.period)) + (t3 ? '' : ' (off)') + '<b>' + (t3 ? K.compact.format(Number(r.trailing_3m)) : '–') + '</b></div>';
	}
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [trend], () => ['lines: ' + ([ytd ? 'YTD' : '', t3 ? 'trailing 3 months' : ''].filter(Boolean).join(', ') || 'none') + ' (renderer state)']);
}
app.subscribe(draw);
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Click **YTD**: a dashed line climbs through each year and resets in January
2. Click **Trailing 3 months**: a green line shows the rolling 3-month total
3. Click a month to read its revenue, YTD and trailing 3 months under the chart

# Drill down

> Click a region to see its countries, then customers, then their orders, and climb back with breadcrumbs.

- Pattern id: `hierarchy-drill`
- Category: Drilling (also Selections)
- Status: Works with app code: anfra supplies the queries, the app adds some logic
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#hierarchy-drill
- Full Data App: https://demo.anfra.ai/apps/patterns/drill-down
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader clicks **APAC**, then **Australia**, then **Customer 184**, and lands on that customer's 13 orders. The breadcrumb reads "All regions › APAC › Australia › Customer 184"; clicking a crumb climbs back. The KPIs and trend on the right follow the path.

Why: A drill path answers "why is this number big?" one step at a time.

## What to build

Clicking a value opens the next level down filtered to it, and the breadcrumb records each step so far.

Layout: Bars at each level with a breadcrumb trail.

Instruction: Let the reader drill down level by level by clicking, with a breadcrumb to climb back up.

Done when: Each level's values add up to the one clicked, and clicking a crumb returns to that level with its filters.

On the ecommerce sample: Clicking APAC, Australia, then Customer 184 lists that customer's 13 orders, the breadcrumb reads All regions › APAC › Australia › Customer 184, and APAC climbs back.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { key: markets.name }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue, order_n: order_count, buyers: count_distinct(orders, orders.customer_id) }
  sorts { total_revenue desc }
}
```

Reader input the SDK sent:

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "field": "markets.region",
      "operator": "is",
      "values": [
        "APAC"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Saved result:

| key | total_revenue | order_n | buyers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Australia | 313397.48 | 347 | 43 |
| Singapore | 255030.20 | 317 | 41 |
| Vietnam | 185254.77 | 202 | 28 |
| Japan | 118326.31 | 146 | 22 |

The recording is the real Data App `apps/patterns/drill-down.html`, running on the ecommerce sample. Each level is its own query, and the path is one filter per level: `markets.region`, `markets.name`, `customers.id`. The input above is the path after clicking APAC.

## SDK wiring

```js
const levels = [
  // a filter control per level
  { q: byCategory, f: category },
  { q: byProduct, f: product },
  { q: orders, f: null },
];
// level i+1 is mapped to the filters of levels 0..i
chart.on('click', (p) => {
  const lvl = levels[depth];
  lvl.f.setCondition({
    operator: 'is',
    values: [lvl.q.result.rows[p.dataIndex][lvl.key]],
  });
  depth++;
  app.execute();
  renderLevel(depth);
});
crumb.onclick = (i) => {
  for (const l of levels.slice(i)) l.f?.reset();
  depth = i;
  app.execute();
};
```

State it touches: Drill context: the path [category, product] stored as filter conditions, plus the current depth (renderer).

## Notes

- The path is just filters, so it shows in `executedAql` and can be bookmarked like any other filter
- Limits: Works with app code. A proposed `createDrillPath([...fields])` would hold the path and depth as one control.

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<style>
	.crumbs { display: flex; gap: 2px; align-items: center; flex-wrap: wrap; font-size: 12px; }
	.crumbs button { height: 24px; padding: 0 8px; font-size: 12px; border-radius: 6px; }
	.crumbs .sep { color: var(--muted); }
	.crumbs .here { font-weight: 600; padding: 0 6px; }
	.lv { max-height: 200px; overflow: auto; }
	.kp { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 6px; margin-bottom: 8px; }
	.kp > div { font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; color: var(--muted); }
	#mini .colz { height: 96px; }
	</style>
	<div class="app">
		<div class="crumbs" id="crumbs"></div>
		<div class="cols" style="grid-template-columns: 1.25fr 1fr">
			<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b id="title">Regions</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div class="lv"><div id="level"></div></div><div class="hint" id="lh"></div></div>
			<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>The path so far</b><span class="status" id="s2"></span></div>
				<div class="kp"><div>Revenue<div class="kpi" id="k1">–</div></div><div>Orders<div class="kpi" id="k2">–</div></div></div>
				<div class="lbl">Monthly revenue</div><div id="mini"></div></div>
		</div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Drill down', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const DS = 'ecommerce', M = 'measures { total_revenue: revenue, order_n: order_count }';
const byRegion = app.createQuery('byRegion', { dataset: DS, aql: 'explore { dimensions { key: markets.region } ' + M + ' sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const byCountry = app.createQuery('byCountry', { dataset: DS, aql: 'explore { dimensions { key: markets.name } ' + M + ' sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const byCustomer = app.createQuery('byCustomer', { dataset: DS, aql: 'explore { dimensions { key: customers.name, cid: customers.id } ' + M + ' sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const orders = app.createQuery('orders', { dataset: DS, pageSize: 25, aql: 'explore { dimensions { order_id: orders.id, ordered_on: orders.ordered_at, order_status: orders.status } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { ordered_on desc, order_id desc } }' });
const scope = app.createQuery('scope', { dataset: DS, aql: 'explore { ' + M + ' }' });
const scopeTrend = app.createQuery('scopeTrend', { dataset: DS, aql: 'explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { period asc } }' });
const L = [
	{ q: byRegion, f: app.createFilter('region', { dataset: DS, field: 'markets.region', label: 'Region' }), field: 'markets.region', name: 'Regions', val: (r) => r.key },
	{ q: byCountry, f: app.createFilter('country', { dataset: DS, field: 'markets.name', label: 'Country' }), field: 'markets.name', name: 'Countries', val: (r) => r.key },
	{ q: byCustomer, f: app.createFilter('customer', { dataset: DS, field: 'customers.id', label: 'Customer' }), field: 'customers.id', name: 'Customers', val: (r) => String(r.cid) },
	{ q: orders, f: null, name: 'Orders' },
];
// level i is filtered by every level above it; the KPIs and trend follow the whole path
L.forEach((lvl, i) => L.slice(0, i).forEach((up) => app.mapControl(up.f, lvl.q, { field: up.field })));
for (const q of [scope, scopeTrend]) for (const up of L.slice(0, 3)) app.mapControl(up.f, q, { field: up.field });
const path = []; // labels picked so far
let depth = 0;
function down (r) { const lvl = L[depth]; lvl.f.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [lvl.val(r)] }); path.push(r.key); depth++; app.execute(); }
function climb (i) { for (const l of L.slice(i, 3)) l.f.reset(); path.length = i; depth = i; app.execute(); }
const mon = (v) => new Date(v).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', year: '2-digit', timeZone: 'UTC' });
const dd = (v) => new Date(String(v).slice(0, 10) + 'T00:00:00Z').toLocaleDateString('en-GB', { day: 'numeric', month: 'short', year: 'numeric', timeZone: 'UTC' }).replace('Sept', 'Sep');
app.subscribe(() => {
const lvl = L[depth];
K.status(lvl.q, K.$('#s1')); K.status(scope, K.$('#s2'));
const cr = K.$('#crumbs'); cr.innerHTML = '';
['All regions'].concat(path).forEach((t, i) => {
	if (i) { const s = document.createElement('span'); s.className = 'sep'; s.textContent = '›'; cr.appendChild(s); }
	if (i === path.length) { const s = document.createElement('span'); s.className = 'here'; s.textContent = t; cr.appendChild(s); }
	else { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = t; b.onclick = () => climb(i); cr.appendChild(b); }
});
K.$('#title').textContent = lvl.name + (path.length ? (depth === 3 ? ' of ' : ' in ') + path[path.length - 1] : '');
if (lvl.q.result) {
	if (depth < 3) { K.bars(K.$('#level'), lvl.q.result.rows, { label: (r) => r.key, value: (r) => r.total_revenue, pick: (r) => down(r) }); K.$('#lh').textContent = 'Click a bar to drill in'; }
	else {
		K.table(K.$('#level'), [{ key: 'order_id', label: 'Order', fmt: (v) => '#' + v }, { key: 'ordered_on', label: 'Date', fmt: (v) => dd(v) }, { key: 'order_status', label: 'Status' }, { key: 'total_revenue', label: 'Revenue', num: true, fmt: (v) => K.money.format(v) }], lvl.q.result.rows);
		K.$('#lh').textContent = 'Click a crumb above to climb back';
	}
}
if (scope.result) { const s = scope.result.rows[0] || {}; K.$('#k1').textContent = K.compact.format(Number(s.total_revenue || 0)); K.$('#k2').textContent = K.int.format(Number(s.order_n || 0)); }
if (scopeTrend.result) K.columns(K.$('#mini'), scopeTrend.result.rows, { label: (r) => mon(r.period), value: (r) => r.total_revenue });
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [lvl.q, scope], () => ['depth: ' + depth + ' of 3 (renderer state; the path is the filter conditions)']);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Click **APAC** in **Regions**
2. Click **Australia** in **Countries in APAC**
3. Click **Customer 184**: the table lists that customer's 13 orders
4. Read the breadcrumb, **All regions › APAC › Australia › Customer 184**, and the KPIs and trend on the right, which follow the path
5. Click **APAC** in the breadcrumb to climb back

- [Drill path](drill-path.md): Keep a trail of every step down and up, and click any step to go back to it.
- [Break down](adhoc-breakdown.md): Right-click a bar to split it by another field, like order status.
- [View underlying data](underlying-records.md): Click a column on a chart to see the individual orders behind it.

# Drill path

> Keep a trail of every step down and up, and click any step to go back to it.

- Pattern id: `drill-path`
- Category: Drilling (also Save & share)
- Status: Works with app code: anfra supplies the queries, the app adds some logic
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#drill-path
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader drills **APAC › Australia**, goes **↑ up** to APAC, then drills into **Singapore**. The drill path reads "All regions › ↓ APAC › ↓ Australia › ↑ APAC › ↓ Singapore"; clicking **↓ Australia** brings back Australia's customers and its $313,397.

Why: A breadcrumb shows where the reader is. A drill path shows how they got there, so they can compare branches without starting over.

## What to build

Each drill down or up adds a step that remembers its filters; clicking a step sets those filters again.

Layout: Bars at the current level, with the drill path as a row of steps above them.

Instruction: Let readers drill down and up, keep every step as a drill path of breadcrumbs, and click any breadcrumb to go back to that step.

Done when: The path lists every step in order, up steps included, and clicking one shows exactly what the reader saw then.

On the ecommerce sample: Drill APAC, Australia, go up, then drill Singapore: the path shows all five steps, and clicking ↓ Australia brings back its $313,397.

## AQL

Not run as written: each step is the same level query with the path's filters.

```aql
explore { dimensions { key: markets.name } measures { total_revenue: revenue } filters { markets.region is 'APAC' } sorts { total_revenue desc } }
```

## SDK wiring

```js
// each step keeps the filter values it left behind
const trail = [{ label: 'All regions', picks: [] }];
let at = 0;
function step(label, picks) {
  trail.splice(at + 1); // a new step after a jump drops the rest
  trail.push({ label, picks });
  at = trail.length - 1;
  show(picks);
}
function show(picks) {
  levels.slice(0, 2).forEach((l, i) =>
    picks[i] != null
      ? l.filter.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [picks[i]] })
      : l.filter.reset(),
  );
  app.execute();
}
// down: step(row.key, [...picks, row.key])
// up:   step(parent, picks.slice(0, -1))
// jump: at = i; show(trail[i].picks)
```

State it touches: Drill context: the path as filter conditions, plus the list of steps (renderer state) that records how the reader got there.

## Notes

- Each step is a set of filter conditions; jumping back sets them again
- Limits: Works with app code: the app keeps the list of steps. A proposed `createDrillPath()` would hold the path, and its history, as one control.

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<style>
	.trail { display: flex; gap: 4px; align-items: center; flex-wrap: wrap; font-size: 12px; min-height: 28px; }
	.trail .lbl { margin-right: 4px; }
	.trail button { height: 24px; padding: 0 8px; font-size: 12px; border-radius: 6px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
	.trail button[aria-current='step'] { border: 2px solid var(--violet-ink); color: var(--violet-ink); font-weight: 600; }
	.trail button.after { opacity: 0.45; }
	.trail .sep { color: var(--muted); }
	.trail .up { color: #b4541a; }
	.lv { max-height: 220px; overflow: auto; }
	</style>
	<div class="app">
		<div class="trail" id="trail"></div>
		<div class="row"><button type="button" id="up">↑ Up a level</button><span class="hint" id="hint"></span></div>
		<div class="cols" style="grid-template-columns: 1.3fr 1fr">
			<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b id="title">Regions</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div class="lv"><div id="level"></div></div></div>
			<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue here</b><span class="status" id="s2"></span></div><div class="kpi" id="k1">–</div><div class="hint" id="where">All regions</div></div>
		</div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Drill path', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const DS = 'ecommerce', M = 'measures { total_revenue: revenue }';
const byRegion = app.createQuery('byRegion', { dataset: DS, aql: 'explore { dimensions { key: markets.region } ' + M + ' sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const byCountry = app.createQuery('byCountry', { dataset: DS, aql: 'explore { dimensions { key: markets.name } ' + M + ' sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const byCustomer = app.createQuery('byCustomer', { dataset: DS, aql: 'explore { dimensions { key: customers.name } ' + M + ' sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const scope = app.createQuery('scope', { dataset: DS, aql: 'explore { ' + M + ' }' });
const L = [
	{ q: byRegion, f: app.createFilter('region', { dataset: DS, field: 'markets.region', label: 'Region' }), field: 'markets.region', name: 'Regions' },
	{ q: byCountry, f: app.createFilter('country', { dataset: DS, field: 'markets.name', label: 'Country' }), field: 'markets.name', name: 'Countries' },
	{ q: byCustomer, f: null, name: 'Customers' },
];
// each level is filtered by the levels above it; the KPI follows the whole path
L.forEach((lvl, i) => L.slice(0, i).forEach((up) => app.mapControl(up.f, lvl.q, { field: up.field })));
for (const up of L.slice(0, 2)) app.mapControl(up.f, scope, { field: up.field });
// the drill path: every step down or up, as the filter conditions it left behind
const trail = [{ label: 'All regions', dir: '', picks: [] }];
let at = 0;
const picks = () => trail[at].picks;
function show (p) {
	L.slice(0, 2).forEach((l, i) => { if (p[i] != null) l.f.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [p[i]] }); else l.f.reset(); });
	app.execute();
}
function step (label, dir, p) { trail.splice(at + 1); trail.push({ label, dir, picks: p }); at = trail.length - 1; show(p); }
const down = (r) => step(r.key, '↓', picks().concat(r.key));
K.$('#up').onclick = () => { const p = picks().slice(0, -1); if (picks().length) step(p.length ? p[p.length - 1] : 'All regions', '↑', p); };
function jump (i) { at = i; show(trail[i].picks); }
app.subscribe(() => {
const p = picks(), lvl = L[p.length];
K.status(lvl.q, K.$('#s1')); K.status(scope, K.$('#s2'));
const tr = K.$('#trail'); tr.innerHTML = '<span class="lbl">Drill path</span>';
trail.forEach((s, i) => {
	if (i) { const sep = document.createElement('span'); sep.className = 'sep'; sep.textContent = '›'; tr.appendChild(sep); }
	const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button';
	b.innerHTML = (s.dir ? '<span class="' + (s.dir === '↑' ? 'up' : '') + '">' + s.dir + '</span> ' : '') + K.esc(s.label);
	if (i === at) b.setAttribute('aria-current', 'step'); else if (i > at) b.className = 'after';
	b.title = s.picks.length ? s.picks.join(' › ') : 'All regions';
	b.onclick = () => jump(i);
	tr.appendChild(b);
});
K.$('#up').disabled = !p.length;
K.$('#title').textContent = lvl.name + (p.length ? ' in ' + p[p.length - 1] : '');
K.$('#where').textContent = p.length ? p.join(' › ') : 'All regions';
K.$('#hint').textContent = p.length < 2 ? 'Click a bar to drill down' : 'Customers is the last level';
if (lvl.q.result) K.bars(K.$('#level'), lvl.q.result.rows, { label: (r) => r.key, value: (r) => r.total_revenue, pick: p.length < 2 ? (r) => down(r) : null });
if (scope.result) K.$('#k1').textContent = K.money.format(Number((scope.result.rows[0] || {}).total_revenue || 0));
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [lvl.q, scope], () => ['drill path → step ' + (at + 1) + ' of ' + trail.length + ' (the path is the app\'s list; each step is just filter conditions)']);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Click **APAC** in **Regions**, then **Australia**: the drill path reads **All regions › ↓ APAC › ↓ Australia**
2. Click **↑ Up a level**: you're back in **Countries in APAC**, and the path adds **↑ APAC**
3. Click **Singapore**: the path keeps every step, **… › ↑ APAC › ↓ Singapore**
4. Click **↓ Australia** in the path: Australia's customers come back, with **Revenue here** at $313,397

## Other Drilling patterns

- [Drill down](hierarchy-drill.md): Click a region to see its countries, then customers, then their orders, and climb back with breadcrumbs.
- [Break down](adhoc-breakdown.md): Right-click a bar to split it by another field, like order status.
- [View underlying data](underlying-records.md): Click a column on a chart to see the individual orders behind it.
- [Drill-through](drillthrough.md): Click a country to open another app already filtered to that country.
- [Row actions](row-actions.md): Put links on each table row: open the customer in your CRM, email them, or see their orders.

# Break down

> Right-click a bar to split it by another field, like order status.

- Pattern id: `adhoc-breakdown`
- Category: Drilling (also Tables & calculations)
- Status: Works with app code: anfra supplies the queries, the app adds some logic
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#adhoc-breakdown
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader right-clicks **Software** and picks **Break down by → Status**. A new panel shows Software revenue by status.

Why: The next question is often about a different dimension, not a deeper one.

## What to build

Right-clicking a bar opens a short list of fields, and picking one opens a panel splitting that bar's value by it.

Layout: Context menu over a bar, then a new breakdown panel.

Instruction: Let the reader right-click a bar and break that value down by another field from a short list.

Done when: The new panel's parts add up to the bar clicked, and closing it leaves the main chart as it was.

On the ecommerce sample: Right-clicking Software and picking Status opens a Software by status panel with completed, shipped and cancelled, and Close breakdown clears it.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { status: orders.status }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count }
  sorts { total_revenue desc }
}
```

Reader input the SDK sent:

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "field": "products.category",
      "operator": "is",
      "values": [
        "Software"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Saved result:

| status | total_revenue | num_orders |
|---|---|---|
| completed | 292664.00 | 375 |
| shipped | 104828.00 | 135 |
| cancelled | 99902.00 | 132 |

## SDK wiring

```js
let n = 0;
// dimRef from a fixed list, never typed text
function breakdown(row, dimRef, alias) {
  const q = app.createQuery('bd' + ++n, {
    dataset: 'ecommerce',
    aql: `
      explore {
        dimensions { ${alias}: ${dimRef} }
        measures { total_revenue: revenue }
        sorts { total_revenue desc }
      }
    `,
  });
  const f = app.createFilter('bdf' + n, {
    dataset: 'ecommerce',
    field: 'products.category',
  });
  f.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [row.category] });
  app.mapControl(f, q, { field: 'products.category' });
  return app.execute();
}
```

## Notes

- A new `explore` from a fixed list of dimensions. The parent value is a mapped filter, not text in the query
- Limits: Works with app code: "AQL is fixed once declared", so each breakdown is a new query.

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<style>
		.menu { position: fixed; z-index: 5; background: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong); border-radius: 10px; box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgb(24 20 31 / 0.14); padding: 4px; display: grid; min-width: 168px; }
		.menu[hidden] { display: none; }
		.menu .mh { font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; color: var(--muted); padding: 4px 8px; }
		.menu button { border: 0; border-radius: 6px; text-align: left; height: 28px; font-size: 14px; }
		.menu button:hover { background: var(--violet-soft); }
		#bd .b, #bycat .b { grid-template-columns: 88px minmax(0, 1fr) 54px; }
		</style>
		<div class="row"><span class="hint">Right-click (or click) a category to break it down by another field</span></div>
		<div class="cols"><div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by category</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="bycat"></div></div>
		<div class="panel" id="bdp"><div class="ph"><b id="bdt">Breakdown</b><span class="status" id="s2"></span></div><div id="bd"><div class="hint">No breakdown yet</div></div><div class="row" style="margin-top:8px"><button type="button" id="close" hidden>Close breakdown</button></div></div></div>
		<div class="menu" id="menu" hidden></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Break down', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const byCategory = app.createQuery('byCategory', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { category_name: products.category } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const DIMS = [{ id: 'status', label: 'Status', ref: 'orders.status' }, { id: 'country', label: 'Country', ref: 'customers.country' }, { id: 'product', label: 'Product', ref: 'products.name' }];
const made = {};
let active = null, parent = null;
function breakdown (row, d) {
	if (!made[d.id]) {
		const q = app.createQuery('by_' + d.id, { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { part: ' + d.ref + ' } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
		const f = app.createFilter('of_' + d.id, { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'products.category', label: 'Category' });
		app.mapControl(f, q, { field: 'products.category' });
		made[d.id] = { q, f, d };
	}
	made[d.id].f.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [row.category_name] });
	active = made[d.id]; parent = row.category_name;
	return app.execute();
}
const menu = K.$('#menu');
function openMenu (row, x, y) {
	menu.innerHTML = '<div class="mh">Break down ' + K.esc(row.category_name) + ' by</div>';
	for (const d of DIMS) { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = d.label; b.onclick = () => { menu.hidden = true; breakdown(row, d); }; menu.appendChild(b); }
	menu.hidden = false;
	menu.style.left = Math.min(x, innerWidth - 180) + 'px'; menu.style.top = Math.min(y, innerHeight - 130) + 'px';
	menu.querySelector('button').focus();
}
document.addEventListener('pointerdown', (e) => { if (!menu.contains(e.target) && !e.target.closest('#bycat')) menu.hidden = true; });
document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => { if (e.key === 'Escape') menu.hidden = true; });
K.$('#close').onclick = () => { active = null; parent = null; draw(); };
function draw () {
	K.status(byCategory, K.$('#s1'));
	if (byCategory.result) {
		K.bars(K.$('#bycat'), byCategory.result.rows, { label: (r) => r.category_name, value: (r) => r.total_revenue, on: parent ? (r) => r.category_name === parent : null,
			pick: (r, e) => { const b = e.currentTarget.getBoundingClientRect(); openMenu(r, e.clientX || b.left + 24, e.clientY || b.bottom); } });
		K.$('#bycat').querySelectorAll('.b').forEach((el, i) => { el.oncontextmenu = (e) => { e.preventDefault(); openMenu(byCategory.result.rows[i], e.clientX, e.clientY); }; });
	}
	K.$('#close').hidden = !active;
	if (active) {
		K.status(active.q, K.$('#s2'));
		K.$('#bdt').textContent = parent + ' by ' + active.d.label.toLowerCase();
		if (active.q.result) K.bars(K.$('#bd'), active.q.result.rows, { label: (r) => r.part, value: (r) => r.total_revenue });
	} else { K.$('#s2').textContent = ''; K.$('#bdt').textContent = 'Breakdown'; K.$('#bd').className = ''; K.$('#bd').innerHTML = '<div class="hint">No breakdown yet</div>'; }
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, active ? [active.q] : [byCategory], () => [active ? 'new query by_' + active.d.id + ': dimensions { part: ' + active.d.ref + ' }' : null]);
}
app.subscribe(draw);
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Right-click the **Software** bar, or just click it
2. Pick **Status** in the **Break down Software by** menu
3. Read the new panel, **Software by status**: completed, shipped and cancelled
4. Click **Close breakdown** to clear it
