# View underlying data

> Click a column on a chart to see the individual orders behind it.

- Pattern id: `underlying-records`
- Category: Drilling (also Tables & calculations)
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#underlying-records
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

KPIs and a revenue-by-month chart show $1,283,053 from 1,500 orders. The reader clicks **May 2026**: the KPIs narrow to that month, and a drawer opens with its 101 orders, newest first, 25 at a time. **Load more** fetches the next 25.

Why: Seeing the actual orders is how readers come to trust a total.

## What to build

Clicking a chart element filters to its values and opens a drawer with the records behind it, a page at a time.

Layout: Three KPIs and a revenue-by-month column chart; clicking a column opens a drawer with the order table, a row count and Load more.

Instruction: Clicking a point or column in my charts narrows the KPIs to it and opens a drawer listing the records behind it, newest first, with Load more.

Done when: The drawer lists only records matching the clicked element, newest first, and Load more adds the next page without repeats.

On the ecommerce sample: Clicking May 2026 shows $88,378 and opens a drawer with the first 25 of its 101 orders, newest first; Load more adds the next 25.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions {
    order_id: orders.id,
    ordered_at: orders.ordered_at,
    customer: customers.name,
    country: customers.country,
    status: orders.status,
  }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue, units: units_sold }
  sorts { ordered_at desc, order_id desc }
}
```

Reader input the SDK sent:

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "field": "products.category",
      "operator": "is",
      "values": [
        "Software"
      ]
    },
    {
      "field": "customers.country",
      "operator": "is",
      "values": [
        "Japan"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Saved result:

| order_id | ordered_at | customer | country | status | total_revenue | units |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 566 | 2026-09-22 | Customer 72 | Japan | completed | 596.00 | 4 |
| 175 | 2026-09-18 | Customer 136 | Japan | completed | 596.00 | 4 |
| 874 | 2026-09-02 | Customer 136 | Japan | completed | 299.00 | 1 |
| 958 | 2026-08-26 | Customer 62 | Japan | completed | 745.00 | 5 |
| 1305 | 2026-08-24 | Customer 166 | Japan | completed | 897.00 | 3 |
| 307 | 2026-08-22 | Customer 98 | Japan | completed | 745.00 | 5 |
| 816 | 2026-08-16 | Customer 164 | Japan | cancelled | 447.00 | 3 |
| 985 | 2026-08-10 | Customer 164 | Japan | completed | 897.00 | 3 |
| 799 | 2026-08-08 | Customer 182 | Japan | shipped | 1495.00 | 5 |
| 190 | 2026-08-08 | Customer 103 | Japan | shipped | 1196.00 | 4 |
| 1195 | 2026-07-28 | Customer 190 | Japan | shipped | 299.00 | 1 |

(28 more rows)

## SDK wiring

```js
const records = app.createQuery('records', {
  dataset: 'ecommerce',
  aql: RECORDS_AQL,
  pageSize: 25,
});
// the clicked month filters the KPIs and the records
app.mapControl(month, kpis, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });
app.mapControl(month, records, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });
column.onclick = () => {
  month.setCondition({ operator: 'between',
    values: [monthStart, monthEnd] });
  app.execute();
};
// appends; rejects on failure
loadMore.onclick = () => records.fetchMore();
loadMore.hidden = !records.hasMore;
```

State it touches: Analytical: the clicked month and the page. Runtime: rows loaded so far and `hasMore`.

## Notes

- A records `explore` plus a cross-filter edge. Paging is `pageSize` and `fetchMore()`

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<style>
	.stage { position: relative; min-height: 360px; overflow: hidden; display: grid; gap: 10px; align-content: start; }
	.kpis { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 8px; }
	.kpis .panel { padding: 8px 12px; }
	.kpis .lab { font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; color: var(--muted); }
	.colz .cw.on .c { background: var(--violet-ink); }
	.drawer { position: absolute; inset: 82px 0 0 48px; background: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong); border-radius: 10px; padding: 10px 12px; box-shadow: -8px 0 24px rgb(24 20 31 / 0.10); transform: translateX(105%); visibility: hidden; transition: transform 240ms var(--ease), visibility 240ms; }
	.drawer.open { transform: none; visibility: visible; }
	.drawer .tw { max-height: 200px; }
	.drawer .ft { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; }
	.drawer .ph { margin-bottom: 0; align-items: center; }
	.drawer .ph button { height: 24px; padding: 0 8px; font-size: 12px; border-radius: 6px; }
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'View underlying data', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const trend = app.createQuery('trend', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() } measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count } sorts { period asc } }' });
const kpis = app.createQuery('kpis', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count, avg_order_value: aov } }' });
const records = app.createQuery('records', { dataset: 'ecommerce', pageSize: 25, aql: 'explore { dimensions { order_id: orders.id, ordered_on: orders.ordered_at, customer_name: customers.name, order_status: orders.status } measures { total_revenue: revenue, units: units_sold } sorts { ordered_on desc, order_id desc } }' });
// the clicked month narrows the KPIs and the records; the trend keeps every month
const month = app.createFilter('month', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'orders.ordered_at', label: 'Month' });
app.mapControl(month, kpis, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });
app.mapControl(month, records, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });
let picked = null, err = '';
const MON = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec'];
const d0 = (v) => new Date(String(v).slice(0, 10) + 'T00:00:00Z');
const iso = (x) => x.toISOString().slice(0, 10);
const mlabel = (v) => { const x = d0(v); return MON[x.getUTCMonth()] + ' ' + x.getUTCFullYear(); };
const dd = (v) => { const x = d0(v); return x.getUTCDate() + ' ' + MON[x.getUTCMonth()] + ' ' + String(x.getUTCFullYear()).slice(2); };
function open (r) {
	const s = d0(r.period), e = new Date(Date.UTC(s.getUTCFullYear(), s.getUTCMonth() + 1, 0));
	picked = r; err = '';
	month.setCondition({ operator: 'between', values: [iso(s), iso(e)] });
	app.execute();
}
K.$('#close').onclick = () => { picked = null; month.reset(); app.execute(); };
K.$('#more').onclick = () => { err = ''; records.fetchMore().catch((e) => { err = 'Couldn\'t load more: ' + e.message; draw(); }); };
function draw () {
	K.status(trend, K.$('#s1'));
	if (kpis.result && kpis.result.rows[0]) {
		const k = kpis.result.rows[0];
		K.$('#l1').textContent = 'Revenue · ' + (picked ? mlabel(picked.period) : 'all months');
		K.$('#k1').textContent = K.money.format(Number(k.total_revenue || 0));
		K.$('#k2').textContent = K.int.format(Number(k.num_orders || 0));
		K.$('#k3').textContent = K.money.format(Number(k.avg_order_value || 0));
	}
	if (trend.result) {
		K.columns(K.$('#trend'), trend.result.rows, { label: (r) => mlabel(r.period), value: (r) => r.total_revenue, pick: open });
		K.$('#trend').querySelectorAll('.cw').forEach((c, i) => c.classList.toggle('on', !!picked && String(trend.result.rows[i].period) === String(picked.period)));
	}
	const dr = K.$('#drawer'); dr.classList.toggle('open', !!picked); dr.setAttribute('aria-hidden', String(!picked));
	if (picked) {
		K.status(records, K.$('#s2'));
		K.$('#dt').textContent = mlabel(picked.period) + ' · ' + K.money.format(Number(picked.total_revenue));
		if (records.result && records.state !== 'executing') {
			K.table(K.$('#records'), [{ key: 'order_id', label: 'Order', fmt: (v) => '#' + v }, { key: 'ordered_on', label: 'Date', fmt: dd }, { key: 'customer_name', label: 'Customer' }, { key: 'order_status', label: 'Status' }, { key: 'total_revenue', label: 'Revenue', num: true, fmt: (v) => K.money.format(v) }], records.result.rows);
			K.$('#count').textContent = err || (K.int.format(records.result.rows.length) + ' of ' + K.int.format(Number(picked.num_orders)) + ' orders loaded, newest first');
		}
		K.$('#more').hidden = !records.hasMore;
	}
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, picked ? [kpis, records] : [kpis, trend], () => [picked ? 'pageSize 25 · pages loaded: ' + records.page + (records.hasMore ? ' · more to load' : ' · all loaded') : '']);
}
app.subscribe(draw);
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read the KPIs: **$1,283,053** from **1,500** orders, and revenue by month below
2. Click the **May 2026** column: the KPIs narrow to **$88,378**, and a drawer opens with that month's orders, newest first
3. Click **Load more**: the next 25 of its 101 orders load
4. Click **Close**: the KPIs go back to all months

# Drill-through

> Click a country to open another app already filtered to that country.

- Pattern id: `drillthrough`
- Category: Drilling (also Save & share)
- Status: Proposed: anfra cannot do this yet (checked on 0.13.3: no write path, no query parameters, and the app frame allows scripts only, so no navigation or storage). Build the closest version and say what is missing
- Gallery card: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#drillthrough
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

From a summary page, the reader clicks **Japan**, picks **Open in Cohort Heatmap**, and that app opens with Country = Japan.

Why: Data Apps work better as a connected set than as islands.

## What to build

Clicking a value opens a link to another Data App, passing that value so the app opens already filtered.

Layout: A context menu, then a second app frame with the filter already set.

Instruction: Clicking a value opens another Data App with that value already filtered.

Done when: The other app opens with the clicked value set in its filter, and its numbers match that value's slice.

On the ecommerce sample: Clicking Japan and picking Open in Cohort Heatmap opens that app with Country = Japan already set in its filter.

## AQL

Not run as written: no query change.

```aql
// target app: the same field-backed filter, set from the context the host passes in
// country.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: ['Japan'] })
```

## SDK wiring

```js
// Proposed (not real API):
// Anfra.open('reports/cohort-heatmap', { controls: { country: {
// operator: 'is', values: ['Japan'] } } })
// and in the target: Anfra.context.controls
```

## Notes

- Proposed: the host carries a snapshot (control conditions) into the target app
- Limits: Proposed. The app sandbox allows scripts only: navigation and popups are blocked, and `localStorage` throws.

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Click **Japan** on the summary page
2. Pick **Open in Cohort Heatmap**
3. Read the Cohort Heatmap app: it opens with Country = Japan

## Other Drilling patterns

- [Drill down](hierarchy-drill.md): Click a region to see its countries, then customers, then their orders, and climb back with breadcrumbs.
- [Drill path](drill-path.md): Keep a trail of every step down and up, and click any step to go back to it.
- [Break down](adhoc-breakdown.md): Right-click a bar to split it by another field, like order status.
- [View underlying data](underlying-records.md): Click a column on a chart to see the individual orders behind it.
- [Row actions](row-actions.md): Put links on each table row: open the customer in your CRM, email them, or see their orders.

# Row actions

> Put links on each table row: open the customer in your CRM, email them, or see their orders.

- Pattern id: `row-actions`
- Category: Drilling (also Controls)
- Status: Works with app code: anfra supplies the queries, the app adds some logic
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#row-actions
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

Each row of the top-customers table has three actions. **Open in CRM** and **Email** use URLs built in AQL from the row, such as `https://crm.example.com/accounts/184`. **View orders** is an in-app URL: on Customer 184 it opens their latest orders, starting with #803 on 23 Aug 26 for $4,243.

Why: A table of customers is a to-do list. Actions take the reader from the number to the next step without copying IDs between tools.

## What to build

Each action's URL is a field built in AQL from the row's values. An outside link opens another tool; an in-app link sets a filter and shows another view.

Layout: A customer table with an Actions column, and the orders view an in-app action opens.

Instruction: Add row actions to a table in my Data App: links built from each row's fields, such as an Open in CRM URL, plus an in-app action that opens a filtered view.

Done when: Every row's links carry that row's values, and the in-app action shows only that row's records.

On the ecommerce sample: Customer 184's CRM link ends in /accounts/184, and View orders lists #803 first, on 23 Aug 26 for $4,243.

## AQL

Not run as written: each action's URL is a dimension, built in AQL from the row's fields.

```aql
dimension customers.crm_url = concat('https://crm.example.com/accounts/', cast(customers.id, 'text'));
dimension customers.email_url = concat('mailto:', customers.email, '?subject=Your%20order%20history');
explore { dimensions { customer_name: customers.name, crm_url: customers.crm_url, email_url: customers.email_url } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }
```

`concat` takes text only, so a number such as `customers.id` needs `cast(…, 'text')`. Defined in the Dataset, the URL field can be reused by every app.

## SDK wiring

```js
// the URLs come back as columns, one per action
const ACTIONS = [
  { key: 'crm_url', label: 'Open in CRM' },
  { key: 'email_url', label: 'Email' },
  { key: 'orders_url', label: 'View orders' }, // in-app
];
link.onclick = (e) => {
  e.preventDefault();
  const id = /customer=(\d+)/.exec(row.orders_url)[1];
  // number filter values are strings
  customer.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [id] });
  app.execute();
};
```

State it touches: Interaction mapping: each action is a URL field on the row. An in-app action turns into a filter condition; an outside one leaves the app.

## Notes

- Define `crm_url` once in the Dataset; every query and app can show it
- Limits: Works with app code: the URLs are AQL fields, but Data Apps run in a sandbox that allows scripts only, so links to other sites can't open a tab or leave the page. In-app actions work. A proposed host API, `Anfra.openUrl(url)` with an allowlist of domains, would open the rest.

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<style>
		.acts { display: flex; gap: 4px; justify-content: flex-end; }
		.acts a { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; height: 24px; padding: 0 8px; border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong); border-radius: 6px; font-size: 12px; color: var(--ink); text-decoration: none; white-space: nowrap; }
		.acts a:hover { border-color: var(--violet); color: var(--violet-ink); background: var(--violet-soft); }
		.acts a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--violet); outline-offset: 1px; }
		#last { font: 400 12px/16px 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; color: var(--violet-ink); min-height: 16px; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
		#orders[hidden] { display: none; }
	</style>
	<div class="app">
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Top customers · each row has actions</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div class="tw" id="tbl"></div></div>
		<div id="last" aria-live="polite"></div>
		<div class="panel" id="orders" hidden><div class="ph"><b id="ot"></b><span class="status" id="s2"></span></div><div class="tw" id="otbl"></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Row actions', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
// each action's URL is a field: built in AQL from the row's own values
const URLS = 'dimension customers.crm_url = concat(\'https://crm.example.com/accounts/\', cast(customers.id, \'text\'));\n'
	+ 'dimension customers.email_url = concat(\'mailto:\', customers.email, \'?subject=Your%20order%20history\');\n'
	+ 'dimension customers.orders_url = concat(\'#orders?customer=\', cast(customers.id, \'text\'));\n';
const top = app.createQuery('topCustomers', { dataset: 'ecommerce', pageSize: 8, aql: URLS + 'explore { dimensions { customer_name: customers.name, country_name: customers.country, crm_url: customers.crm_url, email_url: customers.email_url, orders_url: customers.orders_url } measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const orders = app.createQuery('orders', { dataset: 'ecommerce', pageSize: 6, aql: 'explore { dimensions { order_id: orders.id, ordered_on: orders.ordered_at, order_status: orders.status } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { ordered_on desc, order_id desc } }' });
const customer = app.createFilter('customer', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.id', label: 'Customer' });
app.mapControl(customer, orders, { field: 'customers.id' });
let who = null;
const ACTIONS = [
	{ key: 'crm_url', label: 'Open in CRM ↗', external: true },
	{ key: 'email_url', label: 'Email', external: true },
	{ key: 'orders_url', label: 'View orders →' },
];
// an in-app URL opens another view of this app; the id goes to the filter as a string
function go (url, r) {
	const m = /customer=(\d+)/.exec(url); if (!m) return;
	who = r.customer_name; customer.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [m[1]] }); app.execute();
}
const dd = (v) => { const x = new Date(String(v).slice(0, 10) + 'T00:00:00Z'); return x.getUTCDate() + ' ' + ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec'][x.getUTCMonth()] + ' ' + String(x.getUTCFullYear()).slice(2); };
function draw () {
	K.status(top, K.$('#s1'));
	if (top.result) {
		K.table(K.$('#tbl'), [{ key: 'customer_name', label: 'Customer' }, { key: 'country_name', label: 'Country' }, { key: 'num_orders', label: 'Orders', num: true }, { key: 'total_revenue', label: 'Revenue', num: true, fmt: (v) => K.money.format(v) }, { key: 'crm_url', label: 'Actions', num: true, fmt: () => '' }], top.result.rows);
		K.$('#tbl').querySelectorAll('tbody tr').forEach((tr, i) => {
			const r = top.result.rows[i], cell = tr.lastElementChild;
			const box = document.createElement('div'); box.className = 'acts';
			for (const a of ACTIONS) {
				const url = String(r[a.key] || ''), el = document.createElement('a');
				el.textContent = a.label; el.href = url; el.title = url;
								el.setAttribute('aria-label', a.label.replace(/[↗→]/g, '').trim() + ': ' + r.customer_name);
				el.onclick = (e) => { e.preventDefault(); if (a.external) K.$('#last').textContent = 'Opens ' + url + ' · blocked here: a sandboxed app can\'t open tabs or leave the page'; else { K.$('#last').textContent = 'Goes to ' + url; go(url, r); } };
				box.appendChild(el);
			}
			cell.replaceChildren(box);
		});
	}
	K.$('#orders').hidden = !who;
	if (who) {
		K.status(orders, K.$('#s2'));
		K.$('#ot').textContent = 'Latest orders from ' + who;
		if (orders.result) K.table(K.$('#otbl'), [{ key: 'order_id', label: 'Order', fmt: (v) => '#' + v }, { key: 'ordered_on', label: 'Date', fmt: dd }, { key: 'order_status', label: 'Status' }, { key: 'total_revenue', label: 'Revenue', num: true, fmt: (v) => K.money.format(v) }], orders.result.rows);
	}
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, who ? [top, orders] : [top]);
}
app.subscribe(draw);
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read the table: each customer row ends with **Open in CRM ↗**, **Email** and **View orders →**
2. Hover **Open in CRM** on Customer 184: its URL is `https://crm.example.com/accounts/184`, built in the query
3. Click it: the app shows the URL, and says the sandbox won't let it open a tab
4. Click **View orders →** on Customer 184: their latest orders open below, starting with **#803** on 23 Aug 26 for $4,243

# Dynamic metric

> Switch the chart between revenue, orders and units with one click.

- Pattern id: `metric-switch`
- Category: Tables & calculations (also Controls)
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#metric-switch
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader switches **Revenue → Units**. The bars reorder: Hardware leads on units (2,775, excluding cancelled orders), and Services leads on revenue. No query runs.

Why: Switching should feel instant. Fetching all three metrics once makes it renderer-only state.

## What to build

The page loads all the measures at once, so switching which one the chart shows only redraws and reorders the bars.

Layout: Segmented metric control above category bars that reorder.

Instruction: Add a switch for which number the chart shows, so the bars reorder instantly.

Done when: The bars reorder at once for each measure, the axis and labels follow it, and nothing new loads.

On the ecommerce sample: Services leads on Revenue; switching to Units puts Hardware first with 2,775 units with cancelled orders left out, and the count of queries run does not change.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { category: products.category }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count, units: units_sold }
  sorts { total_revenue desc }
}
```

Reader input the SDK sent:

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "field": "orders.status",
      "operator": "is_not",
      "values": [
        "cancelled"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Saved result:

| category | total_revenue | num_orders | units |
|---|---|---|---|
| Services | 467000.00 | 284 | 934 |
| Software | 397492.00 | 510 | 1808 |
| Hardware | 162100.74 | 718 | 2775 |
| Parts | 10586.75 | 490 | 1781 |

Orders by category add up to more than 1,500, because an order with two categories counts once in each.

## SDK wiring

```js
// one query returns revenue, orders, units
// no execute()
metricBtns.onclick = (e) => {
  metric = e.target.value;
  draw(byCategory.result, metric);
};
```

State it touches: Renderer-only: which metric is drawn. The analytical state doesn't change.

## Notes

- Return every metric in one `explore`, and switching becomes a redraw

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Metric</span><span class="seg" id="metrics"></span><span class="chips"><button type="button" id="nocancel" aria-pressed="true">Leave out cancelled</button></span></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>By category · <span id="mname">Revenue</span></b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="bars"></div>
		<div class="hint" id="runs"></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Dynamic metric', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const byCat = app.createQuery('byCategory', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { category_name: products.category } measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count, units: units_sold } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const status = app.createFilter('status', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'orders.status', label: 'Status' });
app.mapControl(status, byCat, { field: 'orders.status' });
const M = [{ k: 'total_revenue', l: 'Revenue', f: K.compact.format }, { k: 'num_orders', l: 'Orders', f: K.int.format }, { k: 'units', l: 'Units', f: K.int.format }];
let metric = M[0], runs = 0, was = '';
const seg = K.$('#metrics'), box = K.$('#bars'), nc = K.$('#nocancel');
const cancelled = () => { if (nc.getAttribute('aria-pressed') === 'true') status.setCondition({ operator: 'is_not', values: ['cancelled'] }); else status.reset(); };
cancelled();
nc.onclick = () => { nc.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(nc.getAttribute('aria-pressed') !== 'true')); cancelled(); app.execute(); };
// draw with an animated reorder: each bar slides from its old place, and grows from its old width
function draw () {
	if (!byCat.result) return;
	const old = new Map([...box.children].map((b) => [b.querySelector('.n').textContent, { top: b.getBoundingClientRect().top, w: b.querySelector('.f').style.width }]));
	const rows = [...byCat.result.rows].sort((a, b) => Number(b[metric.k]) - Number(a[metric.k]));
	K.bars(box, rows, { label: (r) => r.category_name, value: (r) => r[metric.k], fmt: metric.f });
	[...box.children].forEach((b) => {
		const o = old.get(b.querySelector('.n').textContent); if (!o) return;
		b.querySelector('.f').style.width = o.w;
		const dy = o.top - b.getBoundingClientRect().top;
		if (dy) b.animate([{ transform: 'translateY(' + dy + 'px)' }, { transform: 'none' }], { duration: 420, easing: 'cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)' });
	});
}
for (const m of M) { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = m.l; b.onclick = () => { metric = m; paint(); draw(); }; seg.appendChild(b); }
function paint () {
	seg.querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.textContent === metric.l)));
	K.$('#mname').textContent = metric.l;
	K.$('#runs').textContent = 'Queries run so far: ' + runs + '. Switching the metric only redraws';
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [byCat], () => ['metric → ' + metric.k + ' (drawn in the browser, not sent)']);
}
let drawnFor = null;
app.subscribe(() => {
	if (byCat.state === 'executing' && was !== 'executing') runs++;
	was = byCat.state;
	K.status(byCat, K.$('#s1'));
	if (byCat.result && byCat.result !== drawnFor) { drawnFor = byCat.result; draw(); }
	paint();
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read the bars on **Revenue**: Services leads
2. Click **Units**: the bars reorder and Hardware leads with 2,775 units, with **Leave out cancelled** on
3. Read the hint: the count of queries run does not change, because switching the metric only redraws

## Other Tables & calculations patterns

- [Dynamic dimension](dimension-switch.md): Switch how the chart groups data: by country, category or status.
- [Sort](sort.md): Click a column header to sort the table by that column.
- [Top N & Others](top-n.md): Show the top 3 countries and group the rest into "Others".
- [Pivot table](pivot.md): Countries down the side, categories across the top, and each cell's share of its row.
- [Subtotals & grand totals](totals.md): Add a total for each category and one for everything.
- [Percent of total](percent-of-total.md): Show each country's share of all revenue, like Australia at 24%.
- [Running total & moving calculation](cumulative-moving.md): Add a running total and a 3-month average to a monthly chart.
- [Indexed view](index-100.md): Start every line at 100, so growth compares fairly between big and small series.
- [Rank](ranking.md): Number each customer by revenue, overall and within their country.

# Dynamic dimension

> Switch how the chart groups data: by country, category or status.

- Pattern id: `dimension-switch`
- Category: Tables & calculations (also Drilling)
- Status: Works with app code: anfra supplies the queries, the app adds some logic
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#dimension-switch
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader switches **Group by: Country → Status**, and the bars rebuild with completed, shipped and cancelled.

Why: Let the reader decide how to slice the data, instead of building three charts.

## What to build

Picking a field in the Group by menu reruns the chart split by that field instead.

Layout: Dropdown + bars that rebuild.

Instruction: Add a "Group by" dropdown that changes what the chart's bars break down by.

Done when: The bars rebuild with the new field's values, and their total stays the same for every grouping.

On the ecommerce sample: Picking Status in Group by rebuilds the bars as completed, shipped and cancelled, and picking Category rebuilds them by category.

## AQL

Not run as written: three small queries, each like the "Percent of total" query.

```aql
// declare one query per allowed dimension, up front
explore { dimensions { key: customers.country }  measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }
explore { dimensions { key: products.category } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }
explore { dimensions { key: orders.status }     measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }
```

## SDK wiring

```js
const by = Object.fromEntries(
  DIMS.map((d) => [
    d.id,
    app.createQuery('by_' + d.id, {
      dataset: 'ecommerce',
      aql: aqlFor(d.ref),
    }),
  ]),
);
for (const q of Object.values(by))
  app.mapControl(country, q, { field: 'customers.country' });
// executes only the stale one
groupBy.onchange = () => {
  active = by[groupBy.value];
  app.execute();
};
```

## Notes

- Same alias in every query, so one renderer handles them all. `execute()` skips queries that are already fresh
- Limits: Works with app code. Declare each allowed dimension up front, and use the same alias (`key`) so the renderer stays the same.

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><label class="lbl" for="gb">Group by</label><select id="gb"></select><label class="lbl" for="ct">Country</label><select id="ct"><option value="">All countries</option></select></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by <span id="by">country</span></b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="bars"></div></div>
		<div class="hint">One query per option, declared up front with the same alias, so one renderer draws them all</div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Dynamic dimension', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const DIMS = [{ id: 'country', label: 'Country', ref: 'customers.country' }, { id: 'category', label: 'Category', ref: 'products.category' }, { id: 'status', label: 'Status', ref: 'orders.status' }];
const aqlFor = (ref) => 'explore { dimensions { key: ' + ref + ' } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }';
const by = Object.fromEntries(DIMS.map((d) => [d.id, app.createQuery('by_' + d.id, { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: aqlFor(d.ref) })]));
const country = app.createFilter('country', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.country', label: 'Country' });
for (const q of Object.values(by)) app.mapControl(country, q, { field: 'customers.country' });
const gb = K.$('#gb'), ct = K.$('#ct');
DIMS.forEach((d) => gb.add(new Option(d.label, d.id)));
country.loadOptions().then((vals) => vals.forEach((v) => ct.add(new Option(v, v))));
let active = by.country, ran = '';
gb.onchange = () => { active = by[gb.value]; const stale = active.isDirty || !active.result; ran = stale ? 'execute() ran ' + active.name : 'execute() skipped ' + active.name + ': already fresh'; draw(); app.execute(); };
ct.onchange = () => { if (ct.value) country.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [ct.value] }); else country.reset(); ran = ''; app.execute(); };
function draw () {
K.status(active, K.$('#s1'));
K.$('#by').textContent = DIMS.find((d) => by[d.id] === active).label.toLowerCase();
if (active.result) K.bars(K.$('#bars'), active.result.rows, { label: (r) => r.key, value: (r) => r.total_revenue, fmt: (v) => K.money.format(v) });
K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [active], () => ['showing ' + active.name + ' (alias key)', ran || null]);
}
app.subscribe(draw);
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read **Revenue by country** with **Group by** set to **Country**
2. Pick **Status** in **Group by**: the bars rebuild as completed, shipped and cancelled
3. Pick **Category** to see a third grouping

# Sort

> Click a column header to sort the table by that column.

- Pattern id: `sort`
- Category: Tables & calculations
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#sort
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader clicks the **Orders** header. The table re-sorts on the server, so page 2 continues the new order.

Why: A sort done in the browser on page 1 of 8 is wrong.

## What to build

Clicking a column header asks the server to sort by that column, and a second click flips the direction.

Layout: Table with sortable headers.

Instruction: Make the table sort by any column on a header click, with paging that keeps the sort.

Done when: Every page after the first continues the new sort, with no rows repeated or skipped.

On the ecommerce sample: Clicking the Orders header sorts most orders first, Load 25 more continues that order on page 2, and a second click flips it.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { customer: customers.name, country: customers.country }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count }
  filters { orders.status == 'completed' }
  sorts { total_revenue desc }
}
```

Reader input the SDK sent:

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "field": "customers.name",
      "operator": "contains",
      "values": [
        "customer 1"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "sorts": [
    {
      "field": "num_orders",
      "direction": "desc"
    }
  ]
}
```

Saved result:

| customer | country | total_revenue | num_orders |
|---|---|---|---|
| Customer 127 | Australia | 6832.78 | 10 |
| Customer 199 | United States | 8000.64 | 9 |
| Customer 14 | Australia | 7602.60 | 8 |
| Customer 101 | Singapore | 7600.60 | 8 |
| Customer 175 | Germany | 1770.03 | 8 |
| Customer 155 | Singapore | 7767.50 | 8 |
| Customer 15 | United States | 3074.15 | 8 |
| Customer 171 | Germany | 3119.01 | 8 |
| Customer 184 | Australia | 14270.00 | 7 |
| Customer 17 | Singapore | 7813.01 | 7 |
| Customer 18 | Singapore | 5743.48 | 7 |
| Customer 129 | Japan | 3052.50 | 7 |

(28 more rows)

The input's `sorts` replaces the AQL's own `sorts` for that run. `setSort([])` brings the AQL order back.

## SDK wiring

```js
th.onclick = () => {
  dir = dir === 'desc' ? 'asc' : 'desc';
  // a result column name
  table.setSort([{ field: th.dataset.col, direction: dir }]);
  app.execute();
};
```

## Notes

- `setSort` takes a result column name and doesn't change the AQL

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<style>#tbl tbody tr:nth-child(25n+1):not(:first-child) td { border-top: 2px solid var(--violet-faint); }</style>
	<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><span class="hint">Click a column header to sort on the server. Click it again to flip the direction</span><button type="button" id="reset" hidden>AQL order</button></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Customers, completed orders</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="tbl"></div>
		<div class="row" style="justify-content: space-between; margin-top: 8px"><span class="hint" id="foot"></span><button type="button" id="more">Load 25 more</button></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Sort', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const customers = app.createQuery('customers', { dataset: 'ecommerce', pageSize: 25,
	aql: 'explore { dimensions { customer_name: customers.name, country_name: customers.country } measures { total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count } filters { orders.status == \'completed\' } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const COLS = [
	{ key: 'n', label: '#', num: true, fixed: true },
	{ key: 'customer_name', label: 'Customer', first: 'asc' },
	{ key: 'country_name', label: 'Country', first: 'asc' },
	{ key: 'total_revenue', label: 'Revenue', num: true, first: 'desc', fmt: (v) => K.money.format(Number(v)) },
	{ key: 'num_orders', label: 'Orders', num: true, first: 'desc' },
];
let sort = null; // { field, direction } or null for the AQL's own order
const box = K.$('#tbl'), more = K.$('#more');
function sortBy (c) {
	if (c.fixed) return;
	const dir = sort && sort.field === c.key ? (sort.direction === 'desc' ? 'asc' : 'desc') : c.first;
	sort = { field: c.key, direction: dir };
	// the customer name breaks ties, so page 2 never repeats or skips a row
	customers.setSort(c.key === 'customer_name' ? [sort] : [sort, { field: 'customer_name', direction: 'asc' }]);
	box.dataset.top = '0';
	app.execute();
}
K.$('#reset').onclick = () => { sort = null; customers.setSort([]); app.execute(); };
more.onclick = () => { more.disabled = true; customers.fetchMore().catch(() => {}).finally(() => { more.disabled = false; }); };
app.subscribe(() => {
	K.status(customers, K.$('#s1'));
	K.$('#reset').hidden = !sort;
	if (customers.result) {
		const tw = box.querySelector('.tw'), top = box.dataset.top === '0' ? 0 : (tw ? tw.scrollTop : 0);
		delete box.dataset.top;
		const rows = customers.result.rows.map((r, i) => Object.assign({ n: i + 1 }, r));
		K.table(box, COLS.map((c) => Object.assign({}, c, { label: c.label + (sort && sort.field === c.key ? (sort.direction === 'desc' ? ' ▼' : ' ▲') : (!sort && c.key === 'total_revenue' ? ' ▽' : '')) })), rows);
		box.querySelectorAll('th').forEach((th, i) => { if (COLS[i].fixed) return; th.style.cursor = 'pointer'; th.tabIndex = 0; th.title = 'Sort by ' + COLS[i].label; th.onclick = () => sortBy(COLS[i]); th.onkeydown = (e) => { if (e.key === 'Enter') sortBy(COLS[i]); }; if (sort && sort.field === COLS[i].key) th.style.color = 'var(--violet-ink)'; });
		box.querySelector('.tw').scrollTop = top;
		K.$('#foot').textContent = rows.length + ' loaded · page ' + customers.page + (customers.hasMore ? '' : ' · all loaded');
		more.hidden = !customers.hasMore;
	}
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [customers], () => [sort ? 'sort → ' + customers.sort.map((s) => s.field + ' ' + s.direction).join(', ') : 'sort → none, the AQL\'s own (total_revenue desc)', 'page → ' + customers.page + ', 25 rows per page']);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read the table: it is sorted by **Revenue**, the AQL default
2. Click the **Orders** header: the server re-sorts by orders, most first
3. Click **Load 25 more**: page 2 continues the new order
4. Click **Orders** again to flip the direction, or **AQL order** to go back

# Top N & Others

> Show the top 3 countries and group the rest into "Others".

- Pattern id: `top-n`
- Category: Tables & calculations (also Scenarios & analyses)
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#top-n
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader picks **Top 3**: Australia, Singapore and Germany. An **Other** bar holds the remaining $509k, so the bars still add up to $1.28M.

Why: A Top N chart without "Other" quietly drops part of the total.

## What to build

Picking N from the menu keeps the N largest items and folds the rest into one Other bar.

Layout: Bars for the top N and an italic "Other" bar.

Instruction: Let the reader show only the top N items, with an "Other" bar for the rest.

Done when: The kept items are the largest, and the bars, Other included, still add up to the full total.

On the ecommerce sample: Top 3 keeps Australia, Singapore and Germany, an Other (3) bar holds $509k, and the bars still add up to $1.28M.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
metric top_3_countries = top(3, customers.country, by: revenue);
explore {
  dimensions { country: customers.country }
  measures {
    total_revenue: revenue,
    all_countries: revenue | exclude_grains(customers.country),
  }
  filters { customers.country in top_3_countries }
  sorts { total_revenue desc }
}
```

Saved result:

| country | total_revenue | all_countries |
|---|---|---|
| Australia | 313397.48 | 1283052.95 |
| Singapore | 255030.20 | 1283052.95 |
| Germany | 205890.48 | 1283052.95 |

A single "Top 3 or Other" dimension doesn't work yet: `case(when: country in top_3 …)` crashed the compiler, and a dimensionalized rank came back as 1 on every row. The N lives in the AQL text, so a reader-chosen N is a new query, or a dataset metric for the rank.

## SDK wiring

```js
// n from a fixed menu: 3, 5, 10
function topN(n) {
  const q = app.createQuery('top' + n, {
    dataset: 'ecommerce',
    aql: topAql(n),
  });
  app.mapControl(status, q, { field: 'orders.status' });
  return app.execute().then(() => {
    const rows = q.result.rows,
      total = Number(rows[0].all_countries);
    return [
      ...rows,
      {
        country: 'Other',
        total_revenue:
          total -
          rows.reduce((a, r) => a + Number(r.total_revenue), 0),
      },
    ];
  });
}
```

## Notes

- `top(3, customers.country, by: revenue)` in the filters, plus an `exclude_grains` total

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Show</span><span class="seg" id="ns"></span><label class="lbl" for="status">Status</label><select id="status"><option value="">Any status</option></select></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b id="title">Revenue by country</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="bars"></div>
		<div class="hint" id="sum"></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Top N & Others', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const status = app.createFilter('status', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'orders.status', label: 'Status' });
const MEASURES = ' measures { total_revenue: revenue, all_countries: revenue | exclude_grains(customers.country), n_countries: count_distinct(customers.country) | exclude_grains(customers.country) }';
// N is part of the AQL text, so each choice from the menu is its own query, declared the first time it is picked
const aqlFor = (n) => n ? 'metric top_countries = top(' + n + ', customers.country, by: revenue); explore { dimensions { country_name: customers.country }' + MEASURES + ' filters { customers.country in top_countries } sorts { total_revenue desc } }'
	: 'explore { dimensions { country_name: customers.country }' + MEASURES + ' sorts { total_revenue desc } }';
const Q = {};
const queryFor = (n) => { if (!Q[n]) { Q[n] = app.createQuery(n ? 'top' + n : 'allCountries', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: aqlFor(n) }); app.mapControl(status, Q[n], { field: 'orders.status' }); } return Q[n]; };
let n = 3, q = queryFor(3);
const seg = K.$('#ns'), sel = K.$('#status');
for (const x of [3, 5, 0]) { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = x ? 'Top ' + x : 'All'; b.dataset.n = x; b.onclick = () => { n = x; q = queryFor(x); draw(); app.execute(); }; seg.appendChild(b); }
status.loadOptions().then((vals) => vals.forEach((v) => sel.add(new Option(v[0].toUpperCase() + v.slice(1), v))));
sel.onchange = () => { if (sel.value) status.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [sel.value] }); else status.reset(); app.execute(); };
function draw () {
	seg.querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(Number(b.dataset.n) === n)));
	K.status(q, K.$('#s1'));
	K.$('#title').textContent = n ? 'Top ' + n + ' countries by revenue, and Other' : 'Revenue, all countries';
	if (q.result && q.result.rows.length) {
		const rows = q.result.rows.map((r) => ({ name: r.country_name, v: Number(r.total_revenue) }));
		const total = Number(q.result.rows[0].all_countries), rest = Number(q.result.rows[0].n_countries) - rows.length;
		const shown = rows.reduce((t, r) => t + r.v, 0);
		if (n && rest > 0) rows.push({ name: 'Other (' + rest + ')', v: total - shown, other: true });
		K.bars(K.$('#bars'), rows, { label: (r) => r.name, value: (r) => r.v });
		const last = K.$('#bars').lastElementChild;
		if (rows[rows.length - 1].other && last) { last.querySelector('.n').style.fontStyle = 'italic'; last.querySelector('.f').style.background = 'rgb(24 20 31 / 0.32)'; }
		K.$('#sum').textContent = (n && rest > 0 ? 'Other = all countries ' + K.compact.format(total) + ' − top ' + n + ' ' + K.compact.format(shown) + '. ' : '') + 'The bars add up to ' + K.compact.format(total);
	} else if (q.result) { K.$('#bars').textContent = ''; K.$('#sum').textContent = 'No orders match'; }
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [q], () => [n ? 'N → ' + n + ', in the AQL text: top(' + n + ', customers.country, by: revenue)' : 'N → all, no top() filter']);
}
app.subscribe(draw);
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Click **All** to see all 6 countries
2. Click **Top 3**: Australia, Singapore and Germany stay
3. Read the **Other (3)** bar: it holds the remaining $509k
4. Read the hint under the bars: they still add up to $1.28M

# Pivot table

> Countries down the side, categories across the top, and each cell's share of its row.

- Pattern id: `pivot`
- Category: Tables & calculations
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#pivot
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The pivot shows countries down the side and categories across the top. A toggle switches the cells to **% of country**: Services is 46% of Australia.

Why: A pivot is how a spreadsheet user reads a breakdown.

## What to build

Rows and columns each come from a field, and the toggle switches cells from values to each row's percent split.

Layout: Heatmap-style pivot table with a $ / % toggle.

Instruction: Add a pivot table with a toggle between values and each row's percent split.

Done when: In percent mode each row adds up to 100%, and switching back shows the same values as before.

On the ecommerce sample: On % of country each row adds up to 100% and Services is 46% of Australia; % of category makes each column add up instead.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions {
    rows { country: customers.country }
    columns { category: products.category }
  }
  measures {
    total_revenue: revenue,
    share_of_country: percent_of_total(revenue, 'row_total'),
  }
}
```

Saved result:

| country | category | total_revenue | share_of_country | __column_header__ | __pivot_row__ | __pivot_column__ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|  | Hardware |  |  | 1 | 0 | 1 |
|  | Parts |  |  | 1 | 0 | 2 |
|  | Services |  |  | 1 | 0 | 3 |
|  | Software |  |  | 1 | 0 | 4 |
| Australia | Hardware | 41112.53 | 0.13118334582652036 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| Australia | Parts | 3356.95 | 0.010711477322663858 | 0 | 1 | 2 |
| Australia | Services | 143500.00 | 0.45788498363164887 | 0 | 1 | 3 |
| Australia | Software | 125428.00 | 0.40022019321916696 | 0 | 1 | 4 |
| Germany | Hardware | 34581.38 | 0.16796007275324237 | 0 | 2 | 1 |
| Germany | Parts | 2073.10 | 0.010068945392715583 | 0 | 2 | 2 |
| Germany | Services | 104000.00 | 0.50512291777648 | 0 | 2 | 3 |
| Germany | Software | 65236.00 | 0.316848064077562 | 0 | 2 | 4 |

(16 more rows)

The result includes header rows, marked by `__pivot_row__` and `__pivot_column__`. `percent_of_total` returns a fraction (0.458), so format it as a percentage.

## SDK wiring

```js
// no pageSize
const pivot = app.createQuery('pivot', {
  dataset: 'ecommerce',
  aql: PIVOT_AQL,
});
const cells = pivot.result.rows.filter(
  (r) => r.__column_header__ === '0',
);
```

## Notes

- `rows { }` and `columns { }` inside `dimensions`. Shares use `percent_of_total`

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Cells show</span><span class="seg" id="modes"></span></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b id="title">Revenue, country × category</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="grid"></div>
		<div class="hint" id="note"></div><div class="hint">App code: the browser lays out a flat query as the grid, because a rows { } columns { } query fails in the SDK today</div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Pivot table', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const pivot = app.createQuery('pivot', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { country_name: customers.country, category_name: products.category } measures { total_revenue: revenue, share_of_country: revenue * 1.0 / (revenue | exclude_grains(products.category)), share_of_category: revenue * 1.0 / (revenue | exclude_grains(customers.country)) } sorts { country_name asc, category_name asc } }' });
const MODES = [
	{ k: 'total_revenue', l: '$', t: 'Revenue, country × category', f: (v) => K.compact.format(v), note: 'Each cell is one country and one category' },
	{ k: 'share_of_country', l: '% of country', t: 'Share of each country\'s revenue', f: (v) => (v * 100).toFixed(0) + '%', note: 'Each row adds up to 100%: revenue / (revenue | exclude_grains(products.category))' },
	{ k: 'share_of_category', l: '% of category', t: 'Share of each category\'s revenue', f: (v) => (v * 100).toFixed(0) + '%', note: 'Each column adds up to 100%: revenue / (revenue | exclude_grains(customers.country))' },
];
let mode = MODES[0];
const seg = K.$('#modes');
for (const m of MODES) { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = m.l; b.onclick = () => { mode = m; draw(); }; seg.appendChild(b); }
function draw () {
	seg.querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.textContent === mode.l)));
	K.$('#title').textContent = mode.t; K.$('#note').textContent = mode.note;
	K.status(pivot, K.$('#s1'));
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [pivot], () => ['cells → ' + mode.k + ' (drawn in the browser, not sent)']);
	if (!pivot.result) return;
	const cells = pivot.result.rows;
	// the query is flat; the browser lays it out as countries down, categories across
	const rows = [...new Set(cells.map((r) => r.country_name))], cols = [...new Set(cells.map((r) => r.category_name))];
	const at = (c, k) => cells.find((r) => r.country_name === c && r.category_name === k);
	const vals = cells.map((r) => Number(r[mode.k]) || 0), max = Math.max(...vals, 1e-9);
	let h = '<div class="tw"><table><thead><tr><th>Country</th>' + cols.map((k) => '<th class="num">' + K.esc(k) + '</th>').join('') + '</tr></thead><tbody>';
	for (const c of rows) {
		h += '<tr><td>' + K.esc(c) + '</td>' + cols.map((k) => { const r = at(c, k); if (!r) return '<td class="num">–</td>'; const v = Number(r[mode.k]), a = Math.sqrt(v / max);
			return '<td class="num" title="' + K.esc(c + ' · ' + k + ': ' + K.money.format(Number(r.total_revenue)) + ', ' + (r.share_of_country * 100).toFixed(1) + '% of ' + c + ', ' + (r.share_of_category * 100).toFixed(1) + '% of ' + k) + '" style="background: rgb(138 81 212 / ' + (0.06 + a * 0.7).toFixed(2) + '); color: ' + (a > 0.86 ? '#fff' : 'var(--ink)') + '; border: 2px solid #fff">' + mode.f(v) + '</td>'; }).join('') + '</tr>';
	}
	K.$('#grid').innerHTML = h + '</tbody></table></div>';
}
app.subscribe(draw);
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read the grid on **$**: countries down the side, categories across the top
2. Click **% of country**: each row now adds up to 100%
3. Read the **Australia** row: **Services** is 46% of Australia
4. Click **% of category** to make each column add up to 100% instead

# Subtotals & grand totals

> Add a total for each category and one for everything.

- Pattern id: `totals`
- Category: Tables & calculations
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#totals
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The product table shows each product's revenue, its **category subtotal** and its **share of category**. Gizmo is 61% of Hardware. The grand total is $1.28M.

Why: Totals that come from the same query always add up.

## What to build

Rows sit under one subtotal row per group, each shows its share of the group, and a grand total ends the table.

Layout: Grouped table with subtotal rows.

Instruction: Group the table rows under subtotal rows, with each row's share of its group and a grand total.

Done when: Each subtotal equals the sum of its rows, shares within a group add up to 100%, and the grand total matches.

On the ecommerce sample: Gizmo shows 61% of Hardware, the Hardware subtotal sits under its products, and the grand total reads $1.28M.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { category: products.category, product: products.name }
  measures {
    total_revenue: revenue,
    category_total: revenue | exclude_grains(products.name),
    grand_total: revenue | exclude_grains(products.category, products.name),
    share_in_category: revenue * 100.0 / (revenue | exclude_grains(products.name)),
  }
  sorts { category asc, total_revenue desc }
}
```

Saved result:

| category | product | total_revenue | category_total | grand_total | share_in_category |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hardware | Gizmo | 118701.00 | 193999.60 | 1283052.95 | 61.186208631358 |
| Hardware | Gadget | 53509.50 | 193999.60 | 1283052.95 | 27.582273365512094 |
| Hardware | Widget | 21789.10 | 193999.60 | 1283052.95 | 11.231518003129903 |
| Parts | Flange | 8478.60 | 13659.35 | 1283052.95 | 62.07176769026344 |
| Parts | Sprocket | 5180.75 | 13659.35 | 1283052.95 | 37.92823230973655 |
| Services | Support Plan | 578000.00 | 578000.00 | 1283052.95 | 100 |
| Software | Analytics Pro | 321425.00 | 497394.00 | 1283052.95 | 64.62180886781907 |
| Software | Dashboard Kit | 175969.00 | 497394.00 | 1283052.95 | 35.37819113218093 |

## SDK wiring

```js
// render subtotal rows when category changes; grand_total is on
// every row
const rows = totals.result.rows;
```

## Notes

- `revenue | exclude_grains(products.name)` is "revenue for the whole category", and it follows the filters

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<style>#tbl .tw { max-height: 300px; } #tbl td { padding: 3px 6px; } tr.sub td { font-weight: 600; background: var(--sunken); } tr.grand td { font-weight: 600; border-top: 2px solid var(--ink); border-bottom: 0; position: sticky; bottom: 0; background: #fff; } td.ind { padding-left: 18px; }</style>
	<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><label class="lbl" for="country">Country</label><select id="country"><option value="">All countries</option></select><span class="hint">Subtotals, shares and the total all follow the filter</span></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by product, with category subtotals</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="tbl"></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Subtotals & grand totals', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const totals = app.createQuery('totals', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { category_name: products.category, product_name: products.name } measures { total_revenue: revenue, category_total: revenue | exclude_grains(products.name), grand_total: revenue | exclude_grains(products.category, products.name), share_in_category: revenue * 100.0 / (revenue | exclude_grains(products.name)) } sorts { category_name asc, total_revenue desc } }' });
const country = app.createFilter('country', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.country', label: 'Country' });
app.mapControl(country, totals, { field: 'customers.country' });
const sel = K.$('#country');
country.loadOptions().then((vals) => vals.forEach((v) => sel.add(new Option(v, v))));
sel.onchange = () => { if (sel.value) country.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [sel.value] }); else country.reset(); app.execute(); };
const m = (v) => K.money.format(Number(v));
app.subscribe(() => {
	K.status(totals, K.$('#s1'));
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [totals]);
	if (!totals.result) return;
	const rows = totals.result.rows;
	let h = '<div class="tw"><table><thead><tr><th>Product</th><th class="num">Revenue</th><th class="num">Share of category</th><th class="num">Share of all</th></tr></thead><tbody>';
	const sub = (r) => '<tr class="sub"><td>' + K.esc(r.category_name) + ' subtotal</td><td class="num">' + m(r.category_total) + '</td><td class="num">100%</td><td class="num">' + (r.category_total / r.grand_total * 100).toFixed(1) + '%</td></tr>';
	rows.forEach((r, i) => {
		h += '<tr><td class="ind">' + K.esc(r.product_name) + ' <span class="hint">' + K.esc(r.category_name) + '</span></td><td class="num">' + m(r.total_revenue) + '</td><td class="num">' + Number(r.share_in_category).toFixed(0) + '%</td><td class="num">' + (r.total_revenue / r.grand_total * 100).toFixed(1) + '%</td></tr>';
		if (!rows[i + 1] || rows[i + 1].category_name !== r.category_name) h += sub(r);
	});
	h += '</tbody><tfoot>';
	if (rows[0]) h += '<tr class="grand"><td>Grand total</td><td class="num">' + m(rows[0].grand_total) + '</td><td></td><td class="num">100%</td></tr>';
	K.$('#tbl').innerHTML = h + '</tfoot></table></div>';
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read the **Share of category** column: **Gizmo** is 61% of Hardware
2. Read the **Hardware subtotal** row under the Hardware products
3. Read the **Grand total** row at the bottom: $1,283,053, or $1.28M
4. Pick a country in **Country**: the subtotals, shares and total all follow

# Percent of total

> Show each country's share of all revenue, like Australia at 24%.

- Pattern id: `percent-of-total`
- Category: Tables & calculations
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#percent-of-total
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

Each country bar is labelled with its share. Australia has 24.4% and Japan 9.2%. Filtering to Software changes the shares.

Why: Shares are easier to compare than raw sums.

## What to build

Each bar's value is divided by the total for the current filters, so the labels change when a filter changes.

Layout: Bars with % labels.

Instruction: Label each bar with its share of the total, following the page's filters.

Done when: The share labels add up to 100% under any filter, and each matches the bar's value over the total.

On the ecommerce sample: Australia reads 24.4% and Japan 9.2%; filtering to Software changes the shares, and they still add up to 100%.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { country: customers.country }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue, share: percent_of_total(revenue, 'grand_total') }
  sorts { total_revenue desc }
}
```

Saved result:

| country | total_revenue | share |
|---|---|---|
| Australia | 313397.48 | 0.24425919444711927 |
| Singapore | 255030.20 | 0.19876825816113047 |
| Germany | 205890.48 | 0.16046919965384127 |
| United States | 205153.71 | 0.15989496770183959 |
| Vietnam | 185254.77 | 0.14438591174276946 |
| Japan | 118326.31 | 0.09222246829329998 |

Found while checking: the result is a fraction (0.244). The reference describes a value from 0 to 100.

## SDK wiring

```js
// Intl.NumberFormat({ style: 'percent' })
label: (r) => pct.format(Number(r.share));
```

## Notes

- A built-in function with row, column and grand totals

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<style>#bars .b { grid-template-columns: 100px minmax(0, 1fr) 116px; } #bars .v b { color: var(--ink); font-weight: 600; }</style>
	<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Category</span><span class="chips" id="cats"></span></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Share of <span id="of">all revenue</span> by country</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="bars"></div>
		<div class="hint" id="sum"></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Percent of total', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const shares = app.createQuery('shares', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { country_name: customers.country } measures { total_revenue: revenue, share: percent_of_total(revenue, \'grand_total\') } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const cat = app.createFilter('category', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'products.category', label: 'Category' });
app.mapControl(cat, shares, { field: 'products.category' });
const pct = new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', { style: 'percent', minimumFractionDigits: 1, maximumFractionDigits: 1 });
let picked = '';
const chips = K.$('#cats');
const chip = (v, l) => { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = l; b.dataset.v = v; b.onclick = () => { picked = v; if (v) cat.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [v] }); else cat.reset(); app.execute(); }; chips.appendChild(b); };
chip('', 'All');
cat.loadOptions().then((vals) => vals.forEach((v) => chip(v, v)));
app.subscribe(() => {
	chips.querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.dataset.v === picked)));
	K.status(shares, K.$('#s1'));
	K.$('#of').textContent = picked ? picked + ' revenue' : 'all revenue';
	if (shares.result) {
		const rows = shares.result.rows;
		K.bars(K.$('#bars'), rows, { label: (r) => r.country_name, value: (r) => r.share });
		[...K.$('#bars').children].forEach((b, i) => { b.querySelector('.v').innerHTML = '<b>' + pct.format(Number(rows[i].share)) + '</b> · ' + K.compact.format(Number(rows[i].total_revenue)); });
		const sum = rows.reduce((t, r) => t + Number(r.share), 0), tot = rows.reduce((t, r) => t + Number(r.total_revenue), 0);
		K.$('#sum').textContent = 'Shares add up to ' + pct.format(sum) + ' of ' + K.compact.format(tot) + (rows[0] ? ' · the query returns ' + Number(rows[0].share).toFixed(3) + ', shown as ' + pct.format(Number(rows[0].share)) : '');
	}
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [shares]);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read the share on each bar: **Australia** has 24.4% and **Japan** 9.2%
2. Click **Software** next to **Category**: the shares change, and still add up to 100%
3. Click **All** to go back

# Running total & moving calculation

> Add a running total and a 3-month average to a monthly chart.

- Pattern id: `cumulative-moving`
- Category: Tables & calculations (also Dates & time)
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#cumulative-moving
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

Toggles add a **running total** line and a **3-month moving average** over the monthly bars.

Why: Readers ask two questions here: "are we on track?" and "is it trending?"

## What to build

Each toggle adds a line over the bars: one keeps a running sum, the other averages each period with the two before.

Layout: Columns with two overlay lines.

Instruction: Add toggles for a running total and a 3-period moving average on the trend.

Done when: The running total's last point equals the sum of all bars, and the average line is smoother than the bars.

On the ecommerce sample: The running total climbs over the monthly bars on its own scale, and hovering a month shows its revenue, 3-month average and running total.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() }
  measures {
    total_revenue: revenue,
    cumulative: revenue | running_total(orders.ordered_at),
    avg_3m: window_avg(revenue, -2..0, order: orders.ordered_at | month()),
  }
  sorts { period asc }
}
```

Saved result:

| period | total_revenue | cumulative | avg_3m |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-06-01 | 97537.24 | 97537.24 | 97537.24 |
| 2025-07-01 | 66278.66 | 163815.90 | 81907.95 |
| 2025-08-01 | 70722.63 | 234538.53 | 78179.51 |
| 2025-09-01 | 94775.86 | 329314.39 | 77259.05 |
| 2025-10-01 | 85563.86 | 414878.25 | 83687.45 |
| 2025-11-01 | 74836.51 | 489714.76 | 85058.74333333333 |
| 2025-12-01 | 65537.03 | 555251.79 | 75312.46666666666 |
| 2026-01-01 | 82610.21 | 637862.00 | 74327.91666666667 |
| 2026-02-01 | 86602.09 | 724464.09 | 78249.77666666667 |
| 2026-03-01 | 61464.65 | 785928.74 | 76892.31666666667 |
| 2026-04-01 | 77023.03 | 862951.77 | 75029.92333333334 |
| 2026-05-01 | 88378.49 | 951330.26 | 75622.05666666667 |

(4 more rows)

## SDK wiring

```js
// one query, three measures; the toggles only redraw
```

## Notes

- `running_total` and `window_avg` with a range such as `-2..0`

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<style>#chart svg { display: block; overflow: visible; } #chart text { font-size: 12px; fill: var(--muted); } .key { display: inline-block; width: 14px; height: 0; border-top: 2px solid; vertical-align: 4px; margin-right: 4px; }</style>
	<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Overlay</span><span class="chips"><button type="button" id="tRun" aria-pressed="false"><i class="key" style="border-color: var(--ink)"></i>Running total</button><button type="button" id="tAvg" aria-pressed="false"><i class="key" style="border-color: var(--violet-ink); border-top-style: dashed"></i>3-month average</button></span></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Monthly revenue</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="chart"></div>
		<div class="hint" id="read"></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Running total & moving average', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const q = app.createQuery('monthly', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() } measures { total_revenue: revenue, cumulative: revenue | running_total(orders.ordered_at), avg_3m: window_avg(revenue, -2..0, order: orders.ordered_at | month()) } sorts { period asc } }' });
const on = { run: false, avg: false };
let hover = -1;
const mon = (v) => new Date(v).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', year: '2-digit', timeZone: 'UTC' });
const tog = (id, k) => { const b = K.$(id); b.onclick = () => { on[k] = !on[k]; b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(on[k])); draw(); }; };
tog('#tRun', 'run'); tog('#tAvg', 'avg');
function draw () {
	K.status(q, K.$('#s1'));
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [q], () => ['overlays → ' + (['running total', '3-month average'].filter((x, i) => on[i ? 'avg' : 'run']).join(' + ') || 'none') + ' (drawn in the browser, the query already returned all three)']);
	if (!q.result) return;
	const rows = q.result.rows, n = rows.length;
	const W = K.$('#chart').clientWidth, H = 170, L = 40, R = on.run ? 46 : 8, T = 6, B = 20, w = W - L - R, h = H - T - B;
	const rev = rows.map((r) => Number(r.total_revenue)), avg = rows.map((r) => Number(r.avg_3m)), cum = rows.map((r) => Number(r.cumulative));
	const nice = (v) => { const p = Math.pow(10, Math.floor(Math.log10(v))), m = v / p; return (m <= 1 ? 1 : m <= 2 ? 2 : m <= 2.5 ? 2.5 : m <= 5 ? 5 : 10) * p; };
	const max = nice(Math.max(...rev, ...avg)), cmax = nice(Math.max(...cum));
	const step = w / n, x = (i) => L + step * i + step / 2, y = (v) => T + h - v / max * h, yc = (v) => T + h - v / cmax * h;
	const path = (vals, f) => vals.map((v, i) => (i ? 'L' : 'M') + x(i).toFixed(1) + ' ' + f(v).toFixed(1)).join(' ');
	let s = '<svg width="' + W + '" height="' + H + '">';
	for (const t of [0, 0.5, 1]) s += '<line x1="' + L + '" x2="' + (W - R) + '" y1="' + y(max * t) + '" y2="' + y(max * t) + '" stroke="var(--rule)"/><text x="' + (L - 4) + '" y="' + (y(max * t) + 4) + '" text-anchor="end">' + K.compact.format(max * t) + '</text>';
	if (on.run) for (const t of [0, 0.5, 1]) s += '<text x="' + (W - R + 4) + '" y="' + (yc(cmax * t) + 4) + '" style="fill: var(--ink)">' + K.compact.format(cmax * t) + '</text>';
	rev.forEach((v, i) => { s += '<rect x="' + (x(i) - step * 0.38).toFixed(1) + '" width="' + (step * 0.76).toFixed(1) + '" y="' + y(v).toFixed(1) + '" height="' + (T + h - y(v)).toFixed(1) + '" rx="2" fill="' + (i === hover ? 'var(--violet)' : (on.run || on.avg ? 'var(--violet-faint)' : 'var(--violet)')) + '"/>'; });
	if (on.avg) s += '<path d="' + path(avg, y) + '" fill="none" stroke="var(--violet-ink)" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="5 3"/>';
	if (on.run) s += '<path d="' + path(cum, yc) + '" fill="none" stroke="var(--ink)" stroke-width="2"/>' + '<circle cx="' + x(n - 1) + '" cy="' + yc(cum[n - 1]) + '" r="3" fill="var(--ink)"/>';
	s += '<text x="' + x(0) + '" y="' + (H - 4) + '" text-anchor="middle">' + mon(rows[0].period) + '</text><text x="' + x(n - 1) + '" y="' + (H - 4) + '" text-anchor="middle">' + mon(rows[n - 1].period) + '</text>';
	rows.forEach((r, i) => { s += '<rect data-i="' + i + '" x="' + (L + step * i) + '" width="' + step + '" y="' + T + '" height="' + h + '" fill="transparent"/>'; });
	K.$('#chart').innerHTML = s + '</svg>';
	K.$('#chart').querySelectorAll('rect[data-i]').forEach((el) => { el.onmouseenter = () => { const i = Number(el.dataset.i); if (i !== hover) { hover = i; draw(); } }; });
	K.$('#chart svg').onmouseleave = () => { if (hover !== -1) { hover = -1; draw(); } };
	const i = hover < 0 ? n - 1 : hover;
	K.$('#read').textContent = mon(rows[i].period) + ': revenue ' + K.money.format(rev[i]) + (on.avg ? ' · 3-month average ' + K.money.format(avg[i]) : '') + (on.run ? ' · running total ' + K.money.format(cum[i]) : '') + (hover < 0 && !on.run && !on.avg ? ' · hover a month' : '');
}
app.subscribe(draw);
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Click **Running total**: a line climbs over the bars, on its own scale at the right
2. Click **3-month average**: a dashed line smooths the monthly bars
3. Hover a month to read its revenue, 3-month average and running total under the chart

## Other Tables & calculations patterns

- [Dynamic metric](metric-switch.md): Switch the chart between revenue, orders and units with one click.
- [Dynamic dimension](dimension-switch.md): Switch how the chart groups data: by country, category or status.
- [Sort](sort.md): Click a column header to sort the table by that column.
- [Top N & Others](top-n.md): Show the top 3 countries and group the rest into "Others".
- [Pivot table](pivot.md): Countries down the side, categories across the top, and each cell's share of its row.
- [Subtotals & grand totals](totals.md): Add a total for each category and one for everything.
- [Percent of total](percent-of-total.md): Show each country's share of all revenue, like Australia at 24%.
- [Indexed view](index-100.md): Start every line at 100, so growth compares fairly between big and small series.
- [Rank](ranking.md): Number each customer by revenue, overall and within their country.
