# Indexed view

> Start every line at 100, so growth compares fairly between big and small series.

- Pattern id: `index-100`
- Category: Tables & calculations (also Dates & time)
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#index-100
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The lines switch from dollars to an index. Parts (worth a few hundred dollars a month) and Services (worth tens of thousands) now share one scale. Parts ends at 84.

Why: Comparing growth across series of very different sizes is hard in raw units.

## What to build

Clicking the Index toggle divides each line by its own first value, so every line starts at 100 on one scale.

Layout: Four category lines, rebased.

Instruction: Rebase every line to 100 at its first period, so series of very different sizes compare on one scale.

Done when: Every line starts at 100 in the first period, and switching back shows the original values unchanged.

On the ecommerce sample: After clicking Index, every category starts at 100 in Jun 25 on one shared scale, and Parts ends at 84 in Sep 26.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month(), category: products.category }
  measures {
    total_revenue: revenue,
    index_100: revenue * 100.0 / first_value(revenue, order: orders.ordered_at | month(), partition: products.category),
  }
  sorts { category asc, period asc }
}
```

Saved result:

| period | category | total_revenue | index_100 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-06-01 | Hardware | 13004.19 | 100 |
| 2025-07-01 | Hardware | 12268.36 | 94.34159297887834 |
| 2025-08-01 | Hardware | 10002.78 | 76.91966973721546 |
| 2025-09-01 | Hardware | 14003.71 | 107.68613808318703 |
| 2025-10-01 | Hardware | 11678.16 | 89.80305578432797 |
| 2025-11-01 | Hardware | 12913.76 | 99.30460874533516 |
| 2025-12-01 | Hardware | 9702.93 | 74.61387445123457 |
| 2026-01-01 | Hardware | 12172.21 | 93.60221590118262 |
| 2026-02-01 | Hardware | 12057.99 | 92.72388360982114 |
| 2026-03-01 | Hardware | 10655.80 | 81.94128200218545 |
| 2026-04-01 | Hardware | 9702.93 | 74.61387445123457 |
| 2026-05-01 | Hardware | 12605.34 | 96.93291162309994 |

(28 more rows)

## SDK wiring

```js
unitToggle.onchange = () =>
  draw(
    q.result,
    unitToggle.value === 'index' ? 'index_100' : 'revenue',
  );
```

## Notes

- `first_value` with `partition`, in one measure

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<style>#chart svg { display: block; overflow: visible; } #chart text { font-size: 12px; fill: var(--muted); } #lg button { height: 28px; padding: 0 10px; border-radius: 999px; font-size: 12px; } #lg i { display: inline-block; width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 2px; margin-right: 6px; vertical-align: -1px; }</style>
	<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Units</span><span class="seg" id="units"></span></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b id="title">Revenue by category</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="chart"></div>
		<div class="row" id="lg" style="margin-top: 6px"></div><div class="hint" id="read" style="margin-top: 4px"></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Indexed view', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const q = app.createQuery('byCategory', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month(), category_name: products.category } measures { total_revenue: revenue, index_100: revenue * 100.0 / first_value(revenue, order: orders.ordered_at | month(), partition: products.category) } sorts { category_name asc, period asc } }' });
const COLORS = { Services: '#8a51d4', Software: '#18141f', Hardware: '#1d7f74', Parts: '#c2410c' };
const UNITS = [{ k: 'total_revenue', l: '$', t: 'Revenue by category', f: (v) => K.compact.format(v) }, { k: 'index_100', l: 'Index (first month = 100)', t: 'Index by category, Jun 25 = 100', f: (v) => Math.round(v) }];
let unit = UNITS[0], focus = null, hover = -1;
const seg = K.$('#units');
for (const u of UNITS) { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = u.l; b.onclick = () => { unit = u; draw(); }; seg.appendChild(b); }
const mon = (v) => new Date(v).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', year: '2-digit', timeZone: 'UTC' });
function draw () {
	seg.querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.textContent === unit.l)));
	K.$('#title').textContent = unit.t;
	K.status(q, K.$('#s1'));
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [q], () => ['units → ' + unit.k + ' (drawn in the browser, the query returned both)']);
	if (!q.result) return;
	const rows = q.result.rows;
	const months = [...new Set(rows.map((r) => r.period))].sort(), cats = Object.keys(COLORS).filter((c) => rows.some((r) => r.category_name === c));
	const val = (c, m) => { const r = rows.find((x) => x.category_name === c && x.period === m); return r ? Number(r[unit.k]) : null; };
	const all = rows.map((r) => Number(r[unit.k]));
	const nice = (v) => { const p = Math.pow(10, Math.floor(Math.log10(v))), m = v / p; return (m <= 1 ? 1 : m <= 2 ? 2 : m <= 2.5 ? 2.5 : m <= 5 ? 5 : 10) * p; };
	const idx = unit.k === 'index_100', lo = idx ? Math.floor(Math.min(...all, 100) / 20) * 20 : 0, hi = idx ? Math.ceil(Math.max(...all) / 20) * 20 : nice(Math.max(...all));
	const W = K.$('#chart').clientWidth, H = 170, L = 40, R = 112, T = 6, B = 20, w = W - L - R, h = H - T - B;
	const x = (i) => L + w * i / (months.length - 1), y = (v) => T + h - (v - lo) / (hi - lo) * h;
	let s = '<svg width="' + W + '" height="' + H + '">';
	const ticks = idx ? [lo, 100, hi] : [0, hi / 2, hi];
	for (const t of ticks) s += '<line x1="' + L + '" x2="' + (L + w) + '" y1="' + y(t) + '" y2="' + y(t) + '" stroke="' + (unit.k === 'index_100' && t === 100 ? 'var(--rule-strong)' : 'var(--rule)') + '"/><text x="' + (L - 4) + '" y="' + (y(t) + 4) + '" text-anchor="end">' + unit.f(t) + '</text>';
	if (hover >= 0) s += '<line x1="' + x(hover) + '" x2="' + x(hover) + '" y1="' + T + '" y2="' + (T + h) + '" stroke="var(--rule-strong)"/>';
	const ends = [];
	for (const c of cats) {
		const pts = months.map((m, i) => [x(i), val(c, m)]).filter((p) => p[1] != null);
		const dim = focus && focus !== c;
		s += '<path d="' + pts.map((p, i) => (i ? 'L' : 'M') + p[0].toFixed(1) + ' ' + y(p[1]).toFixed(1)).join(' ') + '" fill="none" stroke="' + COLORS[c] + '" stroke-width="' + (focus === c ? 3 : 2) + '" opacity="' + (dim ? 0.18 : 1) + '"/>';
		const last = pts[pts.length - 1]; if (last) ends.push({ c, v: last[1], y: y(last[1]), dim });
	}
	// end labels, nudged apart so they don't overlap
	ends.sort((a, b) => a.y - b.y); for (let i = 1; i < ends.length; i++) ends[i].y = Math.max(ends[i].y, ends[i - 1].y + 14);
	for (const e of ends) s += '<text x="' + (L + w + 6) + '" y="' + (e.y + 4) + '" style="fill: ' + COLORS[e.c] + '; opacity: ' + (e.dim ? 0.3 : 1) + '; font-weight: 600">' + K.esc(e.c) + ' ' + unit.f(e.v) + '</text>';
	s += '<text x="' + L + '" y="' + (H - 4) + '">' + mon(months[0]) + '</text><text x="' + (L + w) + '" y="' + (H - 4) + '" text-anchor="end">' + mon(months[months.length - 1]) + '</text>';
	months.forEach((m, i) => { s += '<rect data-i="' + i + '" x="' + (x(i) - w / (months.length - 1) / 2) + '" width="' + (w / (months.length - 1)) + '" y="' + T + '" height="' + h + '" fill="transparent"/>'; });
	K.$('#chart').innerHTML = s + '</svg>';
	K.$('#chart').querySelectorAll('rect[data-i]').forEach((el) => { el.onmouseenter = () => { const i = Number(el.dataset.i); if (i !== hover) { hover = i; draw(); } }; });
	K.$('#chart svg').onmouseleave = () => { if (hover !== -1) { hover = -1; draw(); } };
	K.$('#lg').innerHTML = '';
	for (const c of cats) { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(focus === c)); b.innerHTML = '<i style="background:' + COLORS[c] + '"></i>' + K.esc(c); b.onclick = () => { focus = focus === c ? null : c; draw(); }; K.$('#lg').appendChild(b); }
	const i = hover < 0 ? months.length - 1 : hover;
	K.$('#read').textContent = mon(months[i]) + ': ' + cats.map((c) => c + ' ' + (val(c, months[i]) == null ? '–' : unit.f(val(c, months[i])))).join(' · ');
}
app.subscribe(draw);
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read the lines in **$**: Services earns tens of thousands a month, Parts only a few hundred
2. Click **Index (first month = 100)**
3. Read the lines: every category starts at 100 in Jun 25 and shares one scale
4. Read the line under the chart: Parts ends at 84 in Sep 26

# Rank

> Number each customer by revenue, overall and within their country.

- Pattern id: `ranking`
- Category: Tables & calculations
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#ranking
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

Two rank columns appear: overall, and within the customer's country.

Why: Saying "the best in each region" needs a rank within each group.

## What to build

Each row gets two ranks, one across all rows and one within its group, and a toggle keeps only each group's leader.

Layout: Leaderboard with rank badges.

Instruction: Show each row's rank overall and within its group side by side, so the leaders stand out.

Done when: The top row overall also ranks first in its group, and the leaders toggle leaves exactly one row per group.

On the ecommerce sample: Customer 184 shows #1 both overall and in its country, and Country leaders only keeps one #1 customer per country.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { customer: customers.name, country: customers.country }
  measures {
    total_revenue: revenue,
    overall_rank: rank(order: revenue | desc(), partition: []),
    rank_in_country: rank(order: revenue | desc(), partition: customers.country),
  }
  sorts { total_revenue desc }
}
```

Saved result:

| customer | country | total_revenue | overall_rank | rank_in_country |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Customer 184 | Australia | 23750.30 | 1 | 1 |
| Customer 25 | Singapore | 20785.85 | 2 | 1 |
| Customer 140 | United States | 16482.34 | 3 | 1 |
| Customer 27 | Vietnam | 13553.76 | 4 | 1 |
| Customer 14 | Australia | 13460.39 | 5 | 2 |
| Customer 55 | Australia | 13447.66 | 6 | 3 |
| Customer 92 | Germany | 13118.24 | 7 | 1 |
| Customer 66 | Vietnam | 12779.49 | 8 | 2 |
| Customer 85 | United States | 12760.59 | 9 | 2 |
| Customer 43 | Singapore | 12551.70 | 10 | 2 |
| Customer 127 | Australia | 12543.48 | 11 | 4 |
| Customer 114 | Vietnam | 12464.46 | 12 | 3 |

(28 more rows)

Leaving out `partition` ranks each row against itself. Use `partition: []` for a whole-table rank.

## SDK wiring

```js
// read rank columns straight from the rows; sort stays server-side
```

## Notes

- `rank(order: revenue | desc(), partition: customers.country)`

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<style>.rk { display: inline-block; min-width: 28px; padding: 0 6px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--sunken); text-align: center; font-weight: 500; } .rk.top { background: var(--violet); color: #fff; } #tbl .tw { max-height: 252px; } #tbl td { padding: 3px 6px; }</style>
	<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><label class="lbl" for="cat">Revenue from</label><select id="cat"><option value="">All categories</option></select><span class="chips"><button type="button" id="leaders" aria-pressed="false">Country leaders only</button></span></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Customer leaderboard</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="tbl"></div>
		<div class="hint" id="note"></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Rank', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const board = app.createQuery('leaderboard', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { customer_name: customers.name, country_name: customers.country } measures { total_revenue: revenue, overall_rank: rank(order: revenue | desc(), partition: []), rank_in_country: rank(order: revenue | desc(), partition: customers.country) } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const cat = app.createFilter('category', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'products.category', label: 'Category' });
app.mapControl(cat, board, { field: 'products.category' });
const sel = K.$('#cat'), lead = K.$('#leaders');
cat.loadOptions().then((vals) => vals.forEach((v) => sel.add(new Option(v, v))));
sel.onchange = () => { if (sel.value) cat.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [sel.value] }); else cat.reset(); app.execute(); };
let leaders = false;
lead.onclick = () => { leaders = !leaders; lead.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(leaders)); draw(); };
const badge = (v) => '<span class="rk' + (Number(v) === 1 ? ' top' : '') + '">' + v + '</span>';
function draw () {
	K.status(board, K.$('#s1'));
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [board], () => [leaders ? 'leaders only → rank_in_country = 1 (picked in the browser, not sent)' : null]);
	if (!board.result) return;
	const rows = board.result.rows.filter((r) => !leaders || Number(r.rank_in_country) === 1);
	let h = '<div class="tw"><table><thead><tr><th class="num">Overall</th><th>Customer</th><th>Country</th><th class="num">Revenue</th><th class="num">In country</th></tr></thead><tbody>';
	for (const r of rows) h += '<tr><td class="num">' + badge(r.overall_rank) + '</td><td>' + K.esc(r.customer_name) + '</td><td>' + K.esc(r.country_name) + '</td><td class="num">' + K.money.format(Number(r.total_revenue)) + '</td><td class="num">' + badge(r.rank_in_country) + '</td></tr>';
	K.$('#tbl').innerHTML = h + '</tbody></table></div>';
	K.$('#note').textContent = K.int.format(rows.length) + ' customers. Both ranks come from the query and follow the category filter';
}
app.subscribe(draw);
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read the **Overall** and **In country** columns: Customer 184 is #1 in both
2. Click **Country leaders only** to keep just the #1 customer of each country
3. Pick a category in **Revenue from**, such as **Software**: both ranks change with it

# Binning

> Group orders into size bands, like under $100 or over $1,000.

- Pattern id: `bins`
- Category: Scenarios & analyses (also Tables & calculations)
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#bins
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

Orders fall into four value bands. A width slider rebuilds the histogram at $250 or $500 per bin.

Why: Bands turn a long list of order values into a story about order size.

## What to build

Each value falls into a band or bin, and picking a bin width regroups the values and redraws the histogram.

Layout: Band bars with orders and revenue.

Instruction: Group a number into bands or a histogram, and let the reader pick the bin width.

Done when: The band counts add up to the total, and a wider bin width shows fewer, taller bars.

On the ecommerce sample: The bands show 295 orders under $100, 421 at $100-499, 294 at $500-999 and 490 at $1,000+, and $500 bins redraw the histogram.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
dimension orders.value_band = case(
  when: orders.order_value < 100, then: '1. under $100',
  when: orders.order_value < 500, then: '2. $100-499',
  when: orders.order_value < 1000, then: '3. $500-999',
  else: '4. $1,000+'
);
explore {
  dimensions { band: orders.value_band }
  measures { num_orders: order_count, total_revenue: revenue }
  sorts { band asc }
}
```

Saved result:

| band | num_orders | total_revenue |
|---|---|---|
| 1. under $100 | 295 | 12566.89 |
| 2. $100-499 | 421 | 122893.17 |
| 3. $500-999 | 294 | 201976.78 |
| 4. $1,000+ | 490 | 945616.11 |

`orders.order_value` is a Dataset dimension (each order's revenue), and `case()` labels the band. The bin width lives in the AQL text, so each width is a new query built from a fixed list.

## SDK wiring

```js
// a fixed list: never free text
const WIDTHS = [100, 250, 500];
widthMenu.onchange = () =>
  showQuery(binsQuery(WIDTHS[widthMenu.selectedIndex]));
```

## Notes

- Declare `orders.order_value` and the band once. The joins and the two levels of grouping are handled for you

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Bin width</span><span class="seg" id="widths"></span><span class="hint">Each width is a new query built from a fixed list</span></div>
		<div class="cols" style="grid-template-columns: 1fr 1.1fr">
			<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b><span id="bt">Orders</span> by value band</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="bands"></div>
			<div class="row" style="margin-top:8px"><span class="lbl">Bars show</span><span class="seg" id="measure"><button type="button" data-m="num_orders" aria-pressed="true">Orders</button><button type="button" data-m="total_revenue" aria-pressed="false">Revenue</button></span></div></div>
			<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Histogram · <span id="wl">$250</span> bins</b><span class="status" id="s2"></span></div><div id="hist"></div></div>
		</div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Binning', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const BANDS = 'dimension orders.value_band = case(when: orders.order_value < 100, then: \'1. under $100\', when: orders.order_value < 500, then: \'2. $100-499\', when: orders.order_value < 1000, then: \'3. $500-999\', else: \'4. $1,000+\'); explore { dimensions { band: orders.value_band } measures { num_orders: order_count, total_revenue: revenue } sorts { band asc } }';
const bands = app.createQuery('bands', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: BANDS });
const WIDTHS = [100, 250, 500];
const hist = {};
const histQuery = (w) => hist[w] || (hist[w] = app.createQuery('histogram' + w, { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'dimension orders.value_bin = floor(orders.order_value / ' + Number(w) + ') * ' + Number(w) + '; explore { dimensions { bin_start: orders.value_bin } measures { num_orders: order_count } sorts { bin_start asc } }' }));
let w = 250, m = 'num_orders';
histQuery(w);
const seg = K.$('#widths');
for (const x of WIDTHS) { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = '$' + x; b.dataset.w = x; b.onclick = () => { w = x; histQuery(w); app.execute(); draw(); }; seg.appendChild(b); }
K.$('#measure').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => { b.onclick = () => { m = b.dataset.m; K.$('#measure').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((x) => x.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(x === b))); draw(); }; });
const usd = (v) => '$' + K.int.format(v);
function draw () {
	const h = hist[w];
	if (!h) return; // createQuery notifies subscribers before it returns
	seg.querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(Number(b.dataset.w) === w)));
	K.$('#wl').textContent = usd(w);
	K.status(bands, K.$('#s1')); K.status(h, K.$('#s2'));
	if (bands.result) K.bars(K.$('#bands'), bands.result.rows, { label: (r) => r.band.slice(3), value: (r) => r[m], fmt: m === 'num_orders' ? (v) => K.int.format(v) : (v) => K.compact.format(v) });
	K.$('#bt').textContent = m === 'num_orders' ? 'Orders' : 'Revenue';
	if (h.result) {
		const got = new Map(h.result.rows.map((r) => [Number(r.bin_start), Number(r.num_orders)]));
		const top = Math.max(...got.keys()), rows = [];
		for (let s = 0; s <= top; s += w) rows.push({ s, n: got.get(s) || 0 });
		K.columns(K.$('#hist'), rows, { label: (r) => usd(r.s) + '–' + usd(r.s + w - 1), value: (r) => r.n, fmt: (v) => K.int.format(v) + ' orders' });
	}
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [bands, h], () => ['bin width → ' + usd(w) + ', written into the AQL text of histogram' + w + ' (no query parameters in anfra 0.8.0)']);
}
app.subscribe(draw);
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read **Orders by value band**: 295 orders under $100, 421 at $100-499, 294 at $500-999 and 490 at $1,000+
2. Click **Revenue** next to **Bars show**: the $1,000+ band brings in most of the money
3. Click **$500** in **Bin width**: the histogram rebuilds with $500 bins
4. Click **$250** to go back to $250 bins

# Reference line

> Draw a target line and show how far each month is above or below it.

- Pattern id: `targets`
- Category: Scenarios & analyses (also Dates & time)
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#targets
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

Each month's revenue sits against the **monthly target** of the markets in view: $84k for all six countries. Filtering to **Japan** moves the line to Japan's $8k, where only August beat it (160%).

Why: Most performance pages need a plan to compare against, and the plan has to follow the filters.

## What to build

The target is drawn as a line that uses the same filters as the actuals, so changing a filter moves both together.

Layout: Columns with a dashed target line and attainment labels.

Instruction: Draw the target as a line that follows the same filters as the actuals, with attainment for each period.

Done when: Changing a filter moves the target line along with the bars, and periods above the line show attainment over 100%.

On the ecommerce sample: With all countries the dashed target is $84k. Picking Japan moves it to $8k, and only August beats it, at 160%.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() }
  measures {
    total_revenue: revenue,
    target: monthly_target,
    attainment: revenue * 1.0 / monthly_target,
  }
  filters { orders.ordered_at matches @(2026) }
  sorts { period asc }
}
```

Reader input the SDK sent:

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "field": "customers.country",
      "operator": "is",
      "values": [
        "Japan"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Saved result:

| period | total_revenue | target | attainment |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-01-01 | 6967.41 | 8000.00 | 0.87092625 |
| 2026-02-01 | 7590.35 | 8000.00 | 0.94879375 |
| 2026-03-01 | 5856.24 | 8000.00 | 0.73203 |
| 2026-04-01 | 5443.75 | 8000.00 | 0.68046875 |
| 2026-05-01 | 7528.85 | 8000.00 | 0.94110625 |
| 2026-06-01 | 7261.95 | 8000.00 | 0.90774375 |
| 2026-07-01 | 7852.40 | 8000.00 | 0.9815499999999999 |
| 2026-08-01 | 12777.85 | 8000.00 | 1.59723125 |
| 2026-09-01 | 5708.14 | 8000.00 | 0.7135175 |

`monthly_target` is a Dataset metric over a new `markets` model (one row per country, with its monthly target), added to the ecommerce sample for this card. Because it sums the markets in scope, it follows any country filter.

## SDK wiring

```js
// the target is data, so it obeys the same mappings as revenue
app.mapControl(country, trend, { field: 'customers.country' });
// draw target as a dashed line; colour bars where revenue / target
// >= 1
```

State it touches: Analytical: the target comes from the data and follows filters. A renderer-only constant would not.

## Notes

- `monthly_target` is a metric like revenue: the same filters reach both

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><label class="lbl" for="country">Country</label><select id="country"><option value="">All countries</option></select><span class="hint">The target is a metric, so the filter reaches it too</span></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue 2026 vs target<span id="for"></span></b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div>
		<div id="chart"></div>
		<div class="legend"><span><i style="background:var(--violet)"></i>Beat the target</span><span><i style="background:var(--violet-faint)"></i>Below it</span><span><i style="background:none;border-top:2px dashed var(--ink);height:0;border-radius:0"></i><span id="tl">Monthly target</span></span></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Reference line', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const trend = app.createQuery('trend', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() } measures { total_revenue: revenue, target: monthly_target, attainment: revenue * 1.0 / monthly_target } filters { orders.ordered_at matches @(2026) } sorts { period asc } }' });
const country = app.createFilter('country', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.country', label: 'Country' });
app.mapControl(country, trend, { field: 'customers.country' });
const sel = K.$('#country');
country.loadOptions().then((vals) => vals.forEach((v) => sel.add(new Option(v, v))));
sel.onchange = () => { if (sel.value) country.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [sel.value] }); else country.reset(); app.execute(); };
const pct = (v) => Math.round(v * 100) + '%';
const mon = (v) => new Date(v).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', timeZone: 'UTC' });
function chart (el, rows) {
	const tgt = Math.max(...rows.map((r) => Number(r.target)), 0);
	const max = Math.max(tgt, ...rows.map((r) => Number(r.total_revenue))) * 1.15 || 1;
	const cols = rows.map((r) => { const v = Number(r.total_revenue), a = Number(r.attainment), hit = a >= 1;
		return '<div style="flex:1;position:relative;height:100%" title="' + mon(r.period) + ': ' + K.money.format(v) + ' of ' + K.money.format(Number(r.target)) + ' (' + pct(a) + ')">'
			+ '<span style="position:absolute;left:12%;right:12%;bottom:0;height:' + (v / max * 100) + '%;background:' + (hit ? 'var(--violet)' : 'var(--violet-faint)') + ';border-radius:3px 3px 0 0;transition:height 320ms"></span>'
			+ '</div>'; }).join('');
	el.innerHTML = '<div style="position:relative;height:150px;display:flex;gap:4px;align-items:flex-end">' + cols
		+ '<div style="position:absolute;left:0;right:0;bottom:' + (tgt / max * 100) + '%;border-top:2px dashed var(--ink);pointer-events:none"></div></div>'
		+ '<div style="display:flex;gap:4px;font-size:12px;line-height:16px;color:var(--muted);margin-top:4px">' + rows.map((r) => { const a = Number(r.attainment); return '<span style="flex:1;text-align:center">' + mon(r.period) + '<br><b style="font-weight:' + (a >= 1 ? '600;color:var(--violet-ink)' : '400') + '">' + pct(a) + '</b></span>'; }).join('') + '</div>';
}
app.subscribe(() => {
	K.status(trend, K.$('#s1'));
	const c = country.appliedCondition && country.appliedCondition.values && country.appliedCondition.values[0];
	K.$('#for').textContent = c ? ' · ' + c : ' · all countries';
	if (trend.result) {
		const rows = trend.result.rows;
		chart(K.$('#chart'), rows);
		const hits = rows.filter((r) => Number(r.attainment) >= 1).length;
		K.$('#tl').textContent = 'Monthly target ' + K.compact.format(Number(rows[0] ? rows[0].target : 0)) + ' · ' + hits + ' of ' + rows.length + ' months beat it';
	}
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [trend]);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read the chart with **All countries**: the dashed line is the $84k monthly target of all six countries
2. Pick **Japan** in **Country**
3. Read the chart: the line moves to Japan's $8k, and only August beats it (160%)

# Trend line

> Draw the line of best fit through a chart, to show which way it is heading.

- Pattern id: `trend-line`
- Category: Scenarios & analyses (also Dates & time, Tables & calculations)
- Status: Works with app code: anfra supplies the queries, the app adds some logic
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#trend-line
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

A dashed **linear** trend runs through 16 months of revenue. Across every month it slopes down, −$56 a month, because September 2026 has only 23 of 30 days. **Leaving out that month** turns it up, to +$342 a month. **Exponential** and a **3- or 6-month moving average** are one click away, and **Break down by category** fits a line for each: Software grows +$450 a month while Services falls −$202.

Why: Monthly numbers bounce around. A trend line answers "are we growing?" without the reader squinting at the bars.

## What to build

The query returns the points; the app fits a straight or exponential line through them, or draws a moving average that the query computes. A month that isn't over yet is left out of the fit.

Layout: Monthly columns with a dashed trend line; per-category lines when broken down.

Instruction: Add a dashed trend line to my time chart, with Linear, Exponential and Moving average options, one line per series when it has a legend, and an option to leave out the incomplete last period.

Done when: The trend follows the filters, each series gets its own line when broken down, and a short last period doesn't drag the line down.

On the ecommerce sample: Across all 16 months the linear trend is −$56 a month. Leaving out September 2026 (23 of 30 days) turns it to +$342 a month. Broken down by category, Software grows +$450 a month and Services falls −$202.

## AQL

Not run as written: the query returns the points; a moving average comes from window_avg.

```aql
explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() } measures { total_revenue: revenue, avg_3m: window_avg(revenue, -2..0, order: orders.ordered_at | month()), last_order_day: orders | max(orders.ordered_at) } sorts { period asc } }
```

## SDK wiring

```js
// least squares on the rows the query returned
function linear(ys) {
  const n = ys.length, mx = (n - 1) / 2;
  const my = ys.reduce((a, y) => a + y, 0) / n;
  let sxy = 0, sxx = 0;
  ys.forEach((y, x) => {
    sxy += (x - mx) * (y - my);
    sxx += (x - mx) ** 2;
  });
  const b = sxy / sxx; // change per month
  return ys.map((_, x) => my + b * (x - mx));
}
const rows = q.result.rows;
const last = rows.at(-1);
// leave out a month that isn't over yet
const full = isPartial(last.last_order_day)
  ? rows.slice(0, -1) : rows;
drawDashed(linear(full.map((r) => +r.total_revenue)));
```

State it touches: Renderer state: the fit type and its options. The points, the moving average and the incomplete-month check come from the query, so filters reach them.

## Notes

- The query returns the points and `last_order_day`; the moving average is `window_avg` with a `partition` for each category
- Limits: Works with app code: AQL has no regression function, so the app fits linear and exponential lines on the returned rows, as a chart library would. Exponential needs values above zero.

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<style>#chart svg { display: block; overflow: visible; } #chart text { font-size: 12px; fill: var(--muted); } .key { display: inline-block; width: 14px; height: 0; border-top: 2px dashed; vertical-align: 4px; margin-right: 4px; } #per[hidden] { display: none; } .cat { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; margin-right: 12px; } .cat i { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; }</style>
	<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Trend line</span><span class="seg" id="types"></span><span class="seg" id="per"></span></div>
		<div class="row"><span class="chips"><button type="button" id="split" aria-pressed="false">Break down by category</button><button type="button" id="skip" aria-pressed="true">Leave out the incomplete month</button></span></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Monthly revenue<span id="by"></span></b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="chart"></div>
		<div class="hint" id="read"></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Trend line', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const m = 'orders.ordered_at | month()';
const avgs = (p) => 'avg_3m: window_avg(revenue, -2..0, order: ' + m + p + '), avg_6m: window_avg(revenue, -5..0, order: ' + m + p + ')';
const total = app.createQuery('total', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { period: ' + m + ' } measures { total_revenue: revenue, ' + avgs('') + ', last_order_day: orders | max(orders.ordered_at) } sorts { period asc } }' });
const byCat = app.createQuery('byCategory', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { period: ' + m + ', category_name: products.category } measures { total_revenue: revenue, ' + avgs(', partition: products.category') + ' } sorts { category_name asc, period asc } }' });
const TYPES = [['linear', 'Linear'], ['exp', 'Exponential'], ['avg', 'Moving average']];
const ui = { type: 'linear', per: 3, split: false, skip: true };
const COLORS = ['#8a51d4', '#2a78d6', '#eb6834', '#1baf7a', '#eda100'];
const MN = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec'];
const D = (s) => new Date(String(s).slice(0, 10) + 'T00:00:00Z');
const mon = (s) => { const x = D(s); return MN[x.getUTCMonth()] + ' ' + String(x.getUTCFullYear()).slice(2); };
function seg (el, items, key) {
	for (const [v, t] of items) { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = t; b.dataset.v = v; b.onclick = () => { ui[key] = key === 'per' ? Number(v) : v; draw(); }; el.appendChild(b); }
}
seg(K.$('#types'), TYPES, 'type');
seg(K.$('#per'), [[3, '3 months'], [6, '6 months']], 'per');
K.$('#split').onclick = () => { ui.split = !ui.split; draw(); };
K.$('#skip').onclick = () => { ui.skip = !ui.skip; draw(); };
// least squares on x = 0, 1, 2 ... over the points the fit uses
function line (pts) {
	const n = pts.length; if (n < 2) return null;
	const mx = pts.reduce((a, p) => a + p[0], 0) / n, my = pts.reduce((a, p) => a + p[1], 0) / n;
	let sxy = 0, sxx = 0; for (const [x, y] of pts) { sxy += (x - mx) * (y - my); sxx += (x - mx) * (x - mx); }
	const b = sxy / sxx; return { a: my - b * mx, b };
}
// returns the fitted value at each x (null where it is not drawn), and a one-line reading
function fit (rows, use) {
	const ys = rows.map((r) => Number(r.total_revenue)), n = ys.length;
	if (ui.type === 'avg') { const k = ui.per === 6 ? 'avg_6m' : 'avg_3m'; const v = rows.map((r, i) => i >= ui.per - 1 ? Number(r[k]) : null); return { v, read: ui.per + '-month average ends at ' + K.compact.format(v[n - 1]) }; }
	const pts = ys.map((y, i) => [i, y]).filter((p, i) => use(i) && (ui.type !== 'exp' || p[1] > 0));
	if (ui.type === 'exp') {
		const f = line(pts.map(([x, y]) => [x, Math.log(y)])); if (!f) return { v: [], read: '' };
		const g = Math.exp(f.b) - 1;
		return { v: ys.map((_, i) => Math.exp(f.a + f.b * i)), read: (g >= 0 ? '+' : '') + (g * 100).toFixed(2) + '% a month' };
	}
	const f = line(pts); if (!f) return { v: [], read: '' };
	return { v: ys.map((_, i) => f.a + f.b * i), read: (f.b >= 0 ? '+' : '−') + K.money.format(Math.abs(f.b)).replace('-', '') + ' a month' };
}
function draw () {
	K.status(ui.split ? byCat : total, K.$('#s1'));
	K.$('#types').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.dataset.v === ui.type)));
	K.$('#per').hidden = ui.type !== 'avg';
	K.$('#per').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(Number(b.dataset.v) === ui.per)));
	K.$('#split').setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(ui.split));
	K.$('#by').textContent = ui.split ? ' by category' : '';
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [ui.split ? byCat : total], () => ['trend line → ' + (ui.type === 'avg' ? ui.per + '-month window_avg, from the query' : TYPES.find((t) => t[0] === ui.type)[1].toLowerCase() + ' fit, drawn in the browser') + (ui.skip && ui.type !== 'avg' ? ', without the incomplete month' : '')]);
	if (!total.result || !total.result.rows.length) return;
	const rows = total.result.rows, n = rows.length, last = rows[n - 1];
	const end = D(last.period); end.setUTCMonth(end.getUTCMonth() + 1); end.setUTCDate(0);
	const partial = D(last.last_order_day) < end;
	const had = D(last.last_order_day).getUTCDate(), all = end.getUTCDate();
	const skip = ui.skip && partial && ui.type !== 'avg';
	K.$('#skip').textContent = partial ? 'Leave out ' + mon(last.period) + ' (' + had + ' of ' + all + ' days)' : 'Every month is complete';
	K.$('#skip').disabled = !partial || ui.type === 'avg';
	K.$('#skip').setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(skip));
	const use = (i) => !(skip && i === n - 1);
	let series;
	if (ui.split) {
		if (!byCat.result) return;
		const g = {}; for (const r of byCat.result.rows) (g[r.category_name] ||= {})[String(r.period).slice(0, 10)] = r;
		series = Object.keys(g).map((c, j) => { const rs = rows.map((r) => g[c][String(r.period).slice(0, 10)] || { total_revenue: 0, avg_3m: null, avg_6m: null }); return { name: c, color: COLORS[j % COLORS.length], ys: rs.map((r) => Number(r.total_revenue)), f: fit(rs, use) }; });
	} else series = [{ name: 'All categories', color: 'var(--violet)', ys: rows.map((r) => Number(r.total_revenue)), f: fit(rows, use) }];
	const W = K.$('#chart').clientWidth, H = 180, L = 40, R = 8, T = 6, B = 20, w = W - L - R, h = H - T - B;
	const nice = (v) => { const p = Math.pow(10, Math.floor(Math.log10(v))), q = v / p; return (q <= 1 ? 1 : q <= 2 ? 2 : q <= 2.5 ? 2.5 : q <= 5 ? 5 : 10) * p; };
	const max = nice(Math.max(1, ...series.flatMap((s) => s.ys.concat(s.f.v.filter((x) => x != null)))));
	const step = w / n, x = (i) => L + step * i + step / 2, y = (v) => T + h - v / max * h;
	const path = (vals) => { let d = '', pen = false; vals.forEach((v, i) => { if (v == null) { pen = false; return; } d += (pen ? 'L' : 'M') + x(i).toFixed(1) + ' ' + y(v).toFixed(1); pen = true; }); return d; };
	let s = '<svg width="' + W + '" height="' + H + '"><defs><pattern id="hatch" width="6" height="6" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse" patternTransform="rotate(45)"><rect width="3" height="6" fill="var(--violet-faint)"/></pattern></defs>';
	for (const t of [0, 0.5, 1]) s += '<line x1="' + L + '" x2="' + (W - R) + '" y1="' + y(max * t) + '" y2="' + y(max * t) + '" stroke="var(--rule)"/><text x="' + (L - 4) + '" y="' + (y(max * t) + 4) + '" text-anchor="end">' + K.compact.format(max * t) + '</text>';
	if (!ui.split) series[0].ys.forEach((v, i) => { s += '<rect x="' + (x(i) - step * 0.38).toFixed(1) + '" width="' + (step * 0.76).toFixed(1) + '" y="' + y(v).toFixed(1) + '" height="' + (T + h - y(v)).toFixed(1) + '" rx="2" fill="' + (use(i) ? 'var(--violet-faint)' : 'url(#hatch)') + '"' + (use(i) ? '' : ' stroke="var(--violet-faint)"') + '><title>' + mon(rows[i].period) + ': ' + K.money.format(v) + (use(i) ? '' : ' (incomplete, left out of the fit)') + '</title></rect>'; });
	else for (const se of series) s += '<path d="' + path(se.ys) + '" fill="none" stroke="' + se.color + '" stroke-width="1.5" opacity=".45"/>';
	for (const se of series) s += '<path d="' + path(se.f.v) + '" fill="none" stroke="' + (ui.split ? se.color : 'var(--ink)') + '" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>';
	s += '<text x="' + x(0) + '" y="' + (H - 4) + '" text-anchor="middle">' + mon(rows[0].period) + '</text><text x="' + x(n - 1) + '" y="' + (H - 4) + '" text-anchor="middle">' + mon(last.period) + '</text>';
	K.$('#chart').innerHTML = s + '</svg>';
	K.$('#read').innerHTML = series.map((se) => ui.split ? '<span class="cat"><i style="background:' + se.color + '"></i>' + K.esc(se.name) + ': ' + K.esc(se.f.read) + '</span>' : '<span class="key"></span>Trend: <b>' + K.esc(se.f.read) + '</b>' + (skip ? ' · fitted on ' + (n - 1) + ' full months' : ui.type === 'avg' ? '' : ' · fitted on all ' + n + ' months')).join('');
}
app.subscribe(draw);
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read the chart: the dashed **Linear** trend across all 16 months slopes down, **−$56 a month**
2. The last month is hatched: September 2026 has only 23 of 30 days. **Leave out Sep 26** is on, so the fit uses 15 full months and reads **+$342 a month**
3. Click **Leave out Sep 26** to turn it off: the line tips down again
4. Click **Moving average**, then **6 months**: the line now comes from `window_avg` in the query
5. Click **Linear**, then **Break down by category**: each category gets its own trend, Software **+$450 a month** and Services **−$202 a month**

## Other Scenarios & analyses patterns

- [Binning](bins.md): Group orders into size bands, like under $100 or over $1,000.
- [Reference line](targets.md): Draw a target line and show how far each month is above or below it.
- [What-if parameter](what-if.md): Try a price change, like +10% on Software, and watch revenue change.
- [Rule-based cohort](cohort-from-rank.md): Define a group by a rule, like the top 10% of customers by revenue.

---

# What-if parameter

> Try a price change, like +10% on Software, and watch revenue change.

- Pattern id: `what-if`
- Category: Scenarios & analyses
- Status: Works with app code: anfra supplies the queries, the app adds some logic
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#what-if
- Full Data App: https://demo.anfra.ai/apps/patterns/what-if-parameter
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader picks the **Optimistic** preset (Software +10%, Services +5%), drags **Hardware** up, then tries **Price war**. Scenario revenue moves against actual by category and by month: Optimistic is $1,327,669 against $1,283,053 actual, +3.5%.

Why: Readers plan by asking "what if?". Answering in the app saves building a spreadsheet.

## What to build

Moving a slider changes one assumption, and the scenario recalculates from it next to the unchanged actual.

Layout: Actual vs scenario bars, with the delta.

Instruction: Let the reader change an assumption, like a price change, and see the scenario next to the actual result.

Done when: The scenario and the actual show side by side, and setting every slider back to zero makes them match.

On the ecommerce sample: Optimistic (Software +10%, Services +5%) lifts those two scenario bars above actual, and setting every slider to 0% brings the total back to $1,283,053.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
dimension products.price_factor = case(when: products.category == 'Hardware', then: 1.10, when: products.category == 'Software', then: 1.05, else: 1);
dimension products.volume_factor = case(when: products.category == 'Hardware', then: 0.88, when: products.category == 'Software', then: 0.94, else: 1);
metric scenario_revenue = order_items | sum(order_items.quantity * products.price * products.price_factor * products.volume_factor);
explore {
  dimensions { category: products.category }
  measures { total_revenue: revenue, scenario: scenario_revenue }
  sorts { total_revenue desc }
}
```

Saved result:

| category | total_revenue | scenario |
|---|---|---|
| Services | 578000.00 | 578000.000000 |
| Software | 497394.00 | 490927.878000 |
| Hardware | 193999.60 | 187791.612800 |
| Parts | 13659.35 | 13659.350000 |

The recording is the real Data App `apps/patterns/what-if-parameter.html`. Each change rebuilds this query from validated numbers (price factor and volume factor per category), because anfra 0.8.0 has no query parameters. The query above is one example parameter set.

## SDK wiring

```js
// a number from a slider, validated
function scenario(upliftPct) {
  const f = (1 + Number(upliftPct) / 100).toFixed(4);
  prev?.abort();
  prev = app.createQuery('s' + ++n, {
    dataset: 'ecommerce',
    aql: WHATIF_AQL.replace('1.10', f),
  });
  return app.execute();
}
// Proposed: aql with $uplift and app.createParameter('uplift', {
// type: 'number' })
```

## Notes

- A scenario metric sits next to the real one, and both go through the same joins
- Limits: Works with app code. Typed query parameters (`createParameter`) are proposed, so the AQL wouldn't have to be rebuilt.

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app"><style>#presets button { padding: 0 8px; }</style>
		<div class="cols" style="grid-template-columns: 236px 1fr">
			<div class="panel" style="display:grid;gap:8px;align-content:start">
				<div class="lbl">Preset</div>
				<div class="chips" id="presets"><button type="button" data-p="base">Base</button><button type="button" data-p="optimistic">Optimistic</button><button type="button" data-p="pricewar">Price war</button></div>
				<div class="lbl">Price change by category</div>
				<div id="sliders" style="display:grid;gap:2px"></div>
				<div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr auto;font-size:12px;line-height:16px"><label for="el">Units fall per +1% price</label><output id="elo"></output><input id="el" type="range" min="0" max="2" step="0.1" style="grid-column:1 / -1"></div>
			</div>
			<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue: actual vs scenario</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div>
				<div class="row" style="gap:16px;margin-bottom:6px"><div><div class="lbl">Actual</div><div class="kpi" id="ka">–</div></div><div><div class="lbl">Scenario</div><div class="kpi" id="ks" style="color:var(--violet-ink)">–</div></div></div><div class="hint" id="kd" style="margin-bottom:6px"></div>
				<div id="cats"></div>
				<div class="legend" style="margin-top:6px"><span><i style="background:rgb(24 20 31 / 0.14)"></i>Actual</span><span><i style="background:var(--violet)"></i>Scenario</span></div>
			</div>
		</div>
		<div class="hint">App code: each change declares a new query, built only from validated numbers</div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'What-if parameter', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const CATS = ['Services', 'Software', 'Hardware', 'Parts'];
const PRESETS = {
	base: { price: { Services: 0, Software: 0, Hardware: 0, Parts: 0 }, el: 0.6 },
	optimistic: { price: { Services: 5, Software: 10, Hardware: 0, Parts: 0 }, el: 0.4 },
	pricewar: { price: { Services: 0, Software: -5, Hardware: -10, Parts: -10 }, el: 1.2 },
};
let params = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(PRESETS.base)), preset = 'base';
const sl = K.$('#sliders');
for (const c of CATS) {
	const d = document.createElement('div');
	d.style.cssText = 'display:grid;grid-template-columns:62px minmax(0,1fr) 36px;gap:4px;align-items:center;font-size:12px;line-height:16px';
	d.innerHTML = '<label for="p-' + c + '">' + c + '</label><input id="p-' + c + '" type="range" min="-20" max="30" step="1" style="width:100%"><output id="o-' + c + '" style="text-align:right"></output>';
	sl.appendChild(d);
	d.querySelector('input').oninput = (e) => { params.price[c] = Number(e.target.value); preset = null; schedule(); };
}
K.$('#el').oninput = (e) => { params.el = Number(e.target.value); preset = null; schedule(); };
K.$('#presets').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => { b.onclick = () => { params = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(PRESETS[b.dataset.p])); preset = b.dataset.p; schedule(0); }; });
const sign = (v) => (v > 0 ? '+' : v < 0 ? '−' : '') + Math.abs(v) + '%';
function syncInputs () {
	for (const c of CATS) { K.$('#p-' + c).value = params.price[c]; K.$('#o-' + c).textContent = sign(params.price[c]); }
	K.$('#el').value = params.el; K.$('#elo').textContent = params.el.toFixed(1) + '%';
	K.$('#presets').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.dataset.p === preset)));
}
const num = (v, lo, hi) => { const n = Number(v); if (!Number.isFinite(n)) throw new Error('bad parameter'); return Math.min(hi, Math.max(lo, n)); };
function aql () {
	const e = num(params.el, 0, 2);
	const p = CATS.map((c) => [c, num(params.price[c], -20, 30) / 100]);
	const pf = p.map((x) => 'when: products.category == \'' + x[0] + '\', then: ' + (1 + x[1]).toFixed(4)).join(', ');
	const vf = p.map((x) => 'when: products.category == \'' + x[0] + '\', then: ' + Math.max(0, 1 - e * x[1]).toFixed(4)).join(', ');
	return 'dimension products.price_factor = case(' + pf + ', else: 1);\ndimension products.volume_factor = case(' + vf + ', else: 1);\nmetric scenario_revenue = order_items | sum(order_items.quantity * products.price * products.price_factor * products.volume_factor);\nexplore {\n  dimensions { category_name: products.category }\n  measures { total_revenue: revenue, scenario: scenario_revenue }\n  sorts { total_revenue desc }\n}';
}
let n = 0, cur = null, timer = null;
function schedule (wait) { syncInputs(); clearTimeout(timer); timer = setTimeout(run, wait == null ? 250 : wait); }
function run () {
	if (cur) cur.abort();
	cur = app.createQuery('scenario' + (++n), { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: aql() });
	app.execute(); draw();
}
function draw () {
	if (!cur) return;
	K.status(cur, K.$('#s1'));
	if (cur.result) {
		const rows = cur.result.rows;
		const a = rows.reduce((t, r) => t + Number(r.total_revenue), 0), s = rows.reduce((t, r) => t + Number(r.scenario), 0);
		K.$('#ka').textContent = K.money.format(a); K.$('#ks').textContent = K.money.format(s);
		K.$('#kd').innerHTML = 'Change: <b style="color:' + (s >= a ? 'var(--violet-ink)' : '#b42318') + '">' + (s >= a ? '+' : '−') + K.money.format(Math.abs(s - a)) + ' (' + (s >= a ? '+' : '−') + (Math.abs(s - a) / a * 100).toFixed(1) + '%)</b>';
		const max = Math.max(...rows.map((r) => Math.max(Number(r.total_revenue), Number(r.scenario))), 1);
		K.$('#cats').innerHTML = rows.map((r) => { const ac = Number(r.total_revenue), sc = Number(r.scenario), d = sc - ac;
			return '<div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:62px minmax(0,1fr) 64px;gap:6px;align-items:center;font-size:12px;line-height:16px;margin:3px 0"><span>' + K.esc(r.category_name) + '</span>'
				+ '<span style="display:grid;gap:2px"><span style="height:8px;border-radius:2px;background:rgb(24 20 31 / 0.14);width:' + (ac / max * 100) + '%"></span><span style="height:8px;border-radius:2px;background:var(--violet);width:' + (sc / max * 100) + '%;transition:width 320ms"></span></span>'
				+ '<span style="text-align:right;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;color:' + (d < 0 ? '#b42318' : 'var(--violet-ink)') + '">' + (d >= 0 ? '+' : '−') + K.compact.format(Math.abs(d)) + '</span></div>'; }).join('');
	}
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [cur], () => [cur.name + ' (query #' + n + ', declared per change) ← price % ' + CATS.map((c) => c + ' ' + params.price[c]).join(', ') + '; units fall ' + params.el.toFixed(1) + '% per +1%']);
}
app.subscribe(draw);
schedule(0);
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Click **Optimistic** under **Preset**: Software +10%, Services +5%
2. Read the totals: **Scenario** $1,327,669 against **Actual** $1,283,053, a +3.5% change
3. Drag the **Hardware** slider up and watch its bar and the totals move
4. Click **Price war** and compare each category's scenario bar with actual

- [Binning](bins.md): Group orders into size bands, like under $100 or over $1,000.
- [Reference line](targets.md): Draw a target line and show how far each month is above or below it.
- [Trend line](trend-line.md): Draw the line of best fit through a chart, to show which way it is heading.

# Rule-based cohort

> Define a group by a rule, like the top 10% of customers by revenue.

- Pattern id: `cohort-from-rank`
- Category: Scenarios & analyses (also Selections)
- Status: Works with app code: anfra supplies the queries, the app adds some logic
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#cohort-from-rank
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader picks the rule **Top 10% by revenue**. The app ranks customers into deciles and saves decile 1 as a cohort. Other charts can then compare that cohort with everyone else.

Why: A cohort defined by a rule can be explained and rebuilt. One picked by hand can't.

## What to build

Picking a rule like top 10% ranks the rows, saves the matching ones as a group, and compares it with the rest.

Layout: Decile bars, then a cohort chip.

Instruction: Let the reader pick a rule like top 10%, save the matching rows as a group, and compare it with the rest.

Done when: The saved group's size matches the rule, and the comparison shows the group and everyone else side by side.

On the ecommerce sample: Picking 10% saves the top 20 customers as Cohort: Top 10% (20), shown side by side with everyone else.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore {
  dimensions { customer: customers.name }
  measures {
    total_revenue: revenue,
    decile: ntile(10, order: revenue | desc(), partition: []),
  }
  sorts { total_revenue desc }
}
```

Saved result:

| customer | total_revenue | decile |
|---|---|---|
| Customer 184 | 23750.30 | 1 |
| Customer 25 | 20785.85 | 1 |
| Customer 140 | 16482.34 | 1 |
| Customer 27 | 13553.76 | 1 |
| Customer 14 | 13460.39 | 1 |
| Customer 55 | 13447.66 | 1 |
| Customer 92 | 13118.24 | 1 |
| Customer 66 | 12779.49 | 1 |
| Customer 85 | 12760.59 | 1 |
| Customer 43 | 12551.70 | 1 |
| Customer 127 | 12543.48 | 1 |
| Customer 114 | 12464.46 | 1 |

(28 more rows)

## SDK wiring

```js
await app.execute();
const ids = deciles.result.rows
  .filter((r) => r.decile === '1')
  .map((r) => r.id);
inCohort.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: ids });
```

## Notes

- `ntile` in one measure, and the cohort is a list of IDs in a filter
- Limits: Works with app code: two steps, rank and then filter. Promoting the decile to a Dataset dimension would make it one filter.

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app"><style>#deciles .b { height: 19px; } #deciles { gap: 1px; }</style>
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Top customers by revenue</span><span class="seg" id="rules"><button type="button" data-k="1">10%</button><button type="button" data-k="2">20%</button><button type="button" data-k="5">50%</button></span><button type="button" id="save">Save as cohort</button></div>
		<div class="cols" style="grid-template-columns: 1fr 1.15fr">
			<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by customer decile</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="deciles"></div></div>
			<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Cohort vs everyone else</b><span class="status" id="s2"></span></div><div id="chip" class="chips" style="margin-bottom:6px"></div><div id="cmp"><div class="hint">Save a cohort to compare it with the other customers</div></div></div>
		</div>
		<div class="hint">App code: rank with ntile(10), then filter customers.id to the chosen deciles</div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Rule-based cohort', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const ranks = app.createQuery('deciles', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { cust_id: customers.id, cust_name: customers.name } measures { total_revenue: revenue, decile: ntile(10, order: revenue | desc(), partition: []) } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const CMP = 'explore { measures { num_customers: count_distinct(orders.customer_id), total_revenue: revenue, num_orders: order_count, avg_order_value: aov } }';
const inside = app.createQuery('cohort', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: CMP });
const outside = app.createQuery('everyoneElse', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: CMP });
const inCohort = app.createFilter('inCohort', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.id', label: 'In cohort' });
const notInCohort = app.createFilter('notInCohort', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.id', label: 'Not in cohort' });
app.mapControl(inCohort, inside, { field: 'customers.id' });
app.mapControl(notInCohort, outside, { field: 'customers.id' });
let k = 1, saved = null;
const RULE = { 1: 'Top 10%', 2: 'Top 20%', 5: 'Top 50%' };
K.$('#rules').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => { b.onclick = () => { k = Number(b.dataset.k); draw(); }; });
K.$('#save').onclick = () => {
	if (!ranks.result) return;
	const ids = ranks.result.rows.filter((r) => Number(r.decile) <= k).map((r) => String(r.cust_id));
	saved = { rule: RULE[k], k, n: ids.length };
	inCohort.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: ids });
	notInCohort.setCondition({ operator: 'is_not', values: ids });
	app.execute();
};
function draw () {
	K.$('#rules').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(Number(b.dataset.k) === k)));
	K.status(ranks, K.$('#s1'));
	if (ranks.result) {
		const by = new Map();
		for (const r of ranks.result.rows) { const d = Number(r.decile); const x = by.get(d) || { d, rev: 0, n: 0 }; x.rev += Number(r.total_revenue); x.n++; by.set(d, x); }
		const rows = [...by.values()].sort((a, b) => a.d - b.d);
		K.bars(K.$('#deciles'), rows, { label: (r) => 'Decile ' + r.d + ' · ' + r.n, value: (r) => r.rev, on: (r) => r.d <= k, pick: (r) => { k = r.d; draw(); } });
		const n = rows.filter((r) => r.d <= k).reduce((t, r) => t + r.n, 0);
		K.$('#save').textContent = 'Save as cohort (' + n + ')';
	}
	if (saved) {
		K.$('#chip').innerHTML = '<button type="button" aria-pressed="true" id="clr">Cohort: ' + K.esc(saved.rule) + ' (' + saved.n + ') ×</button>';
		K.$('#clr').onclick = () => { saved = null; inCohort.reset(); notInCohort.reset(); K.$('#chip').innerHTML = ''; K.$('#cmp').innerHTML = '<div class="hint">Save a cohort to compare it with the other customers</div>'; draw(); };
		K.status(inside, K.$('#s2'));
		if (inside.result && outside.result && inside.state === 'success' && outside.state === 'success') {
			const a = inside.result.rows[0] || {}, b = outside.result.rows[0] || {};
			const tot = Number(a.total_revenue || 0) + Number(b.total_revenue || 0);
			const rows = [
				{ m: 'Customers', a: K.int.format(a.num_customers), b: K.int.format(b.num_customers) },
				{ m: 'Revenue', a: K.money.format(a.total_revenue), b: K.money.format(b.total_revenue) },
				{ m: 'Revenue share', a: Math.round(a.total_revenue / tot * 100) + '%', b: Math.round(b.total_revenue / tot * 100) + '%' },
				{ m: 'Orders', a: K.int.format(a.num_orders), b: K.int.format(b.num_orders) },
				{ m: 'Avg order', a: K.money.format(a.avg_order_value), b: K.money.format(b.avg_order_value) },
			];
			K.table(K.$('#cmp'), [{ key: 'm', label: '' }, { key: 'a', label: 'Cohort', num: true }, { key: 'b', label: 'Everyone else', num: true }], rows);
		}
	} else K.$('#s2').textContent = '';
	const short = (q) => { const c = app.controls[q === inside ? 'inCohort' : 'notInCohort'].appliedCondition; return c && c.values && c.values.length ? q.name + ' ← customers.id ' + c.operator.replace('_', ' ') + ' [' + c.values.slice(0, 4).join(', ') + (c.values.length > 4 ? ', … ' + c.values.length + ' ids' : '') + ']' : q.name + ' ← no cohort yet'; };
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [ranks], () => [short(inside), short(outside)]);
}
app.subscribe(draw);
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Click **10%** next to **Top customers by revenue**
2. Read **Revenue by customer decile**: decile 1 holds the top 20 customers
3. Click **Save as cohort (20)**
4. Read **Cohort vs everyone else**: the chip **Cohort: Top 10% (20)** sits above a side-by-side of the cohort and the rest

## Other Scenarios & analyses patterns

- [Binning](bins.md): Group orders into size bands, like under $100 or over $1,000.
- [Reference line](targets.md): Draw a target line and show how far each month is above or below it.
- [Trend line](trend-line.md): Draw the line of best fit through a chart, to show which way it is heading.
- [What-if parameter](what-if.md): Try a price change, like +10% on Software, and watch revenue change.

---

# Bookmarks

> Save the current view and come back to it with one click.

- Pattern id: `bookmarks`
- Category: Save & share
- Status: Works with app code: anfra supplies the queries, the app adds some logic
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#bookmarks
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader saves the current view as a bookmark. Later, one click restores the filters, selection, sort, grain and time zone, and the page runs again.

Why: Exploring means trying things, and a bookmark lets the reader come back to one.

## What to build

Saving a bookmark records the current filters, sort and grouping, and clicking it later puts them back and reruns the page.

Layout: A bookmark list beside the chart.

Instruction: Let the reader save the current filters, sort and grouping as a bookmark and bring that view back in one click.

Done when: After changing several filters, clicking a saved bookmark brings back exactly the view it saved.

On the ecommerce sample: Saving Japan, Q2 2026, weekly adds a bookmark. After changing the sort, clicking it brings back Japan, Q2 2026 and weekly.

## AQL

Not run as written: no query change: a bookmark only stores input.

```aql
// a bookmark never stores AQL text, only the reader's input on top of it
```

## SDK wiring

```js
function snapshot() {
  return {
    controls: Object.fromEntries(
      Object.entries(app.controls).map(([k, c]) => [
        k,
        c.appliedCondition,
      ]),
    ),
    selection: app.appliedSelection && {
      source: app.appliedSelection.source,
      rows: app.appliedSelection.rows,
    },
    sorts: Object.fromEntries(
      Object.entries(app.queries).map(([k, q]) => [k, q.sort]),
    ),
    timezone: app.timezone,
  };
}
function restore(s) {
  for (const [k, c] of Object.entries(s.controls))
    c ? app.controls[k].setCondition(c) : app.controls[k].reset();
  for (const [k, so] of Object.entries(s.sorts))
    app.queries[k].setSort(so);
  app.setTimezone(s.timezone);
  // selection rows need re-matching after the source re-runs
  return app.execute();
}
```

State it touches: Snapshot: only analytical state (applied conditions, selection, sorts, time zone). Renderer and runtime state are left out.

## Notes

- The SDK already separates the applied state (`appliedCondition`, `appliedSelection`, `sort`), so a snapshot is a small map
- Limits: Works with app code, for this session only. Data Apps run in a sandbox where `localStorage` throws, so saving across sessions needs a host (see "Saved views").

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><select id="country" aria-label="Country"><option value="">All countries</option></select><select id="range" aria-label="Dates"></select><span class="seg" id="grain"></span></div>
		<div class="row"><span class="lbl">Sort</span><span class="seg" id="sort"><button type="button" data-s="">By date</button><button type="button" data-s="desc">By revenue</button></span><label class="lbl" for="tz">Time zone</label><select id="tz"><option value="Etc/UTC">UTC</option><option value="Asia/Tokyo">Tokyo</option><option value="America/New_York">New York</option></select></div>
		<div class="cols" style="grid-template-columns: 1.45fr 1fr">
			<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue<span id="for"></span></b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="trend"></div></div>
			<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Bookmarks</b><button type="button" id="save" style="height:24px;padding:0 8px;font-size:12px">★ Save view</button></div><div id="marks" style="display:grid;gap:4px"></div></div>
		</div>
		<div class="hint">App code: a bookmark holds only applied input (conditions, sort, time zone), kept in memory for this session</div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Bookmarks', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const trend = app.createQuery('trend', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { period asc } }' });
const country = app.createFilter('country', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.country', label: 'Country' });
const range = app.createFilter('range', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'orders.ordered_at', label: 'Dates' });
const grain = app.createDateDrill('grain', { default: 'month', label: 'Grain' });
app.mapControl(country, trend, { field: 'customers.country' });
app.mapControl(range, trend, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });
app.mapControl(grain, trend, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });
const RANGES = [['', 'All dates'], ['2025-06-01|2025-12-31', 'H2 2025'], ['2026-01-01|2026-03-31', 'Q1 2026'], ['2026-04-01|2026-06-30', 'Q2 2026'], ['2026-07-01|2026-09-30', 'Q3 2026']];
const GRAINS = ['month', 'week', 'day'];
const $c = K.$('#country'), $r = K.$('#range'), $tz = K.$('#tz');
RANGES.forEach((x) => $r.add(new Option(x[1], x[0])));
country.loadOptions().then((vals) => { vals.forEach((v) => $c.add(new Option(v, v))); sync(); });
GRAINS.forEach((g) => { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.dataset.g = g; b.textContent = g[0].toUpperCase() + g.slice(1); b.onclick = () => { grain.setGrain(g); app.execute(); }; K.$('#grain').appendChild(b); });
$c.onchange = () => { if ($c.value) country.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [$c.value] }); else country.reset(); app.execute(); };
$r.onchange = () => { if ($r.value) range.setCondition({ operator: 'between', values: $r.value.split('|') }); else range.reset(); app.execute(); };
K.$('#sort').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => { b.onclick = () => { trend.setSort(b.dataset.s ? [{ field: 'total_revenue', direction: 'desc' }] : []); app.execute(); }; });
$tz.onchange = () => { app.setTimezone($tz.value); app.execute(); };

// the snapshot: applied input only, never AQL or rendered state
const cur = (c) => c.appliedCondition || c.condition;
function snapshot () {
	return { controls: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(app.controls).map(([k, c]) => [k, cur(c)])), selection: app.appliedSelection ? { source: app.appliedSelection.source, rows: app.appliedSelection.rows } : null, sorts: { trend: trend.sort.slice() }, timezone: app.timezone };
}
function restore (s) {
	for (const [k, c] of Object.entries(s.controls)) if (c && c.values && c.values.length) app.controls[k].setCondition(c); else app.controls[k].reset();
	trend.setSort(s.sorts.trend);
	app.setTimezone(s.timezone);
	return app.execute();
}
const val = (c) => c && c.values && c.values.length ? c.values : null;
const gOf = (c) => (val(c) ? String(c.values[0]).replace('datetrunc ', '') : 'month');
function describe (s) {
	const c = val(s.controls.country), r = val(s.controls.range);
	const rl = r ? (RANGES.find((x) => x[0] === r.join('|')) || [0, r.join('–')])[1] : 'all dates';
	return (c ? c[0] : 'All countries') + ' · ' + rl + ' · ' + gOf(s.controls.grain) + 'ly' + (s.sorts.trend.length ? ' · by revenue' : '') + (s.timezone !== 'Etc/UTC' ? ' · ' + s.timezone.split('/')[1].replace('_', ' ') : '');
}
const marks = [];
let active = -1, first = true;
const hhmm = () => new Date().toLocaleTimeString('en-GB', { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit', second: '2-digit' });
K.$('#save').onclick = () => { marks.push({ s: snapshot(), at: hhmm() }); active = marks.length - 1; drawMarks(); };
function drawMarks () {
	const now = JSON.stringify(snapshot());
	K.$('#marks').innerHTML = '';
	marks.forEach((m, i) => {
		const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button';
		b.style.cssText = 'height:auto;min-height:32px;padding:4px 8px;font-size:12px;line-height:16px;text-align:left;display:flex;justify-content:space-between;gap:6px';
		b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(JSON.stringify(m.s) === now));
		b.innerHTML = '<span>' + K.esc(describe(m.s)) + '</span><span style="color:var(--muted)">' + m.at + '</span>';
		b.title = JSON.stringify(m.s);
		b.onclick = () => { active = i; restore(m.s); };
		K.$('#marks').appendChild(b);
	});
}
const fmt = (v, g) => { const x = new Date(v); return g === 'month' ? x.toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', year: '2-digit', timeZone: 'UTC' }) : x.toLocaleDateString('en-US', { day: 'numeric', month: 'short', year: '2-digit', timeZone: 'UTC' }); };
function sync () {
	const s = snapshot();
	$c.value = val(s.controls.country) ? s.controls.country.values[0] : '';
	$r.value = val(s.controls.range) ? s.controls.range.values.join('|') : '';
	$tz.value = s.timezone;
	K.$('#grain').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.dataset.g === gOf(s.controls.grain))));
	K.$('#sort').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(!!b.dataset.s === !!s.sorts.trend.length)));
	return s;
}
app.subscribe(() => {
	const s = sync();
	K.status(trend, K.$('#s1'));
	K.$('#for').textContent = ' · ' + describe(s);
	if (trend.result) {
		const g = gOf(s.controls.grain);
		K.columns(K.$('#trend'), trend.result.rows, { label: (r) => fmt(r.period, g), value: (r) => r.total_revenue });
		if (first && trend.state === 'success') { first = false; marks.push({ s: snapshot(), at: hhmm() }); }
	}
	drawMarks();
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [trend], () => [(trend.sort.length ? 'sort → total_revenue desc' : 'sort → the AQL\'s own (period asc)') + ' · timezone → ' + app.timezone]);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read **Bookmarks**: the first view, **All countries · all dates · monthly**, is already saved
2. Pick **Japan** and **Q2 2026**, then click **Week**
3. Click **★ Save view**: a new bookmark **Japan · Q2 2026 · weekly** appears
4. Click **By revenue** or pick another **Time zone** to change the view
5. Click a bookmark to bring back its filters, sort, grain and time zone and run the page again

# Filter state URL

> Copy a link that opens the app with the same filters.

- Pattern id: `url-state`
- Category: Save & share
- Status: Proposed: anfra cannot do this yet (checked on 0.13.3: no write path, no query parameters, and the app frame allows scripts only, so no navigation or storage). Build the closest version and say what is missing
- Gallery card: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#url-state
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader presses **Share** and gets a link that encodes the snapshot. A colleague opens it and sees Japan, Q2 and weekly.

Why: Saying "look at this" works better with a link than with a set of instructions.

## What to build

Pressing Share turns the current view into text, and pasting that text back reopens the page with the same settings.

Layout: A URL bar that grows parameters as state changes.

Instruction: Let the reader copy the current view as text to send or keep, and paste it back to reopen the same view.

Done when: Pasting the copied text after changing filters brings back every filter and setting it held.

On the ecommerce sample: Share the view on Japan, Q2 and weekly, change the filters, then paste the text back: the page reopens on Japan, Q2 and weekly.

## AQL

Not run as written: no query change.

```aql
// same snapshot as "Bookmarks", carried by the host in the URL
```

## SDK wiring

```js
// Proposed (not real API):
// Anfra.state.write(snapshot());           host encodes into ?s=
// const s = Anfra.state.read(); if (s) restore(s);
// app.d.ts already notes: "a control set from a URL at startup is
// not an unapplied change"
```

## Notes

- Proposed: the host writes the snapshot to the URL and gives it back at startup
- Limits: Proposed. The SDK expects controls to be set at startup ("a control set from a URL at startup is not an unapplied change"), but anfra 0.8.0 has no URL API for the app.

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Set the filters to **Japan**, Q2 and **week**
2. Press **Share**: the link gains a `?s=` part that holds the snapshot
3. Send the link to a colleague: it opens on Japan, Q2 and weekly
