# Reset filters

> Clear one filter, or all of them, back to the defaults.

- Pattern id: `reset`
- Category: Save & share (also Filters)
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#reset
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

Each chip has an × that resets that filter. **Reset all** resets every control, clears the selection and restores the AQL's own sort.

Why: Readers explore more freely when getting back is one click.

## What to build

Each active filter shows as a chip with a clear button, and Reset all returns every filter, selection and sort to default.

Layout: Chips with × and a Reset all link.

Instruction: Give each active filter a clear button, plus Reset all to return every filter, selection and sort to its default.

Done when: Clearing one chip leaves the other filters in place, and Reset all shows the same view as a fresh page load.

On the ecommerce sample: With Japan, Completed and Software selected, the × on one chip clears only that filter, and Reset all returns everything to its default.

## AQL

Not run as written: no query change.

```aql
// defaults live in the declaration: createFilter(name, { default: { operator, values } })
```

Trailer frame 1 approximates the filtered numbers at half of Japan's revenue.

## SDK wiring

```js
chipX.onclick = () => {
  filter.reset();
  app.execute();
};
resetAll.onclick = () => {
  for (const c of Object.values(app.controls)) c.reset();
  app.clearSelection();
  for (const q of Object.values(app.queries)) q.setSort([]);
  app.execute();
};
```

## Notes

- `reset()` returns to the declared `default`, and `setSort([])` to the AQL's order

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><select id="country" aria-label="Country"><option value="">All countries</option></select><select id="status" aria-label="Status"><option value="">Any status</option></select><span class="lbl">Sort categories</span><span class="seg" id="sort"><button type="button" data-s="">By revenue</button><button type="button" data-s="az">A–Z</button></span></div>
		<div class="row" style="min-height:32px"><span class="chips" id="chips"></span><button type="button" id="all" style="height:28px;font-size:12px">Reset all</button></div>
		<div class="cols" style="grid-template-columns: 1fr 1.4fr">
			<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by category</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="cats"></div><div class="hint" style="margin-top:4px">Click a category to select it</div></div>
			<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Monthly revenue: <span id="kpi">–</span></b><span class="status" id="s2"></span></div><div id="trend"></div></div>
		</div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Reset filters', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const byCat = app.createQuery('byCategory', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { category_name: products.category } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const trend = app.createQuery('trend', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { period asc } }' });
const country = app.createFilter('country', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.country', label: 'Country' });
const status = app.createFilter('status', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'orders.status', label: 'Status' });
for (const q of [byCat, trend]) { app.mapControl(country, q, { field: 'customers.country' }); app.mapControl(status, q, { field: 'orders.status' }); }
app.mapCrossFilter(byCat, trend);
const $c = K.$('#country'), $s = K.$('#status');
const cap = (v) => v[0].toUpperCase() + v.slice(1);
country.loadOptions().then((vals) => vals.forEach((v) => $c.add(new Option(v, v))));
status.loadOptions().then((vals) => vals.forEach((v) => $s.add(new Option(cap(v), v))));
const setF = (f, v) => { if (v) f.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [v] }); else f.reset(); app.execute(); };
$c.onchange = () => setF(country, $c.value);
$s.onchange = () => setF(status, $s.value);
K.$('#sort').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => { b.onclick = () => { byCat.setSort(b.dataset.s ? [{ field: 'category_name', direction: 'asc' }] : []); app.execute(); }; });
// one click back to the declared defaults: controls, selection and sorts, then one execute()
K.$('#all').onclick = () => {
	for (const c of Object.values(app.controls)) c.reset();
	app.clearSelection();
	for (const q of Object.values(app.queries)) q.setSort([]);
	app.execute();
};
const one = (c) => (c.condition && c.condition.values && c.condition.values.length ? c.condition.values[0] : null);
const picked = () => (app.selection && app.selection.rows[0] ? app.selection.rows[0].category_name : null);
function chip (text, onX, kind) {
	const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', 'true');
	b.textContent = text + ' ×'; b.title = 'Reset this one'; b.onclick = onX;
	if (kind === 'sel') b.style.borderStyle = 'dashed';
	return b;
}
const mon = (v) => new Date(v).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', year: '2-digit', timeZone: 'UTC' });
app.subscribe(() => {
	const c = one(country), s = one(status), p = picked(), sorted = byCat.sort.length > 0;
	$c.value = c || ''; $s.value = s || '';
	K.$('#sort').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(!!b.dataset.s === sorted)));
	const chips = [];
	if (c) chips.push(chip(c, () => { country.reset(); app.execute(); }));
	if (s) chips.push(chip(cap(s), () => { status.reset(); app.execute(); }));
	if (p) chips.push(chip('Selected: ' + p, () => { app.clearSelection(); app.execute(); }, 'sel'));
	if (sorted) chips.push(chip('Sort: A–Z', () => { byCat.setSort([]); app.execute(); }));
	K.$('#chips').replaceChildren(...chips);
	if (!chips.length) K.$('#chips').innerHTML = '<span class="hint">Every filter, selection and sort is at its default</span>';
	K.$('#all').hidden = chips.length < 1;
	K.status(byCat, K.$('#s1')); K.status(trend, K.$('#s2'));
	if (byCat.result) K.bars(K.$('#cats'), byCat.result.rows, { label: (r) => r.category_name, value: (r) => r.total_revenue, on: (r) => r.category_name === p,
		pick: (r) => { if (p === r.category_name) app.clearSelection(); else byCat.select([r]); app.execute(); } });
	if (trend.result) {
		K.$('#kpi').textContent = K.compact.format(trend.result.rows.reduce((t, r) => t + Number(r.total_revenue), 0));
		K.columns(K.$('#trend'), trend.result.rows, { label: (r) => mon(r.period), value: (r) => r.total_revenue });
	}
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [byCat, trend], () => ['byCategory sort → ' + (sorted ? 'category_name asc (setSort)' : 'the AQL\'s own (total_revenue desc)')]);
});
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Pick **Japan** in the country menu and **Completed** in the status menu
2. Click **Software** in **Revenue by category** to select it
3. Read the chips: **Japan ×**, **Completed ×** and **Selected: Software ×**
4. Click the × on one chip to reset just that filter
5. Click **Reset all**: every filter, the selection and the sort go back to their defaults

# Undo / redo

> Step back and forward through your filter and drill changes.

- Pattern id: `undo-redo`
- Category: Save & share
- Status: Works with app code: anfra supplies the queries, the app adds some logic
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#undo-redo
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

Every applied change pushes a snapshot. **Undo** restores the previous one, and **Redo** goes forward again.

Why: Without undo, readers stay cautious. With it, they try more.

## What to build

Each change to a filter or selection is kept as a step, and Undo goes back one step while Redo goes forward.

Layout: A history strip under the chips.

Instruction: Let the reader undo and redo their changes to filters and selections, one step at a time.

Done when: Undo removes only the last change, and Redo brings it back, ending on the same view as before.

On the ecommerce sample: After picking Japan, Week and Software, Undo leaves weekly Japan with no selection, and Redo brings the Software selection back.

## AQL

Not run as written: no query change.

```aql
// undo replays input, never AQL
```

## SDK wiring

```js
const past = [],
  future = [];
app.subscribe(() => {
  /* after a successful execute with changes */
});
async function commit() {
  past.push(snapshot());
  future.length = 0;
  await app.execute();
}
async function undo() {
  if (past.length < 2) return;
  future.push(past.pop());
  await restore(past.at(-1));
}
async function redo() {
  const s = future.pop();
  if (s) {
    past.push(s);
    await restore(s);
  }
}
```

## Notes

- A snapshot is small and holds only input, so undo is cheap. Results may come from the cache
- Limits: Works with app code, using the snapshot and restore functions from "Bookmarks".

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app">
		<div class="row"><select id="country" aria-label="Country"><option value="">All countries</option></select><span class="seg" id="grain"><button type="button" data-g="month">Month</button><button type="button" data-g="week">Week</button></span><span style="flex:1"></span><button type="button" id="undo" title="Ctrl+Z">↶ Undo</button><button type="button" id="redo" title="Ctrl+Shift+Z">↷ Redo</button></div>
		<div class="cols" style="grid-template-columns: 1fr 1.4fr">
			<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue by category</b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="cats"></div><div class="hint" style="margin-top:4px">Click a category to select it</div></div>
			<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Revenue<span id="for"></span></b><span class="status" id="s2"></span></div><div id="trend"></div></div>
		</div>
		<div class="panel" style="padding:6px 10px"><div class="ph" style="margin-bottom:4px"><b>History</b><span>Click a step to jump to it</span></div><div class="chips" id="hist"></div></div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Undo / redo', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const byCat = app.createQuery('byCategory', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { category_name: products.category } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { total_revenue desc } }' });
const trend = app.createQuery('trend', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { period asc } }' });
const country = app.createFilter('country', { dataset: 'ecommerce', field: 'customers.country', label: 'Country' });
const grain = app.createDateDrill('grain', { default: 'month', label: 'Grain' });
app.mapControl(country, byCat, { field: 'customers.country' });
app.mapControl(country, trend, { field: 'customers.country' });
app.mapControl(grain, trend, { field: 'orders.ordered_at' });
app.mapCrossFilter(byCat, trend);
const $c = K.$('#country');
country.loadOptions().then((vals) => { vals.forEach((v) => $c.add(new Option(v, v))); sync(); });

// a snapshot is the reader's input only: each control's condition, the selection, the time zone
function snapshot (label) {
	return { label, controls: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(app.controls).map(([k, c]) => [k, c.condition])), selection: app.selection ? { source: app.selection.source, rows: app.selection.rows.slice() } : null, timezone: app.timezone };
}
function restore (s) {
	for (const [k, c] of Object.entries(s.controls)) if (c && c.values && c.values.length) app.controls[k].setCondition(c); else app.controls[k].reset();
	if (s.selection) app.queries[s.selection.source].select(s.selection.rows); else app.clearSelection();
	app.setTimezone(s.timezone);
	return app.execute();
}
const hist = [], pos = { i: -1 };
function commit (label) { hist.splice(pos.i + 1); hist.push(snapshot(label)); pos.i = hist.length - 1; app.execute(); draw(); }
function go (i) { if (i < 0 || i >= hist.length || i === pos.i) return; pos.i = i; restore(hist[i]); draw(); }
K.$('#undo').onclick = () => go(pos.i - 1);
K.$('#redo').onclick = () => go(pos.i + 1);
document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => { if ((e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey) && e.key.toLowerCase() === 'z') { e.preventDefault(); go(e.shiftKey ? pos.i + 1 : pos.i - 1); } });
$c.onchange = () => { if ($c.value) country.setCondition({ operator: 'is', values: [$c.value] }); else country.reset(); commit('Country = ' + ($c.value || 'All')); };
K.$('#grain').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => { b.onclick = () => { grain.setGrain(b.dataset.g); commit('Grain = ' + b.dataset.g); }; });
const picked = () => (app.selection && app.selection.rows[0] ? app.selection.rows[0].category_name : null);
const gOf = () => { const c = grain.condition; return c && c.values && c.values.length ? String(c.values[0]).replace('datetrunc ', '') : 'month'; };
function sync () {
	const c = country.condition;
	$c.value = c && c.values && c.values.length ? c.values[0] : '';
	K.$('#grain').querySelectorAll('button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.dataset.g === gOf())));
	K.$('#undo').disabled = pos.i <= 0; K.$('#redo').disabled = pos.i >= hist.length - 1;
	K.$('#undo').style.opacity = pos.i <= 0 ? 0.4 : 1; K.$('#redo').style.opacity = pos.i >= hist.length - 1 ? 0.4 : 1;
}
const fmt = (v) => { const x = new Date(v); return gOf() === 'month' ? x.toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', year: '2-digit', timeZone: 'UTC' }) : x.toLocaleDateString('en-US', { day: 'numeric', month: 'short', year: '2-digit', timeZone: 'UTC' }); };
function draw () {
	sync();
	K.status(byCat, K.$('#s1')); K.status(trend, K.$('#s2'));
	const p = picked(), c = country.condition;
	K.$('#for').textContent = ' · ' + (c && c.values && c.values.length ? c.values[0] : 'all countries') + (p ? ' · ' + p : '') + ' · by ' + gOf();
	if (byCat.result) K.bars(K.$('#cats'), byCat.result.rows, { label: (r) => r.category_name, value: (r) => r.total_revenue, on: (r) => r.category_name === p,
		pick: (r) => { if (p === r.category_name) { app.clearSelection(); commit('Selection cleared'); } else { byCat.select([r]); commit('Selected: ' + r.category_name); } } });
	if (trend.result) K.columns(K.$('#trend'), trend.result.rows, { label: (r) => fmt(r.period), value: (r) => r.total_revenue });
	const h = K.$('#hist'); h.innerHTML = '';
	hist.forEach((s, i) => { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = i + ' · ' + s.label; b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(i === pos.i)); if (i > pos.i) b.style.opacity = 0.5; b.onclick = () => go(i); h.appendChild(b); });
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [trend], () => ['history → step ' + pos.i + ' of ' + (hist.length - 1) + (hist.length - 1 > pos.i ? ' (' + (hist.length - 1 - pos.i) + ' to redo)' : '') + '; undo replays input, never AQL']);
}
app.subscribe(draw);
hist.push(snapshot('Start')); pos.i = 0;
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Pick **Japan** in the country menu, click **Week**, then click **Software** in **Revenue by category**
2. Read **History**: **1 · Country = Japan**, **2 · Grain = week**, **3 · Selected: Software**
3. Click **↶ Undo** or press `Ctrl+Z`: the page goes back to step 2, weekly Japan with no selection
4. Click **↷ Redo** or press `Ctrl+Shift+Z` to bring the Software selection back

# Saved views

> Keep named views that are still there next week, on any device.

- Pattern id: `saved-views`
- Category: Save & share
- Status: Proposed: anfra cannot do this yet (checked on 0.13.3: no write path, no query parameters, and the app frame allows scripts only, so no navigation or storage). Build the closest version and say what is missing
- Gallery card: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#saved-views
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

The reader saves a view. Next week, on another device, it's in their list. Today a bookmark is lost when the frame reloads.

Why: A Data App people return to needs to remember their views.

## What to build

Saving a view stores its filters under a name, and picking that name from the list later brings the view back.

Layout: A saved-views menu.

Instruction: Let the reader save views under a name and reopen them from a list, for now only during the current visit.

Done when: A named view appears in the list and, clicked later in the same visit, brings back the settings it saved.

On the ecommerce sample: A view saved as Monday: APAC weekly appears under Views, and clicking it later in the same visit brings back its filters.

## AQL

Not run as written: no query change.

```aql
// persisted snapshot = same shape as a bookmark
```

## SDK wiring

```js
// Proposed (not real API):
// await Anfra.views.save('Monday: APAC weekly', snapshot());
// const views = await Anfra.views.list();
```

## Notes

- Proposed: host-side storage of snapshots, keyed by reader and app
- Limits: Proposed. API.md: "The origin is opaque: keep state in variables, since localStorage, sessionStorage and cookies throw."

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Save the current view under a name, such as **Monday: APAC weekly**
2. Open the app next week on another device
3. Click **Views**: the saved view is still in your list, next to **Finance: FY27 Q1**
4. Click the view to bring it back

## Other Save & share patterns

- [Bookmarks](bookmarks.md): Save the current view and come back to it with one click.
- [Filter state URL](url-state.md): Copy a link that opens the app with the same filters.
- [Reset filters](reset.md): Clear one filter, or all of them, back to the defaults.
- [Undo / redo](undo-redo.md): Step back and forward through your filter and drill changes.
- [Refresh & cache](refresh.md): Rerun the queries and see how fresh the data is.

---

# Refresh & cache

> Rerun the queries and see how fresh the data is.

- Pattern id: `refresh`
- Category: Save & share (also Dates & time)
- Status: Works today: anfra does it natively
- Gallery card with a live demo: https://anfra.ai/interaction-patterns/interaction-gallery.html#refresh
- Built on: @holistics/anfra-sdk 0.8.0, the `ecommerce` sample Dataset. Swap in your own fields.

## What the reader does

A freshness line shows the newest data, when the query ran and whether it came from cache. **Refresh** skips the cache.

Why: Readers trust a number more when they can see how old it is.

## What to build

A line shows how new the data is and when it loaded, and Refresh skips the cache and fetches everything again.

Layout: A freshness bar with a refresh button.

Instruction: Show how new the data is and when it was loaded, with a Refresh button that fetches it again.

Done when: Pressing Refresh updates the load time, and the freshness line says whether the data came from cache.

On the ecommerce sample: The top line shows the newest order date and when the query ran. Run again re-runs nothing, while Refresh re-runs and updates the time.

## AQL

Ran on anfra 0.8.0 against `ecommerce`. The AQL stays fixed; the reader's choices arrive as the input below, which the SDK builds from controls and selections.

```aql
explore { measures { latest: orders | max(orders.ordered_at), earliest: orders | min(orders.ordered_at) } }
```

Saved result:

| latest | earliest |
|---|---|
| 2026-09-23 | 2025-06-01 |

## SDK wiring

```js
// re-runs everything, skips result cache
refreshBtn.onclick = () => app.refresh();
app.subscribe(() => {
  const d = trend.result?.debug;
  const cache = d?.fromCache ? ' · cache' : '';
  fresh.textContent = `ran ${ago(d?.executedAt)}${cache}`;
});
// live data only
setInterval(() => app.refresh(), 5 * 60_000);
```

State it touches: Runtime: `executedAt` and `fromCache`. Never saved in a snapshot.

## Notes

- `refresh()` and `result.debug` give the run's age and cache status

## Complete working example

The live demo's source: a small Data App the gallery mounts with `mountDataApp`. `Anfra` is the SDK global. `K` is the gallery's drawing kit (`K.bars`, `K.columns`, `K.table`, `K.status`, `K.sent`, formatters): replace it with your own rendering. The SDK calls are the part to copy.

HTML body:

```html
<div class="app"><style>.colz { height: 110px; }</style>
		<div class="row" style="justify-content:space-between"><span id="fresh" class="lbl" style="font-size:14px;color:var(--ink)">–</span><span class="row"><button type="button" id="again" title="app.execute(): runs only queries whose input changed">Run again</button><button type="button" id="refresh" title="app.refresh(): re-runs everything and skips the result cache">⟳ Refresh</button></span></div>
		<div class="panel"><div class="ph"><b>Monthly revenue: <span id="kpi">–</span></b><span class="status" id="s1"></span></div><div id="trend"></div></div>
		<div class="panel" style="padding:6px 10px"><div class="ph" style="margin-bottom:4px"><b>Runs</b><span>Newest first</span></div><div id="log"></div></div>
		<div class="hint">This host's core API backend reports fromCache false on every run, so "cache" never shows here</div>
		<div class="sent" id="sent"></div></div>
```

Script:

```js
const app = Anfra.createApp({ title: 'Refresh & cache', timezone: 'Etc/UTC' });
const trend = app.createQuery('trend', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { dimensions { period: orders.ordered_at | month() } measures { total_revenue: revenue } sorts { period asc } }' });
const anchor = app.createQuery('anchor', { dataset: 'ecommerce', aql: 'explore { measures { latest: orders | max(orders.ordered_at), earliest: orders | min(orders.ordered_at) } }' });
const runs = [];
const t = (d) => d ? new Date(d).toLocaleTimeString('en-GB', { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit', second: '2-digit' }) : '–';
async function run (kind) {
	const before = trend.result && trend.result.debug ? String(trend.result.debug.executedAt) : null, t0 = performance.now();
	const entry = { kind, at: new Date(), ms: null, ran: null };
	runs.unshift(entry); draw();
	const sum = kind === 'Refresh' ? await app.refresh() : await app.execute();
	entry.ms = Math.round(performance.now() - t0);
	entry.ran = sum.succeeded.length + sum.failed.length;
	entry.same = trend.result && trend.result.debug && String(trend.result.debug.executedAt) === before;
	entry.cache = !!(trend.result && trend.result.debug && trend.result.debug.fromCache);
	draw();
}
K.$('#again').onclick = () => run('Run again');
K.$('#refresh').onclick = () => run('Refresh');
const mon = (v) => new Date(v).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', year: '2-digit', timeZone: 'UTC' });
const day = (v) => new Date(v).toLocaleDateString('en-GB', { day: 'numeric', month: 'short', year: 'numeric', timeZone: 'UTC' });
function draw () {
	K.status(trend, K.$('#s1'));
	const d = trend.result && trend.result.debug;
	const latest = anchor.result && anchor.result.rows[0] ? day(anchor.result.rows[0].latest) : '…';
	K.$('#fresh').innerHTML = 'Data as of <b>' + latest + '</b> · ran ' + t(d && d.executedAt) + ' · ' + (trend.state === 'executing' ? 'running…' : d ? (d.fromCache ? 'from cache' : '<span style="color:var(--violet-ink)">fresh</span>') : '…');
	if (trend.result) {
		K.$('#kpi').textContent = K.compact.format(trend.result.rows.reduce((s, r) => s + Number(r.total_revenue), 0));
		K.columns(K.$('#trend'), trend.result.rows, { label: (r) => mon(r.period), value: (r) => r.total_revenue });
	}
	K.$('#log').innerHTML = runs.slice(0, 3).map((r) => '<div style="display:flex;justify-content:space-between;font-size:12px;line-height:20px"><span><b style="font-weight:500">' + r.kind + '</b> at ' + t(r.at) + '</span><span style="color:var(--muted)">'
		+ (r.ran == null ? 'running…' : r.ran === 0 ? 'nothing re-ran: the input did not change, results kept' : r.ran + ' queries re-ran' + (r.kind === 'Refresh' ? ' with bustCache' : '') + ' · ' + r.ms + ' ms · ' + (r.cache ? 'cache' : 'fresh')) + '</span></div>').join('') || '<div class="hint">Press Run again or Refresh</div>';
	K.sent(K.$('#sent'), app, [trend, anchor], () => [(runs[0] ? 'last call → ' + (runs[0].kind === 'Refresh' ? 'app.refresh() (bustCache: true)' : 'app.execute() (changed input only)') : 'first load → app.execute()') + ' · debug.fromCache ' + String(!!(d && d.fromCache))]);
}
app.subscribe(draw);
app.execute();
```

## Walkthrough on the gallery card

1. Read the line at the top: **Data as of** the newest order date, when the query ran, and **fresh**
2. Click **Run again**: under **Runs**, nothing re-runs because the input did not change
3. Click **⟳ Refresh**: every query re-runs past the cache, and the run time updates
